````rust
//! §11 maximal-match admission over selector domains, without loop expansion.
use super::*;

type Domain = Vec<(u128, u128)>;

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum InvocationSteps {
    Root(u128),
    // None is deferred, never an empty domain or an "any budget" proof.
    // ISA 0.8 has no object-level constant token; Some is populated at binding.
    Nested(Option<u128>),
    Action,
}
impl InvocationSteps {
    fn upper(self) -> Option<u128> {
        match self {
            Self::Root(budget) => Some(budget),
            Self::Nested(budget) => budget,
            Self::Action => Some(u128::MAX),
        }
    }
}

fn intersection(a: &Domain, b: &Domain) -> Option<Domain> {
    let out: Domain = a
        .iter()
        .zip(b)
        .map(|(x, y)| (x.0.max(y.0), x.1.min(y.1)))
        .collect();
    out.iter().all(|(lo, hi)| lo <= hi).then_some(out)
}

/// Partition A \ B into disjoint boxes. Boundaries come only from selectors;
/// cost is independent of numeric loop/step bounds. Repeating subtraction
/// checks coverage by the UNION of all higher entries, not one overlapping C.
fn subtract(mut a: Domain, b: &Domain) -> Vec<Domain> {
    let Some(common) = intersection(&a, b) else {
        return vec![a];
    };
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for (i, &(lo, hi)) in common.iter().enumerate() {
        if a[i].0 < lo {
            let mut part = a.clone();
            part[i].1 = lo - 1;
            out.push(part);
            a[i].0 = lo;
        }
        if hi < a[i].1 {
            let mut part = a.clone();
            part[i].0 = hi + 1;
            out.push(part);
            a[i].1 = hi;
        }
    }
    out
}

impl Object {
    /// Each point has its own generated operations (§11), including call/loop
    /// rows. Start at the shortest chains; a new oracle invocation can broaden
    /// their step domain, so has_uncovered_tie also visits those extensions.
    /// The empty prefix is split over every root instruction (not a fictitious
    /// operation with an empty chain). validate_path already checked call edges.
    fn shortest_chains(&self, path: &Json, region: &str) -> Result<Vec<Vec<Json>>> {
        if !path.array()?.is_empty() {
            return Ok(vec![path.array()?.to_vec()]);
        }
        fn points(seq: &[Instruction], ordinal: &mut u128, out: &mut Vec<u128>) {
            for i in seq {
                out.push(*ordinal);
                *ordinal += 1;
                for body in &i.bodies {
                    points(body, ordinal, out);
                }
            }
        }
        let symbol = &self.identity()?.interface_hashes[region];
        let mut chains = Vec::new();
        for block in &self.functions[region].blocks {
            let mut ordinals = Vec::new();
            points(&block.instructions, &mut 0, &mut ordinals);
            for ordinal in ordinals {
                chains.push(vec![Json::Object(std::collections::BTreeMap::from([
                    ("symbol".into(), Json::String(symbol.clone())),
                    (
                        "point".into(),
                        Json::String(format!("{}:{ordinal}", block.name)),
                    ),
                    ("iteration".into(), Json::String("*".into())),
                ]))]);
            }
        }
        Ok(chains)
    }

    fn chain_domain(
        &self,
        chain: &[Json],
        root_budget: Option<u128>,
        arguments: Option<&std::collections::BTreeMap<String, crate::Argument>>,
    ) -> Result<Option<(Domain, InvocationSteps, String)>> {
        let mut domain = Vec::new();
        // The step owner persists through lift.call and lifted action gates.
        // Only an oracle call opens a new token-governed invocation (§11).
        let mut steps = root_budget.map_or(InvocationSteps::Action, InvocationSteps::Root);
        let mut arguments = arguments.cloned();
        if root_budget == Some(0) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        for (index, element) in chain.iter().enumerate() {
            let (block, ordinal) = element
                .get("point")?
                .string()?
                .rsplit_once(':')
                .ok_or_else(|| Error("§11: invalid point".into()))?;
            let point = self.point(
                element.get("symbol")?.string()?,
                block,
                ordinal
                    .parse()
                    .map_err(|_| Error("§11: invalid point ordinal".into()))?,
            )?;
            if index + 1 < chain.len() {
                // lift.call stays in the same oracle/argument environment.
                let call = if matches!(
                    point.instruction.op.as_str(),
                    "lift.oracle_call" | "lift.oracle_uncall" | "lift.perm_call"
                ) {
                    Some(point.instruction.clone())
                } else {
                    normalize_call(point.instruction)
                        .ok()
                        .map(|c| c.instruction)
                };
                if let Some(call) = call {
                    let oracle = matches!(
                        call.op.as_str(),
                        "lift.oracle_call" | "lift.oracle_uncall" | "oracle_call"
                    );
                    if oracle {
                        steps = InvocationSteps::Nested(arguments.as_ref().and_then(|a| {
                            match a.get(&call.operands[1]) {
                                Some(crate::Argument::Token(budget)) => {
                                    Some(u128::from(budget.steps))
                                }
                                _ => None,
                            }
                        }));
                    }
                    if steps.upper() == Some(0) {
                        return Ok(None);
                    }
                    if let Some(old) = arguments.take() {
                        let callee = &self.functions[call.operands[0].trim_start_matches('@')];
                        let group = if oracle { 4 } else { 3 };
                        let operands =
                            crate::object::list(&call.operands[if oracle { 6 } else { 4 }])?;
                        arguments = Some(
                            callee.params[group]
                                .iter()
                                .zip(operands)
                                .map(|(p, n)| {
                                    old.get(&n)
                                        .cloned()
                                        .map(|v| (p.name.clone(), v))
                                        .ok_or_else(|| {
                                            Error(format!("§11: unresolved classical argument {n}"))
                                        })
                                })
                                .collect::<Result<_>>()?,
                        );
                    }
                }
            }
            for bound in point.loops {
                if bound == 0 {
                    return Ok(None);
                }
                domain.push((0, u128::from(bound) - 1));
            }
        }
        // Generated ordinals belong to the bound expansion library. Admission
        // does not execute it; retain the whole ordinal selector domain.
        // Unknown is DEFERRED under INV-5 1.4.3, not a proof of emptiness.
        // A future object-derived token bound can use the same Some branch.
        let Some(upper) = steps.upper() else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if upper == 0 {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        domain.extend([(1, upper), (0, 1), (0, u128::MAX)]);
        Ok(Some((domain, steps, format!("{arguments:?}"))))
    }

    fn entry_domain(&self, entry: &Json, chain: &[Json], base: &Domain) -> Result<Option<Domain>> {
        let path = entry.get("path")?.array()?;
        if path.len() > chain.len() {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let mut domain = base.clone();
        let mut offset = 0;
        for (i, element) in chain.iter().enumerate() {
            let (block, ordinal) = element
                .get("point")?
                .string()?
                .rsplit_once(':')
                .ok_or_else(|| Error("§11: invalid point".into()))?;
            let depth = self
                .point(
                    element.get("symbol")?.string()?,
                    block,
                    ordinal
                        .parse()
                        .map_err(|_| Error("§11: invalid point ordinal".into()))?,
                )?
                .loops
                .len();
            if let Some(selector) = path.get(i) {
                if selector.get("symbol")? != element.get("symbol")?
                    || selector.get("point")? != element.get("point")?
                {
                    return Ok(None);
                }
                let iterations = selector.get("iteration")?;
                if !wildcard(iterations) {
                    for (j, value) in iterations.array()?.iter().enumerate() {
                        let value = value.uint()?;
                        domain[offset + j] = (value, value);
                    }
                }
            }
            offset += depth;
        }
        for (i, key) in ["step", "phase", "generated"].iter().enumerate() {
            let value = entry.get(key)?;
            if !wildcard(value) {
                let n = if *key == "phase" {
                    u128::from(value.string()? == "rev")
                } else {
                    value.uint()?
                };
                domain[offset + i] = (n, n);
            }
        }
        Ok(intersection(&domain, base))
    }

    pub(super) fn has_uncovered_tie(
        &self,
        a: &Json,
        b: &Json,
        entries: &[Json],
        region: &str,
        root_budget: Option<u128>,
    ) -> Result<bool> {
        Ok(self
            .tie_witness(a, b, entries, region, root_budget, None)?
            .is_some())
    }

    fn tie_witness(
        &self,
        a: &Json,
        b: &Json,
        entries: &[Json],
        region: &str,
        root_budget: Option<u128>,
        arguments: Option<&std::collections::BTreeMap<String, crate::Argument>>,
    ) -> Result<Option<Json>> {
        let mut chains = self.shortest_chains(a.get("path")?, region)?;
        let max_path = entries
            .iter()
            .map(|e| e.get("path")?.array().map(<[Json]>::len))
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?
            .into_iter()
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(0);
        // Beyond every selector's path, only the reachable call graph matters.
        // Memoizing suffix points per boundary chain terminates recursive
        // lprocs without a call-depth, step, or loop expansion cap.
        let mut suffixes = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
        while let Some(chain) = chains.pop() {
            let Some((base, steps, bound_arguments)) =
                self.chain_domain(&chain, root_budget, arguments)?
            else {
                continue;
            };
            if !matches!(steps, InvocationSteps::Action) {
                let last = chain
                    .last()
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error("§11: empty operation chain".into()))?;
                let (block, ordinal) = last
                    .get("point")?
                    .string()?
                    .rsplit_once(':')
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error("§11: invalid point".into()))?;
                let point = self.point(
                    last.get("symbol")?.string()?,
                    block,
                    ordinal
                        .parse()
                        .map_err(|_| Error("§11: invalid point ordinal".into()))?,
                )?;
                let callee = if matches!(
                    point.instruction.op.as_str(),
                    "lift.call" | "lift.oracle_call" | "lift.oracle_uncall" | "lift.perm_call"
                ) {
                    Some(
                        point.instruction.operands[0]
                            .trim_start_matches('@')
                            .to_string(),
                    )
                } else {
                    normalize_call(point.instruction).ok().map(|call| {
                        call.instruction.operands[0]
                            .trim_start_matches('@')
                            .to_string()
                    })
                };
                let boundary = chain[..chain.len().min(max_path)].to_vec();
                let key = (
                    Json::Array(boundary).canonical(),
                    last.canonical(),
                    steps.upper(),
                    bound_arguments,
                );
                if chain.len() < max_path || suffixes.insert(key) {
                    if let Some(callee) = callee.filter(|name| self.functions.contains_key(name)) {
                        for suffix in self.shortest_chains(&Json::Array(vec![]), &callee)? {
                            let mut extension = chain.clone();
                            extension.extend(suffix);
                            chains.push(extension);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            let Some(ad) = self.entry_domain(a, &chain, &base)? else {
                continue;
            };
            let Some(bd) = self.entry_domain(b, &chain, &base)? else {
                continue;
            };
            let Some(common) = intersection(&ad, &bd) else {
                continue;
            };
            let mut remaining = vec![common];
            for higher in entries {
                if higher.get("kind")? != a.get("kind")? || specificity(higher)? <= specificity(a)?
                {
                    continue;
                }
                if let Some(cover) = self.entry_domain(higher, &chain, &base)? {
                    remaining = remaining
                        .into_iter()
                        .flat_map(|box_| subtract(box_, &cover))
                        .collect();
                    if remaining.is_empty() {
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
            if let Some(uncovered) = remaining.first() {
                return Ok(Some(self.concrete_witness(&chain, uncovered)?));
            }
        }
        Ok(None)
    }

    fn concrete_witness(&self, chain: &[Json], domain: &Domain) -> Result<Json> {
        let mut path = chain.to_vec();
        let mut offset = 0;
        for element in &mut path {
            let (block, ordinal) = element
                .get("point")?
                .string()?
                .rsplit_once(':')
                .ok_or_else(|| Error("§11: invalid point".into()))?;
            let depth = self
                .point(
                    element.get("symbol")?.string()?,
                    block,
                    ordinal
                        .parse()
                        .map_err(|_| Error("§11: invalid ordinal".into()))?,
                )?
                .loops
                .len();
            let iterations = domain[offset..offset + depth]
                .iter()
                .map(|d| Json::Number(d.0.to_string()))
                .collect();
            if let Json::Object(fields) = element {
                fields.insert("iteration".into(), Json::Array(iterations));
            }
            offset += depth;
        }
        Ok(Json::Object(std::collections::BTreeMap::from([
            ("path".into(), Json::Array(path)),
            ("step".into(), Json::Number(domain[offset].0.to_string())),
            (
                "phase".into(),
                Json::String(
                    if domain[offset + 1].0 == 0 {
                        "fwd"
                    } else {
                        "rev"
                    }
                    .into(),
                ),
            ),
            (
                "generated".into(),
                Json::Number(domain[offset + 2].0.to_string()),
            ),
        ])))
    }

    /// Check matching with the actual run's tokens, before any realisation.
    /// This is the §11 matching gate, not staged target/timing execution.
    /// Unbound admission defers nested domains (SPEC-QUESTIONS 33 / INV-5 1.4.3).
    pub fn check_schedule_matches_for_run(
        &self,
        region: &str,
        budget: crate::Budget,
        args: &[crate::Argument],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let Some(schedule) = self.section("schedule") else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        if schedule
            .get("bindings")?
            .get("region")?
            .string()?
            .trim_start_matches('@')
            != region
        {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let function = &self.functions[region];
        let parameters = &function.params[if function.kind == "oracle" { 4 } else { 3 }];
        if parameters.len() != args.len() {
            return err("§11", "schedule argument count mismatch");
        }
        let arguments = parameters
            .iter()
            .zip(args)
            .map(|(p, v)| {
                crate::oracle::check_argument(self, &p.ty, v)?;
                Ok((p.name.clone(), v.clone()))
            })
            .collect::<Result<std::collections::BTreeMap<_, _>>>()?;
        let entries = schedule.get("entries")?.array()?;
        let root_budget = (function.kind == "oracle").then_some(u128::from(budget.steps));
        for (i, a) in entries.iter().enumerate() {
            for b in &entries[i + 1..] {
                if a.get("kind")? == b.get("kind")?
                    && specificity(a)? == specificity(b)?
                    && overlaps(a, b)?
                {
                    if let Some(operation) =
                        self.tie_witness(a, b, entries, region, root_budget, Some(&arguments))?
                    {
                        // Never choose or apply a realisation on an ambiguous
                        // concrete operation. The resolver owns the diagnostic.
                        self.resolve_schedule(&operation, a.get("kind")?.string()?)?;
                        return err(
                            "§11",
                            "internal maximal-tie witness did not resolve to a tie",
                        );
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
````

````markdown
Round 1 graded snapshot `3dea965`. The codex job continued to `0164b5a`
before the handover, so some witnesses were already fixed when this round's
work began; the tables below say so, with the test that now pins each one.
Work since `0164b5a` is in the `reference-interpreter:` commits from `c3d8bfd`
onward. Every witness is a test in `tests/r1_*.rs`. The file `RED` column
reports that test run against `0164b5a` (it compiled against that tree unless
it says "API absent"): FAIL means it was red before the fix.

`cargo test --offline` (152 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored);

**declined** (the spec sentence that decides it, with a test pinning the
behaviour); **partial** (what remains and why).

## Widths: fable R1-B1, codex B01, muse B1 — resolved

The council's 129- and 256-bit witnesses already ran at `0164b5a` (the codex
job had added vector engines beside the u128 ones). Four narrowings remained
and were red at `0164b5a`: bundle widths were `u16` (wire[70000] rejected),
lifted suffixes were capped at 128 (`lift.const.i300`), layout exponents
H/A_tab/S_cells were capped at 127, and the machine's counters, cells and
slots were u128 rather than §3.7 derived widths. Worse, keeping two engine
pairs had let them diverge: the vector engine computed `ashr` by N or more as
a sign fill while §4.1 says "shift ≥ N → 0", and `tests/bitvectors.rs`
asserted the wrong value.

Changes:
- `src/object.rs` `Type`: `Wire(u64)`, `Reg(u64)`, `Region(u64, u64)`; only
  `iN` keeps 1..=128. `host_count` parses every width exactly; a width beyond
  64 bits is reported as a host limit, not an ISA rule.
- One engine pair. The u128 sequential engine and u128 machine are deleted;
  `src/oracle.rs` `run_oracle_vectors` is the §14.1 interpreter and
  `src/machine.rs` `OracleVectorMachine` the §3.6 machine. `run_oracle`,
  `OracleInput`, `OracleOutcome` and `OracleMachine` are checked adapters that
  fail loudly when a value does not fit u128.
- `src/machine.rs` `DerivedWidths`: Hc = H + 2, Ac = A_tab + 1, Sc = S_cells + 1,
  Dc = max(1, ⌈log₂(depth_limit + 2)⌉), P, Did, W_max, W_cell and per-slot
  widths; counters, stack cells and slots are bit-vectors of those widths,
  exchanged in their low bits with the high bits asserted clean (§3.7 "the
  cell's remaining bits stay clean").
- Layout ranges are exact up to 2^128 (`validate_ranges`); `inrange` is
  computed without wrap (`Memory::valid`).
- `src/bits.rs` `binary`: `ashr` by ≥ N is 0; `division_fault`, `compare`.
- `src/quantum.rs` and `src/action.rs`: the oracle-from-action adapter always
  uses the bit-vector machine (the former 128-bit `read_bits` is gone).

Tests (`tests/r1_widths.rs`): `codex_b01_wire129_identity_at_b0_and_b1`,
`codex_b01_reg129_move_with_bit_128_set_reverses`,
`fable_r1_b1_wide_add_is_2x_mod_2_256_in_both_engines` (x ∈ {0, 1, 2^200,
2^256−1} × B ∈ 0..=3, both engines plus full prefix reversal),
`fable_r1_b1_unused_wide_input_through_the_small_integer_api`,
`muse_b1_mov_of_2_255`, `wide_lifted_suffixes_constants_and_casts`,
`bundle_widths_above_u16_and_large_region_dimensions_are_well_formed`,
`ashr_by_n_or_more_is_zero_in_every_engine`,
`derived_counter_widths_follow_section_3_7` (H = 127 → Hc = 129; H = 128 → 130).
RED at 0164b5a: 4 of 9 FAIL (suffixes, u16 widths, ashr divergence, derived
widths: API absent).

SPEC-QUESTIONS: 4 (revised: the round-0 entry claimed derived widths the
code did not have), 14 (ptr_width ≤ 128 from §4.8's `iN (rlen, width
ptr_width)`), 15 (lifted suffixes name reg widths).

## §6 discipline: fable R1-B3, codex B03, B04, B05, muse B5 — resolved

At `0164b5a` the codex job had already fixed the round-1 witnesses except one:
codex B03(b), `h t; h t; d = qcopy t; quncopy t d`, was rejected because the
closed-window set was permanent. A window now opens at its computation:
`Discipline::closed` counts window-closing events per wire and each `Creation`
snapshots the counts of its dependencies (`window_closed`).

The council asked for a sound checker, so I added a differential test that
does not depend on anyone's reading: `tests/r1_fuzz_discipline.rs` generates
random actions (compute, middle and possibly mutated uncompute sequences, qif,
qloop, nested predicates, local regions, qload/qstore) and requires every
statically accepted one to run exactly clean on all basis inputs and on a
superposed input, forward and adjoint, using the exact simulator (B15). It
found four unsound accepts, all also accepted at `0164b5a`:

1. `h d0; ccx d0 p d1; cx d1 t; ccx d0 p d1; h d0` released d0 entangled with
   t: recorded reads were not transitive. `note_reads` now records the
   transitive dependency set.
2. The same through a predicate: `change` rebuilt each operation key by
   splitting its version at `":context"`, which also occurs inside nested
   snapshots, so the key was wrong and the recorded reads silently fell back to
   direct reads. The key is now taken before formatting.
3. A diagonal phase on a perm value that depends on an `other` value kicks back
   onto it (`h d0; cx d0 d1; cz d1 t; cx d0 d1; h d0`): outstanding diagonal
   phases are now tracked (`Discipline::phases`) and block the adjoint of the
   `other` values they depend on.
4. Gate operation identities used predicate names, not versions, for `other`
   targets (the fable R1-B3 class): versions now include every control and
   effective-control wire's version.

The ignored 200,000-program sweep then accepts 82,797 programs and every one
runs clean (`PROGRESS.md`).

Tests (`tests/r1_discipline.rs`): `fable_r1_b3_predicate_flip_closes_the_window`
(both witnesses and both positive controls),
`codex_b03_predicate_versions_and_windows_start_at_the_computation`,
`codex_b04_qif_arms_are_complementary_and_loops_compose`,
`codex_b05_quantum_memory_cleanup_and_restoration`,
`codex_b05_child_call_advances_loaded_cells`,
`muse_b5_loop_bodies_are_validated_per_iteration`,
`fuzz_witnesses_of_entangling_reads_are_rejected`; each accepted positive is
also executed. RED: codex B03(b) and the fuzz witnesses FAIL; the others pass
(fixed by the codex job after `3dea965`).

SPEC-QUESTIONS 25: the literal §6.2 sentence "other values are released only by
the adjoint of the sequence that produced them" admits witness 1; the crate
implements the stronger reading T5 needs, with a proposed 0.9 wording.

## codex B07 — qinplace — resolved

At load (`validation.rs`, `qinplace` arm) @g and @ginv must be oracles mapping
one wire[n] input to a wire[n] target with no mem and no args and one fault
width (the §4.5 expansion names none). At execution (`action.rs`
`verify_inverse_pair`), before any state change, both oracles run on every
n-bit input under the actual token: FAULT_NONE everywhere and
g∘ginv = ginv∘g = id, else a §4.5 error. Tests (`tests/r1_qinplace.rs`):
`b07_zero_zero_pair_is_rejected_before_mutation` (B = 1 and B = 2, both t,
state unchanged), `b07_not_not_pair_executes_controlled_and_adjoint` (fails at
B = 2, inverts at B = 3, controlled on c, adjoint), and
`b07_interfaces_are_checked_at_load`. RED: 3 FAIL. qinplace had no test at
all before. SPEC-QUESTIONS 26.

## codex B08 — matched oracle uncall — resolved

`src/call_discipline.rs` `validate_matched_oracle_calls` is now a forward
dataflow over the row CFG: each `lift.oracle_uncall` must have an outstanding
`lift.oracle_call` with identical operands on every incoming path (multisets
meet by pointwise minimum), consuming one. An outstanding call is invalidated
by any write to its ins, tgt or fr other than oracle XOR delivery (which
commutes) and by a possible write to a supplied cell: a store whose address is
a known `lift.addr` constant outside the region does not invalidate; an
unknown address, a perm call with a mut region, or a `lift.call` whose closure
stores does. Tests (`tests/r1_rules.rs`):
`b08_two_calls_then_two_matched_uncalls` (input 8, tk = (3,0,0,0), B = 5:
(0, 0, 5); a third uncall is rejected), `b08_disjoint_global_store_between_a_matched_pair`
(store to global g at 32, region db at 16: accepted and run to (0, 0, 6);
store through `lift.addr @db`: rejected). RED: both FAIL.

## codex B09 — whole-run reversal — resolved

`src/classical.rs` `reverse`: history traversal undoes frame effects and skips
reversed frames and uncall markers (§7.4); afterwards the run's administrative
control (activation stack, next instance id, fault/finished/pending) is the
control recorded before the first frame, so a run whose first frame opens a
later-cancelled segment ends at its entry. Test: `b09_whole_run_reversal_after_an_initial_cancelled_segment`
(`main: call @f; uncall @f () (); ret`, `f: ret`; run(4) and reversal twice).
RED: FAIL.

## codex B10 — ptr arguments — resolved

`src/oracle.rs` `check_argument` is the one §3.3 classical-argument check for
oracles, actions and CC region calls (ptr included). Test:
`b10_pointer_arguments_reach_permutation_actions` (B = 2: (1, 0, 2), machine
agrees and reverses; p = 2^32 rejected). RED: FAIL.

## codex B11 — block order — resolved

`src/validation.rs` `validate_classical` types definitions to a fixpoint
(`classical_instruction`), independent of block text order. Reading a name
with no instance on the executed path is FAULT_UB_TRAP. Test:
`b11_classical_definitions_need_not_precede_uses_in_text` (run(4) = 7,
reversal restores entry). RED: FAIL. SPEC-QUESTIONS 24.

## codex B13 — malformed callees — resolved

`src/schema.rs` `validate_local_schemas` checks the §4.8 operand schema of every
structured and classical instruction before any pass reads callee bodies.
Test: `b13_malformed_callee_is_a_diagnostic_never_a_panic` (`Object::parse`
returns a §4.8 error; the CLI exits 1 citing §4.8). RED: FAIL (panic at

## codex B14, muse B6 — borrow frames — resolved

`src/borrow.rs` decides P_F = P′ ⊗ I_B exactly: every wire's final value is an
algebraic-normal-form polynomial over the frame's inputs (canonical, so the
decision covers the full domain); loops are composed by repeated squaring;
permutation actions are inlined; quantum memory is multiplexed exactly;
black-box oracle and qinplace calls are canonical symbols when their inputs do
not depend on borrowed wires. The 16-wire cap and the 10^6 loop cap are gone.
The translation lemma remains the structural route. A frame the decision
cannot settle is admitted only through verified certificate `borrow_frames`
claims (`claims.rs` `borrow_frames_certified`), the "library certificate"
route. `Object::verify_certificate` re-executes claims and rejects altered and
incomplete ones.

Tests (`tests/r1_borrow.rs`): `codex_b14_seventeen_wire_swap_identity_frame`
(512 samples, plus the ignored exhaustive 2^17 run),
`muse_b6_eighteen_wire_paired_cx_frame_and_its_dependent_variant`,
`borrow_frames_inside_bounded_loops_are_composed_not_unrolled` (X^(2^40)
accepted and executed; an odd count rejected; the order-3 map cubed accepted,
squared rejected). `tests/r1_certificates.rs`
`b14_checked_borrow_claim_and_altered_or_incomplete_claims` (a proof against an
identity program and against a full table; one wrong table row rejected; a
domain short of D is evidence and is rejected as a borrow_frames proof; a claim
without the borrowed bundle is rejected) and the ignored 17-wire claim. While
running the 2^40-iteration loop I found the executor ran it literally; it now
skips whole periods once its exact state returns to the loop-entry value.
RED: 3 FAIL; the claim tests had no API at `0164b5a`. SPEC-QUESTIONS 20, 21.

## codex B15 — exact cleanliness — resolved

`src/exact.rs`: every amplitude reachable by §4.4 gates lies in
Q(√2, i)[z, 1/z] with dyadic coefficients and z = e^{i·2^−1075}, because every
finite binary64 angle is an integer multiple of 2^−1074; z is transcendental
(Lindemann–Weierstrass), so a Laurent polynomial is zero iff its coefficients
are. `src/quantum.rs` carries this exact shadow beside the binary64 amplitudes
(which now serve only Born probabilities) and decides release, basis reads and
state equality exactly. The superposition form is sparse over arbitrary-width
basis keys, so the fixed 24-wire limit is gone too. Tests (`tests/r1_exact.rs`):
`b15_tiny_rotation_is_not_clean_and_release_changes_nothing` (ry(1e-13) and
rx(1e-300)), `b15_exact_adjoints_release_cleanly`,
`b15_cc_free_of_an_almost_clean_register_traps` (fault 4, handle still live; the
adjoint pair frees cleanly and reverses), `superpositions_have_no_wire_limit`
(a 200-wire GHZ state). RED: 3 FAIL.

## codex B16, muse B7 — metadata and claims — resolved (variant enum declined in part)

At `0164b5a` the codex job had already added typed recursive schemas: the
council's schedule witnesses (boolean, null and negative budgets, phase
"garbage", malformed paths, negative start time) and certificate witnesses
(`versions:false`, false bindings, false composition fields, `{"bogus":1}`
claims, unknown fields) were rejected there; `tests/r1_certificates.rs`
`b16_schedule_values_are_typed` and
`b16_muse_b7_certificate_values_and_claims_are_typed` pin them. Added now:
variants contain no `:` (keys are `<variant>:<controls>`), domain bounds are
exact at any width (`Json::uint_text`), and claims are checked, not just
parsed (`src/claims.rs`, B14). Declined in part: codex objects to
`variant: "banana"`. The specification never lists variant names (§6.4, §11,
§12 only use "variant" as a key component), so rejecting a name would invent
an enum; SPEC-QUESTIONS 11 proposes 0.9 wording.

## codex B17 — certificate composition — resolved

`src/identity.rs`: closure hashes over pinned imports use the pin (§9.3 makes
the linked closure equal it), so a client's closure hash, and its certificate
region, exist before linking. `src/linking.rs` `compose_certificates` unites
region records and multiplicities (equal where they meet), rebinds every hash
including `<hash>:<variant>:<c>` keys and changed schedule hashes (a rebinding
collision is an error, never an overwrite), requires equal versions, dialect
mapping and target bindings, and recomputes `epsilon_total` exactly
(`exact::Decimal`). Tests (`tests/r1_linking.rs`):
`b17_certified_client_and_callee_link_and_compose` (both regions retained,
bindings re-validated by the re-parse, epsilon_total = 3 × 0.25 × 2 + 0.1 =
1.6, client(8) with tk = 3 → (9, 0, 2)), `b17_incompatible_certificates_are_link_errors`,
`interface_region_names_cannot_alias_symbols` (fable's §9.2 suggestion). RED:
3 FAIL. SPEC-QUESTIONS 22.

## codex B18 — fixture audit — resolved

`tests/r1_fixtures.rs` enumerates `tests/fixtures/*.bisa`
(`b18_every_bisa_file_is_audited_and_has_a_comments_file`), shows a corrupted
tiny_memory hash is detected (`b18_a_corrupted_stored_hash_is_detected_by_the_same_audit`),
and checks the inc8 and sum_db fixtures byte-for-byte against the §16.3 text
(fable's suggestion). The hand-listed loop in `tests/identity.rs` is removed.

and Q regions; a CC function calls CC or R functions; `uncall` follows the same
graph, and a CC segment containing `measure` traps when uncalled (§7.4). The

§4.6 defines `qstore name a v` as "for each i: under `a == i`, `qxor v
cell_i`", and §5.1 admits `in` wires "as `qcopy`/`qxor` sources": the stored
value is a qxor source and is never modified. `qexchm` exchanges its value
into a cell, so an `in` value there is rejected. Test:
`muse_b4_qstore_value_is_a_qxor_source_and_may_be_in`. SPEC-QUESTIONS 23
proposes adding "qstore values" to the §5.1 list.
````

````markdown
# Editor response: council round 10

Both distinct S0 core blockers are resolved. Inputs: the round-10 brief,
binding round-9/8/7 briefs, both members' full blocker text and exact objects
in report.md/out-sol.json/out-codex.json, accepted ISA 0.8, interpreter

completion of staged deliverables 8–11 or an independent council-wide audit.

## Design

1. The §16.2 fhead recognizer couples fn exclusively to cc/r; Q kinds are bare.
2. Function boundaries use that same recognizer; malformed later headers fail grammar before semantic validation.
3. Present bounds and explicit LHS productions require at least one element; empty operands and omitted bounds remain legal.
4. Legal header-like SSA names remain legal; exact object/function bytes are never normalized before hashing.
5. Lexical predicate stacks retain ordering, duplicates, push/pop matching and expansion-owned floors.
6. EffectiveControls resolves scalar physical wire literals, retains polarity, sorts, and deduplicates equal literals.
7. Every §6 context-bearing key uses that semantic set with complete current version-stack snapshots and dependency metadata.
8. Copy/load creation records, oracle/action/gate/memory/phase keys and single/joint changes obey the same rule.
9. Borrow compilation canonicalizes after physical resolution, including direct qpred, and canonicalizes again after callee/loop instantiation.
10. Inverse events still require the same event atop ALL operand histories; those histories retain changes to control versions.
11. ABI operands remain ordered; callee(s), token/classical specialization, polarity and explicit qinplace g/ginv inverse identities remain significant.
12. Physical frames, full borrowed-touch guards, lifetime barriers and every return's restoration/independence obligations remain mandatory. No cap or frame waiver.

and four bare Q kinds. Its optional bounds suffix contains a mandatory first
INT. Its optional assignment contains a mandatory first NAME. By contrast,
operand lists can be empty. Therefore bare cc/r, all four fn-prefixed Q
kinds, bounds {}, and () = are grammar errors before ret/lift.retval executes.
Canonical fn cc @a with a single ret completes in exactly one row and returns
[]; adding an empty regs declaration without bounds has the same execution.
````

````markdown
Hand derivation 1: @o returns its input in one row. At B>=1 it is the
identity permutation: both qinplace rows are I, H² restores c=0 and
CX(0,b)=I on arbitrary bR. At B=0 every input faults with code 1, violating
qinplace's fault-free premise. Reject §4.5, never claim identity execution.

generator's sol-qinplace branch. Direct oracle_call fixtures retain their
valid same-token fault-XOR cancellation. All four R9 object bytes/pins remain.

Hand derivation 2: theta=6.283185307179586 is the exact binary64 rational
884279719003555/140737488355328, not symbolic 2*pi. At t=p=0 the rounded
H p; ctl p phase; H p circuit has amplitudes (1+exp(-i*theta/2))/2 on 00 and
(1-exp(-i*theta/2))/2 on 01. P(p=0)=cos(theta/4)^2 > 0, approximately
3.749399456654644e-33. Both support keys survive display rounding.
S S X S S X instead acts as X Z X Z=-I on both basis vectors. Controlled
minus-I is exactly Z on p, so H Z H takes p=0 to p=1.
````

````markdown
# Editor response: council round 12

Both S0 blockers are resolved: SOL-R12-B01 ≡ codex R12-B01 (contract) and
codex R12-B02 (core). None declined or partial. Sole implementation sub-agent;

## Design

1. A layout leaf carries original JSON key components, rendered path and value.
2. The rendered dotted path never serves as unique structural identity.
3. CC/R retain every layout leaf, including coincident renderings.
4. Oracle selection uses the exact original owner key, preserving round 11.
5. Lprocs select exact referenced global keys and their images, once per leaf.
6. Action/data closure exclusions and image collection remain unchanged.
7. Sort by rendered path bytewise, then original components component-wise bytewise.
8. The tie order is independent of values; dots remain legal at every depth.
9. Graph construction and envelope replacement share contextual token classification.
10. Only lift.addr naming the current oracle's declared interface stays literal.
11. Calls, qregion images and actual globals retain ordinary symbol dependencies.
12. Symbol/import spelling alone imposes no interface-name ban; the separate existing
    actual-global/interface ambiguity is recorded narrowly in SPEC-QUESTIONS 32.

No quantum, budget, borrow, lifetime, causal-history or execution semantics were
changed. All round 4–12 positives and negatives are retained. No cap, frame
waiver, fallback, default address or narrowing of north-star scope was added.
````

````markdown
## Design

1. `metadata_types.rs::Object::validate_metadata_types` checks every accepted
   metadata section before identity, binding or execution consumers.
2. Record/array/map fields and optional/tagged payloads are schema-typed.

6. Host services retain arbitrary string versions; no model-0.8 rule is added.
7. `block_image`, when present, names defined data using the data NAME syntax.
8. Its complete-512-byte-sector invariant is checked at load for every kind.
9. The classical constructor also uses a checked image lookup for mutable Objects.
10. Derived Hc/Ac/Sc additions are checked; depth and bit-vector storage already
    use checked arithmetic. Host representation errors cite the ISA.
11. Legal layout admission and sequential B=0 semantics stay unchanged; no
    exponent cap or quiet fallback is introduced.

    collision is recorded as a 0.9 spec defect, not repaired in the interpreter.

slot sizing. Admitted layouts retain sequential B=0 (0,1,0).
````

## `council/response-round-14.md` (222 lines)

````markdown
# Editor response: council round 14

Both S0 blockers, **R14-B01 and R14-B02**, are resolved; none declined or
partial. Sole implementation sub-agent; binding round-7–14 briefs, repository
instructions and the full codex report/JSON read. Implementation commit
**7f834d0**; final evidence/correction commit **198c08a**. Only owned interpreter paths and this response are committed;
no push. Concurrent spec/conformance work is untouched.

## Design

1. `src/metadata_schema.rs::TABLE` is the single recursive admission grammar:
   **162 named productions**, each with the determining clause.
2. It covers all seven JSON metadata sections: symbols, imports, devices,
   layout, schedule, certificate and coverage; every signature alternative;
   and the textual data section's NAME/HEX projection (§9.1/§16.2).
3. Productions cover §9.1 sections/signatures/integers, §9.2 hashes/points,
   §9.4 frame descriptors, §8.1 expressions, §11 schedules, §12.1 claims and
   interval encoding, §12.2 domains/tuple enumeration and §12.3 composition,
   as well as §13 coverage. Optional keys, closed objects, arrays, maps, tuples,
   enum alternatives and recursive expression operands are explicit.
4. `metadata_types::Object::validate_metadata_types` validates the metadata
   root before identities. `validate_certificate_details` and `validate_claim`
   consume the same table. Signature admission and data-line parsing also use
   it. Metadata hash/text/decimal helpers delegate to table productions.
5. Previous hand-written field/type schemas in object.rs, validation.rs,
   metadata.rs and certificate.rs are removed; no second schema remains.
6. Semantic checks remain where context is available: object.rs resolves
   images and layout intervals; metadata.rs resolves schedule/coverage points,
   checks payload agreement and entry overlap; certificate.rs checks domain
   names/ranges, claim indices, expression arity/environments, live ranges and
   certificate bindings; validation.rs checks device model compatibility.
   These checks cite their determining clauses.
7. Table components are arbitrary-size canonical §9.1 unsigned integers.
   Their truth, cardinality, widths and complete-result comparisons remain
   verifier obligations, not load-time execution.
8. Y entries are four signed finite decimal strings. Ordinary nonnegative
   decimals retain number/string forms; §8.1 expressions retain numeric and
   closed recursive AST forms. No ISA exponent or integer-width cap is added.
9. The derived family walks generated grammar examples and real pinned objects,
   recursively including array elements and object fields. Wrong-kind
   expectations derive from Shape independently of observed validator results.
10. Every production, enum/union alternative and optional absence is generated;
    positive substitutions exercise each accepted alternative at visited paths.
    Table rows/components are populated, including a component above u128.
11. The R13 path-specific union and family are replaced. The historical local
    round-13 response has a correction withdrawing its completeness claim.
12. Numerical/channel execution remains explicitly Unverified at the staged
    interval-verifier boundary. Scope and the recorded §9.2 dotted-path
    limitation are unchanged; no new spec reading or waiver is needed.

## R14-B01 — resolved

Determining clause: §12.1 explicitly encodes Y entries as decimal strings.
The exact reviewer object is copied byte-for-byte as
`tests/support/r14-witnesses/r14-Y-number.bisa`, full-file SHA-256
`578c913bb276d1446e2e038af0ab0a77017d9abe5ec351e3e20b69c307068e11`.

RED tests:

- `metadata::r14_y_endpoints_require_decimal_strings`
- `cli_xam::r14_cli_rejects_numeric_y_endpoints`

Both failed: parse admitted numeric endpoints; CLI check returned exit 0,
status ok and the reviewer's object hash. GREEN rejects the exact object and
````

````markdown
# Editor response: council round 15

Both S0 blockers, **R15-B01 and R15-B02**, are resolved; none declined or
partial. Sole implementation sub-agent; binding round-7–14 briefs, repository
instructions and the full codex report/JSON read. Implementation commit

## Design

1. `src/metadata_schema.rs::TABLE` remains the single recursive structural
   admission grammar, now **163 named productions**, each citing its clause.
2. `translation_witness.frame` uses the new `translation_frame` production:
   `Shape::Tuple(&["point", "point"])`, implementing §12.1's first/last points.
   V and W retain `Array(point)`, including empty and longer arrays.
3. `certificate.rs::validate_claim` consumes the grammar and no longer repeats
   frame cardinality. Claim-index and other contextual checks remain there.
4. Oracle schedule exactness is a semantic value constraint (§§4.4, 5.2, 11).
   After decimal validation, zero means every mantissa digit is zero; the
   decimal scale/exponent cannot change that decision. No binary64 conversion
   is used for the zero decision, and no exponent/precision cap is added.
5. README's metadata Design paragraph records that structural/semantic split
   and the regenerated counts. The family tests enforcement of TABLE, while
   the independent literal cardinality/value controls test the cited rules.

   are unchanged. Numerical/channel claims remain explicitly Unverified at
   the existing staged boundary; no new spec reading or waiver is needed.

constructs literal all-zero-hash points independently of TABLE, samples and

Commit **9283db7**.

gates, and §11 carries accuracy as decimal text. JCS does not canonicalize
````

## `council/response-round-17.md` (267 lines)

````markdown
# Editor response: council round 17

Both S0 blockers, **R17-B01** and **R17-B02**, are resolved; none declined or
partial. Sole implementation sub-agent; repo instructions, binding round-7–16
briefs/responses, full round-17 report and reviewer JSON read. Implementation
commit **e72df8cf78aca2b0516e20496b2f4f631df2e504**. Final evidence commit:
**3458961098c5cc4745092b5ccd923d8c038cbc70**. Only owned interpreter paths and this response are committed.
No push. Concurrent spec/conformance work is untouched.

## Design

1. `src/metadata_schema.rs::TABLE` remains the sole recursive structural
   admission grammar, 163 named productions. `gate_payload` declares
   `epsilon_share?:decimal`, with §§11/17 item 9 cited. `realisation` remains
   required. Present malformed values are never converted to defaults.
2. `Object::schedule_epsilon_share` returns an explicit assigned share, or
   the exact recipe `region epsilon / approximate_operations`; expansion
   must supply the latter count. Exact operations return `Exact`. No binary64
   division, synthetic admission-time share or canonical-document mutation.
   The recipe represents nonterminating rational shares without rounding.
3. The requested class audit found one more incorrectly required default:
   `sampler.count` (§17 item 13). TABLE now marks it optional;
   `claims::sample_count` defaults to 65,536 in the actual replay consumer.
   Explicit counts including 0 are preserved and present values use TABLE.
4. `r17_section17_defaults_are_optional_and_applied` is a literal,
   clause-derived table over every numbered §17 item. Where an item has a
   metadata field, the test asserts the optional TABLE key AND admits the
   independent omitted form. It tests implemented consumer observations and
   records the staged/non-metadata boundaries honestly; target aggregation,
   enclosure procedures and hardware/C-layout choices are not silently
   counted as completed object-metadata consumers.
5. Specificity is the literal §11 lexicographic tuple. Equal-score overlap
   is only a candidate tie. `metadata/schedule_domains.rs` intersects both
   entries with legal invocation/iteration domains and oracle steps 1..B,
   then subtracts the UNION of every strictly higher selector of that kind.
   Ambiguity exists exactly when some selector-domain remainder survives.
6. Domains use interval boxes split only at selector boundaries. Zero-trip
   loop bodies are empty; `[]` outside loops is a singleton. Loop and step
   counts are never expanded or capped. Generated ordinals stay symbolic for
   the bound expansion library; this is admission, not target execution.
7. Shortest real invocation chains suffice: every instruction, including a
   call, has its own generated operations (§11). Longer paths cannot cover
   those operations. Covering them with prefixes covers their extensions too.
   An empty selector path is partitioned over real root instructions, never
   a fictitious empty operation chain. Existing path validation checks every
   symbol/program point/call edge and explicit iteration vector.
8. `resolve_schedule` counts maxima only after inspecting all matches, so
   shadowed ties are harmless regardless of document order, and an actual
   final tie errors rather than selecting the first entry.
9. README Design and PROGRESS document the algorithm, defaults and observed
   evidence. No ISA amendment or new narrowing reading is needed. Existing
   target/schedule-execution and rigorous interval-checking stages remain
   staged/Unverified; neither blocker requires claiming those stages finished.
````

````markdown
# Editor response: council round 4

Round-5 correction: R4-B01/MUSE-R4-B01 evidence below established rejection
without certificates. SOL-R5-B01 found that certificate fallback readmitted
both invalid lifetimes; SOL-R5-B02 found that generic Repeat lost known-clean
entry invariants. The corrective implementation and certified/clean-context
regressions are recorded in response-round-5.md; historical green counts below
are evidence for their stated runs, not certified-admission coverage.

Inputs: codex out-codex.json and sol out-sol.json, snapshot 8e11fe7. This
response is appendable for the pending muse pass. Owned paths are exclusively
reference-interpreter; ISA 0.8, the Python seed and random seeds are unchanged.

## R4-B01 — resolved

RED: `r1_borrow::r4_loop_local_returns_cannot_be_restored_by_later_borrowings`
accepted the exact loop-local borrow/X/return witness before the fix.
`src/borrow.rs::Node` now retains Borrow/Return lifetime boundaries;
Compiler emits them and reverses them under adjoints. Evaluation checks
restoration of every returned wire and independence of every other live
output at Return, then removes the returned system. Repeat proves these
boundaries on the generic body BEFORE composing its surviving-wire map by
squaring. Borrowing starts a fresh independent symbolic entry. Lifetimes
spanning a loop remain in its map and are checked only at their actual return.
Zero-trip loops apply no lifetime; no unrolling threshold or new cap is added.
````

````markdown
non-permutation touches are errors independently of tuple/phase cancellation.
Zero-trip bodies remain unexecuted. This guard never calls certificate
admission recursively and does not require an entire action to be a permutation.

§12.1's structural checker obligation is “check the rule's side conditions
syntactically against the object and the subclaims' results”. Its exhaustive
obligation is “re-execute every domain element … compare full tuples”, not
permission to waive another claim's premise. §5.6 requires “maximal contiguous
permutation-only subcircuits”; §14.3 T3 begins “If the realised unitary V … is a
permutation matrix”. CZ = diag(1,1,1,−1) (§4.4) fails that premise even if
particular reachable inputs hide its phase. Tuple Proof alone is not a borrow
proof; verification.borrow_frames now explicitly checks the premise in both
admission surfaces.
````

````markdown
Inputs: full `out-sol.json` and `out-codex.json`, reviewed snapshot 67d1b94.
All four S0 findings are resolved; no declines or partials. Final verification is recorded below.
Owned paths: `reference-interpreter/` and this response only. No push, dependency,
RNG-distribution, accepted-spec, conformance or Python-seed change.
Tracking: b-isa-spec-lto; cycle-key correction b-isa-spec-gui; performance
follow-up b-isa-spec-436. Staged deliverables 8–11 retain their disclosures.

## Design

1. A live wire has an ANF basis expression; an unconstrained entry is a variable.
2. Only allocation supplies zero. Losing information supplies a fresh unknown.
3. X-family gates transform target expressions; controls remain read-only.
4. Controlled swaps transform both outputs with the complete condition.
5. Diagonal gates preserve basis expressions, including known zero/one.
6. A false predicate disables the gate's fact transfer, not its §5.6 touch guard.
7. Non-diagonal targets become unknown; an untouched exact inverse restores saved expressions.
8. Any intervening operand touch invalidates the inverse record, including entangling gates.
9. Every quantum gate still ends a frame; the full touched set guards borrowed controls/targets.
10. Every return retains restoration and output-independence equations; certificates cannot waive them.
11. Zero trips transfer nothing; permutation loops square maps and obligations with the actual bound.
12. Mixed loops traverse exact entries, skip identical full analysis states, or prove a joined unknown-top invariant.

`src/borrow.rs::Compiler::compile` emits structured Repeat nodes for all loops
and Quantum nodes carrying gate action separately from the full touched set.
`Facts::sequence`, `repeat`, `invariant`, `flush` replace prefix replay.
No `n.min(3)`, frame merging, sampled admission or semantic trip limit remains.
Inverse records preserve old correlations, and every intervening multi-wire
touch invalidates them; unknown results cannot resurrect a clean value.
`Evaluation::apply` retains exact permutation/opaque composition and every
per-return obligation. The cropped translation-lemma route still requires all
lifetime equations. Opaque unresolved proofs retain their certificate route.
Execution's quantum cycle skipping remains separate from analysis.

## SOL-R7-B03 — resolved

RED: `exact::r7_tests::r7_dyadic_scaled_conversion_boundary_rounding_and_subnormals`
failed at k=1024 with NaN instead of 1.0; the pinned CLI replay
`r7_cli_bounded_5000_h_t_reports_finite_amplitudes` failed exit 1, empty stdout,
`§16.1: non-finite binary64 has no JSON number`.
`r7_root2_cancellation_does_not_overflow_intermediate_terms` also failed its
finite-positive assertion for (1−sqrt(2))^810.

`exact.rs::Dyadic::to_f64` rounds a bounded mantissa using guard/sticky bits and
the net exponent (nearest, ties to even). Subnormals use their exact binary64
power-of-two encoding, avoiding powi's intermediate underflow. `Root2::to_f64`
uses `exact/measurement.rs::root2_approximate` when separate terms would
otherwise overflow or severely cancel, refining dyadic enclosures until both
endpoints round alike. No NaN clamp, gate/denominator ceiling, or weakened JSON
non-finite check. Implementation commit: **51d45dc**.
````

````markdown
# Editor response: council round 8

Inputs: full `out-sol.json` and `out-codex.json`, reviewed snapshot 00ceee2,
and both implementation briefs. All four distinct S0 findings are resolved;
final verification is recorded below. Owned paths: `reference-interpreter/`
and this response only. No push, dependency, RNG-distribution, accepted-spec,
conformance or Python-seed change. Tracking: b-isa-spec-41i and the adjacent
version-sensitive cleanup finding b-isa-spec-2kd. Staged deliverables 8–11
retain their disclosures.

## Design

1. A live wire has an ANF basis expression; allocation alone supplies zero.
2. Diagonal gates and read-only controls preserve basis facts; permutations transform ANFs.
3. Non-diagonal targets become fresh unknowns; no unknown result invents a fact.
4. Each information-losing gate pushes its saved expressions on every operand stack.
5. Reversible gates above those histories push likewise; independent wire stacks interleave.
6. An exact adjoint pops only when the same saved event tops ALL operand stacks.
7. Nested pairs restore LIFO; outstanding readers block an outer pop; opaque/lifetime barriers invalidate connected history.
8. One structured source lowering publishes both physical bindings/borrow sets and the fact-node program; zero trips publish none of them. Static dead-body checks and lexical qregion hoisting remain.
9. Local calls reuse canonical structured per-wire transfers, memoised by callee and exact classical specialization; SCC validation excludes action recursion (§5.1).
10. Effective controls predicate callee gates; a known-false call transfers no facts; imported calls leave modified outputs unknown and preserve read-only operands.
11. Every physical quantum gate/call boundary and FULL borrowed-touch guard remains, including disabled calls; every return proves restoration and output independence.
12. Permutation loops square maps AND return obligations; mixed loops visit exact entries, skip identical complete analysis states or prove an unknown-top inductive invariant. No sampled admission or semantic trip cap.

`borrow.rs::Facts::{reversible,forget_inverses,sequence}` implement the causal
per-wire stacks. Ordinary basis permutations need no history unless they touch
an existing quantum history: their ANFs already retain exact basis information.
Saved expressions include every operand, preserving correlations. The stack
checks all controls and targets, so an unmatched entangling operation cannot
resurrect a saved clean control. Physical frame boundaries are retained even
when a pair cancels in the fact domain.

`Compiler::compile` is the sole traversal of source lifetime/binding effects;
it emits the exact structured node program that Facts traverses. Zero-trip
bodies are omitted there before any `produce`, live-borrow mutation, call,
node or trace effect, following the existing `action.rs::LifetimeWidths`
executed-lifetime rule. There is no successor environment inferred from a dead
body. Static validation still checks that body in its cloned state; function
entry still hoists every lexical qregion, including declarations in dead bodies.

`Compiler::call_transfer` compiles a local callee into canonical wire coordinates
once per classical specialization, including nested calls, then remaps the
structured effect onto actual operands. The cache is shared by child compilers.
`Node::Call` separates its complete physical touched set from mutable outputs
and the analysed transfer. `Facts::sequence` handles its predicate and transfer;
`check_permutation_touches` independently checks the full call touch set and
recurses into callee-local lifetimes. Imported calls leave facts unknown only on modified outputs; opaque readers
invalidate inverse history across all touched operands, including read-only
controls, without erasing those controls' current basis facts. The existing Tarjan SCC call-graph validation runs first;
recursion through lifted oracle procedures remains opaque to this action pass.
````

## `council/response-round-9.md` (242 lines)

````markdown
# Editor response: council round 9

Both distinct S0 core blockers are resolved. Inputs are the round-9 brief,
its binding round-8/7 briefs, the full member blocker objects and pins in
report.md/out-sol.json/out-codex.json, and accepted ISA 0.8. Tracking:
b-isa-spec-82k. Sole interpreter implementer; only reference-interpreter/ and
this response were changed/committed. No push, spec/conformance/Python-seed,
dependency, RNG-distribution or seed change. Existing deliverables 8–11 retain
their staging; this response claims neither their completion nor conformance
harness results. The concurrent intentionally red conformance test was not run.

## Design

1. Each live wire has an ANF basis expression; allocation alone supplies zero.
2. Permutations transform expressions, diagonals/readonly controls preserve them, and non-diagonal targets become independent unknowns.
3. Causal events save all operand expressions on every operand's LIFO stack.
4. A matching adjoint restores them only when the same event tops ALL those stacks.
5. Oracle calls carry a self-adjoint key; qinplace carries explicit swapped g/ginv keys.
6. Keys include callees, classical/token specialisation, controls and actual input/memory/output wires.
7. Unmatched opaque readers block outer restoration; lifetime/unresolved-import barriers invalidate connected histories.
8. Assigning qinplace starts history even on known basis entries; its loops use causal transfer, not uninterpreted assignment squaring.
9. Source lifetime lowering consumes released names and resolves each visit against its current live binding map.
10. Equal-width, equal-role, nonoverlapping successor lifetimes alpha-rename to reusable entry slots; changed maps get distinct transfers, recurring maps share a structured cycle.
11. Zero visits publish nothing; lexical qregions remain hoisted. No count cap or sampled/truncated admission.
12. Physical frame boundaries, full borrowed-touch checks and every return's restoration/independence proof remain mandatory. Ordinary permutation maps and return obligations still square; mixed/history transfers retain the existing exact-cycle/invariant rules.

## SOL-R9-B01 ≡ codex R9-B01 — resolved

Sections: §§4.5, 4.7, 5.2, 5.3, 5.6, 6.2, 14.2.

RED before source edits: library **0 passed / 4 failed**, CLI **0 passed /
4 failed**, covering the three opaque subjects and the separate loop subject.
All four in each target rejected with `§5.6: a wire released inside a borrow
frame is not clean`; CLI exit 1 and no data output. Logs:
`.tmp/r9-red-library.log`, `.tmp/r9-red-cli.log`. Initial test setup compilation
mistakes (Argument supplied in the controls slot, then the wrong bindings field)
were corrected before these semantic RED runs and are not reproduction evidence.

Hand derivation: @o reaches lift.retval in one row. At B=1, it XORs c into
Sol's t or codex's d and leaves f=0; the identical call cancels that XOR.
At B=0, payload=0 and code=1, so two fault XORs cancel as well. Thus
H;O;O;H restores c=0 and leaves all other quantum operands unchanged.
CX(0,b)=I for every bR, and every allocated workspace wire is clean at exit.
Sol's qinplace uses a fault-free identity oracle at B=1; the explicit inverse
is normative, and the same cancellation applies to arbitrary valid g/ginv
when the second key swaps them. B=0 must still fail the runtime §4.5 guard.
No function-specific certificate or new specification reading is involved.

Changes: `borrow.rs::Node::{adjoint,instantiate}` preserve an explicit opaque
inverse identity; `Compiler::compile` supplies self-adjoint oracle and swapped
qinplace keys. `Facts::{sequence,reversible}` route opaque events through the
same all-operand stacks as primitive gates, rather than forgetting their
ancestors. Operands read by an unmatched opaque call remain on top, preventing
an outer H pop. `forget_inverses` still invalidates connected history at genuine
barriers. Assigning qinplace creates a saved event even without a preceding H.

An additional RED audit, `r9_qinplace_repeated_pairs_on_clean_workspace`, was
**0/1**, with the same §5.6 diagnostic. A pure permutation Repeat was composing
opaque assignments as g^-1(g(x)), without causal cancellation. `Node::needs_history`
now routes such loops through the stack transfer/cycle. GREEN: **8/0** across
six library regressions and the two R9 families; no runtime or count restriction.

Exact library witnesses:

- `r9_opaque_adjoint_restores_borrow_control` (Sol oracle)
- `r9_matched_opaque_oracle_restores_outer_fact` (codex oracle)
- `r9_qinplace_adjoint_restores_borrow_control` (Sol qinplace)
- `r9_qinplace_zero_budget_rejects_before_mutation`
- `r9_qinplace_repeated_pairs_on_clean_workspace`

`generated_r9_opaque_histories_match_independent_identity`: **13 accepted /

## codex R9-B02 — resolved

Sections: §§3.3, 4.3, 4.6, 5.3, 5.6, 14.2.

The exact library `r9_mixed_loop_threads_reallocated_bindings` and CLI
`r9_cli_mixed_loop_threads_reallocated_bindings` were each RED as part of the
0/4 runs above; now both are GREEN with the member's exact signature, function,
interface/closure and object pins.

Hand derivation: c=0 before the first visit. Each visit applies CX(0,b),
returns b unchanged and independent of every surviving output, frees clean c,
allocates a new zero c, and applies H²=I to t. Induction gives c=0 at every
visit and final release; the region is I_t tensor I_bR on arbitrary bR.
Zero visits leave the original c binding untouched.

Changes: `Compiler::compile` removes consumed qfree/qreturn/quncopy/qunload
bindings. `Compiler::compile_repeat` compiles against the actual current entry
map and publishes its successor. A freshly produced successor can reuse an
entry slot only at equal width/borrow role and after that old slot is absent
from every live successor binding. This renames nonoverlapping lifetimes;
it performs no quantum exchange and carries no fact across release. Allocation
and lifetime barriers still reset/check the reused slot. First-visit changes
(e.g. width 1 to 2) compile separately; repeated live maps reuse the exact cycle
of structured transfers. Frames and trace snapshots receive the same alpha
renaming. No expansion proportional to n and no trip cap. Existing zero-trip
omission and unconditional lexical qregion hoisting remain.

`generated_r9_loop_bindings_match_independent_identity`: **20 accepted /
3 rejected**, covering counts 0/1/2/3, nested loops, alpha-renamed straight-line
expansions, first-visit width changes and dirty controls that reject at their
first invalid return. Nineteen positives execute the independent I_t tensor I_bR
map on all library inputs above; the **2^40** positive checks analysis/hash only.
A fresh-wire runtime exploration at 2^40 was stopped without a completed result:
execution's existing cycle key distinguishes newly allocated wire ids. It is
not claimed as an execution pass or rejection; existing performance follow-up
b-isa-spec-436 now records it. No execution limit was added or capability removed.
````
