````rust
use crate::{err, object::list, validation::normalize_call, Error, Function, Object, Result, Type};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
#[derive(Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
struct Views {
    live: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    dead: BTreeSet<String>,
}
impl Object {
    pub(crate) fn validate_handle_views(
        &self,
        f: &Function,
        types: &BTreeMap<String, Type>,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let mut work = vec![(0usize, Views::default())];
        let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
        while let Some((block, mut views)) = work.pop() {
            if !seen.insert((block, views.clone())) {
                continue;
            }
            for instruction in &f.blocks[block].instructions {
                let op = instruction.op.as_str();
                let a = &instruction.operands;
                let region = matches!(op, "oracle_call" | "action_call" | "ctl" | "adj");
                let operands: Vec<String> = match op {
                    "qreg.new" => Vec::new(),
                    "qreg.slice" | "qreg.free" | "measure" => vec![a[0].clone()],
                    "qreg.concat" => a.clone(),
                    _ => {
                        let mut values = Vec::new();
                        for operand in a {
                            if operand.starts_with('(') {
                                values.extend(list(operand)?);
                            } else if operand.starts_with('^') {
                                if let Some((_, suffix)) = operand.split_once('(') {
                                    values.extend(list(&format!("({suffix}"))?);
                                }
                            } else {
                                values.push(operand.clone());
                            }
                        }
                        values
                    }
                };
                let handles: Vec<_> = operands
                    .into_iter()
                    .filter(|n| matches!(types.get(n), Some(Type::Qreg(_))))
                    .collect();
                for handle in &handles {
                    if views.live.values().any(|parent| parent == handle) {
                        return err("§3.3", format!("use of viewed parent {handle}"));
                    }
                    if views.dead.contains(handle) {
                        return err("§3.3", format!("view {handle} used after its region call"));
                    }
                    if views.live.contains_key(handle) && !region {
                        return err(
                            "§3.3",
                            format!("view {handle} may only be an operand of one region call"),
                        );
                    }
                }
                if op == "qreg.slice" {
                    let view = instruction.lhs[0].clone();
                    views.dead.remove(&view);
                    views.live.insert(view, a[0].clone());
                }
                if region {
                    normalize_call(instruction)?;
                    for handle in handles {
                        if views.live.remove(&handle).is_some() {
                            views.dead.insert(handle);
                        }
                    }
                }
                if op == "br" {
                    for branch in if a.len() == 1 { &a[..] } else { &a[1..] } {
                        let (label, _) = branch
                            .trim_start_matches('^')
                            .split_once('(')
                            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§3.4: malformed branch".into()))?;
                        let target = f
                            .blocks
                            .iter()
                            .position(|b| b.name == label)
                            .expect("validated block");
                        work.push((target, views.clone()));
                    }
                }
                if matches!(op, "ret" | "trap") && !views.live.is_empty() {
                    return err(
                        "§3.3",
                        "view is not consumed by exactly one region call on every exit path",
                    );
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
````

````rust
use crate::{err, json::Json, object::Function, sha256_hex, Error, Object, Result};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Identity {
    pub interface_hashes: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// None denotes a symbol whose dependency closure still has an unresolved import.
    pub closure_hashes: BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>,
    pub envelopes: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    pub object_hash: String,
    pub scc_members: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>,
    pub scc_hashes: BTreeMap<String, String>,
}

/// Symbol reference tokens only: @ inside a quoted string is ordinary text.
fn references(line: &str) -> Vec<(usize, usize, &str)> {
    let bytes = line.as_bytes();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    let mut quoted = false;
    while i < bytes.len() {
        if quoted {
            if bytes[i] == b'\\' {
                i += 2;
                continue;
            }
            if bytes[i] == b'"' {
                quoted = false;
            }
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        if bytes[i] == b'"' {
            quoted = true;
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        if bytes[i] == b'@'
            && i + 1 < bytes.len()
            && (bytes[i + 1].is_ascii_alphabetic() || bytes[i + 1] == b'_')
        {
            let start = i;
            i += 2;
            while i < bytes.len()
                && (bytes[i].is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(bytes[i], b'_' | b'.'))
            {
                i += 1;
            }
            out.push((start, i, &line[start + 1..i]));
        } else {
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Classify the operand in its validated canonical instruction context. Only
/// the sole operand of lift.addr may denote this oracle's interface (§4.2).
/// Calls, qregion images and metadata still use ordinary symbol references.
fn symbol_references<'a>(
    line: &'a str,
    function: Option<&Function>,
) -> Vec<(usize, usize, &'a str)> {
    if let Some(f) = function.filter(|f| f.kind == "oracle") {
        if let Some(region) = line
            .split_once(" = ")
            .and_then(|(_, rhs)| rhs.strip_prefix("lift.addr @"))
        {
            if f.params[3].iter().any(|p| p.name == region) {
                return Vec::new();
            }
        }
    }
    references(line)
}

impl Object {
    pub fn identity(&self) -> Result<Identity> {
        let symbols: BTreeMap<_, _> = self
            .symbols()?
            .values()
            .map(|s| Ok((s.get("name")?.string()?.to_string(), s)))
            .collect::<Result<_>>()?;
        let imports = self
            .section("imports")
            .map(Json::object)
            .transpose()?
            .cloned()
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let mut graph: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>> = BTreeMap::new();
        for n in symbols.keys() {
            let mut deps = Vec::new();
            if let Some(f) = self.functions.get(n) {
                for line in f.lines.iter().skip(1) {
                    for (_, _, r) in symbol_references(line, Some(f)) {
                        if symbols.contains_key(r) || imports.contains_key(r) {
                            if !deps.iter().any(|s| s == r) {
                                deps.push(r.to_string());
                            }
                        } else {
                            return err("§9.3", format!("unresolved undeclared reference @{r}"));
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            graph.insert(n.clone(), deps);
        }
        // Tarjan emits dependency SCCs before their users.
        let components = components(&graph);
        // One hashing pass; `imported` gives the hash an import reference takes,
        // None for an import whose closure is unknown (not pinned).
        let pass = |imported: BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>| -> Result<HashPass> {
            let mut hashes: BTreeMap<String, String> = BTreeMap::new();
            let mut known: BTreeMap<String, bool> = BTreeMap::new();
            for (n, h) in &imported {
                if let Some(h) = h {
                    hashes.insert(n.clone(), h.clone());
                }
                known.insert(n.clone(), h.is_some());
            }
            let mut out = HashPass::default();
            for comp in &components {
                let closed = comp.iter().all(|n| {
                    graph[n]
                        .iter()
                        .all(|r| comp.contains(r) || known.get(r).copied().unwrap_or(false))
                });
                let mut envs = Vec::new();
                for n in comp {
                    let env = self.envelope(n, symbols[n], comp, &hashes)?;
                    out.envelopes.insert(n.clone(), env.clone());
                    envs.push(env);
                }
                let recursive = comp.len() > 1 || graph[&comp[0]].contains(&comp[0]);
                let scc = sha256_hex(envs.concat().as_bytes());
                for (i, n) in comp.iter().enumerate() {
                    out.scc_members.insert(n.clone(), comp.clone());
                    out.scc_hashes.insert(n.clone(), scc.clone());
                    let hash = if recursive {
                        sha256_hex(format!("{scc}:{i}").as_bytes())
                    } else {
                        sha256_hex(envs[i].as_bytes())
                    };
                    known.insert(n.clone(), closed);
                    out.closed.insert(n.clone(), closed);
                    hashes.insert(n.clone(), hash.clone());
                    out.hashes.insert(n.clone(), hash);
                }
            }
            Ok(out)
        };
        // Interface hashes: SHA-256(name || 0x00 || JCS signature) for imports.
        let mut fingerprints = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut pins = BTreeMap::new();
        for (n, im) in &imports {
            let mut seed = n.as_bytes().to_vec();
            seed.push(0);
            seed.extend_from_slice(im.get("signature")?.canonical().as_bytes());
            fingerprints.insert(n.clone(), Some(sha256_hex(&seed)));
            // Closure hashes: a pinned import's closure hash is fixed by its pin
            // (§9.3 requires equality at link time), so closures over pinned
            // imports are determined before linking.
            let pin = im
                .object()?
                .get("pinned_closure_hash")
                .map(|p| p.string().map(str::to_string))
                .transpose()?;
            pins.insert(n.clone(), pin);
        }
        let interface = pass(fingerprints)?;
        let closures = pass(pins)?;
        let hashes = interface.hashes;
        let closure: BTreeMap<String, Option<String>> = closures
            .hashes
            .into_iter()
            .map(|(n, h)| {
                let closed = closures.closed[&n];
                (n, closed.then_some(h))
            })
            .collect();
        let envelopes = interface.envelopes;
        // SCC grouping and ordering keys are those of executable (closure) identity.
        let scc_members = closures.scc_members;
        let scc_hashes = closures.scc_hashes;
        let mut canonical = String::new();
        let mut skip = false;
        let mut pending_blank = false;
        for line in self.text.lines() {
            if line.is_empty() {
                pending_blank = true;
                continue;
            }
            if let Some(s) = line.strip_prefix("section ") {
                skip = matches!(s, "schedule" | "certificate" | "coverage");
            }
            if !skip {
                if pending_blank {
                    canonical.push('\n');
                }
                canonical.push_str(line);
                canonical.push('\n');
            }
            pending_blank = false;
        }
        Ok(Identity {
            interface_hashes: hashes,
            closure_hashes: closure,
            envelopes,
            object_hash: sha256_hex(canonical.as_bytes()),
            scc_members,
            scc_hashes,
        })
    }
    pub fn check_hashes(&self) -> Result<()> {
        let identity = self.identity()?;
        for s in self.symbols()?.values() {
            let n = s.get("name")?.string()?;
            if s.get("interface_hash")?.string()? != identity.interface_hashes[n] {
                return err(
                    "§9.2",
                    format!(
                        "interface_hash mismatch for @{n}: expected {}",
                        identity.interface_hashes[n]
                    ),
                );
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    fn envelope(
        &self,
        n: &str,
        symbol: &Json,
        comp: &[String],
        hashes: &BTreeMap<String, String>,
    ) -> Result<String> {
        let kind = symbol.get("kind")?.string()?;
        let mut body = if let Some(f) = self.functions.get(n) {
            f.lines.clone()
        } else {
            vec![format!("{n} {}", hex(&self.data[n]))]
        };
        let mut leaves = Vec::new();
        let mut images = BTreeSet::new();
        if let Some(layout) = self.section("layout") {
            let all = layout_leaves(layout)?;
            match kind {
                "cc" | "r" => leaves = all,
                // Ownership is an original JSON key, never a dotted prefix.
                "oracle" => {
                    leaves = all
                        .into_iter()
                        .filter(|leaf| leaf.keys[0] != "interface_regions" || leaf.keys[1] == n)
                        .collect();
                }
                "lproc" => {
                    let globals: BTreeSet<_> = self.functions[n]
                        .instructions()
                        .filter(|i| i.op == "lift.addr")
                        .filter_map(|i| i.operands[0].strip_prefix('@').map(str::to_owned))
                        .collect();
                    leaves = all
                        .into_iter()
                        .filter(|leaf| leaf.keys[0] == "globals" && globals.contains(&leaf.keys[1]))
                        .collect();
                }
                _ => {}
            }
            for leaf in &leaves {
                if let Json::Object(o) = &leaf.value {
                    if let Some(img) = o.get("image") {
                        images.insert(img.string()?.to_string());
                    }
                }
            }
            if matches!(kind, "oracle" | "cc" | "r") {
                if let Some(leaf) = leaves.iter().find(|leaf| leaf.keys == ["block_image"]) {
                    images.insert(leaf.value.string()?.to_string());
                }
            }
        }
        let mut refs = Vec::new();
        let replace = |line: &str, function: Option<&Function>, refs: &mut Vec<String>| -> String {
            let mut out = String::new();
            let mut previous = 0;
            for (start, end, r) in symbol_references(line, function) {
                out.push_str(&line[previous..start]);
                if let Some(index) = comp.iter().position(|n| n == r) {
                    out.push_str(&format!("@${index}"));
                } else if let Some(hash) = hashes.get(r) {
                    out.push('@');
                    out.push_str(hash);
                    if !refs.contains(hash) {
                        refs.push(hash.clone());
                    }
                } else {
                    out.push_str(&line[start..end]);
                }
                previous = end;
            }
            out.push_str(&line[previous..]);
            out
        };
        if self.functions.contains_key(n) {
            for line in body.iter_mut().skip(1) {
                *line = replace(line, self.functions.get(n), &mut refs);
            }
        }
        let mut lines = vec![
            "isa=0.8".into(),
            format!("ptr_width={}", self.ptr_width),
            symbol.get("signature")?.canonical(),
        ];
        lines.extend(body);
        for img in images {
            let bytes = self
                .data
                .get(&img)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§9.2: missing closure data {img}")))?;
            lines.push(replace(
                &format!("data {img} {}", hex(bytes)),
                None,
                &mut refs,
            ));
        }
        for leaf in leaves {
            lines.push(replace(
                &format!("layout {} {}", leaf.path, leaf.value.canonical()),
                None,
                &mut refs,
            ));
        }
        if matches!(kind, "cc" | "r") {
            let mut used = BTreeSet::new();
            for i in self.functions[n].instructions() {
                if i.op == "effect" {
                    if let Some((dev, _)) = i.operands.first().and_then(|s| s.split_once('.')) {
                        used.insert(("models", dev.to_string()));
                    }
                }
                if i.op == "hostcall" {
                    if let Some(service) = i.operands.first() {
                        used.insert(("services", crate::object::literal_name(service)?));
                    }
                }
            }
            let devices = self.section("devices");
            let mut entries = BTreeMap::new();
            for (group, key) in used {
                let entry = devices
                    .map(|d| d.get(group).and_then(Json::object))
                    .transpose()?
                    .and_then(|entries| entries.get(&key));
                if let Some(value) = entry {
                    entries.insert(key, value);
                } else if group == "services"
                    || ["console", "clock", "entropy", "block"].contains(&key.as_str())
                {
                    return err("§9.1", format!("missing declared {group} entry {key}"));
                }
            }
            for (key, v) in entries {
                lines.push(format!("device {key} {}", v.canonical()));
            }

}

/// A dotted rendering is not injective (§16.1 permits dots in NAME).
/// Keep structural identity through selection and emit every leaf once.
struct LayoutLeaf {
    keys: Vec<String>,
    path: String,
    value: Json,
}
fn layout_leaves(layout: &Json) -> Result<Vec<LayoutLeaf>> {
    let mut leaves = Vec::new();
    let mut push = |keys: Vec<String>, value: &Json| {
        leaves.push(LayoutLeaf {
            path: keys.join("."),
            keys,
            value: value.clone(),
        });
    };
    for (k, v) in layout.object()? {
        match k.as_str() {
            "globals" => {
                for (n, e) in v.object()? {
                    push(vec![k.clone(), n.clone()], e);
                }
            }
            "interface_regions" => {
                for (n, rs) in v.object()? {
                    for (r, e) in rs.object()? {
                        push(vec![k.clone(), n.clone(), r.clone()], e);
                    }
                }
            }
            _ => push(vec![k.clone()], v),
        }
    }
    // §9.2 dotted-path order; value-independent tie reading in SPEC-QUESTIONS 31.
    leaves.sort_by(|a, b| a.path.cmp(&b.path).then_with(|| a.keys.cmp(&b.keys)));
    Ok(leaves)
}
fn components(graph: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>) -> Vec<Vec<String>> {
    struct Tarjan<'a> {
        graph: &'a BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>,
        index: BTreeMap<String, usize>,
        low: BTreeMap<String, usize>,
        stack: Vec<String>,
        on: BTreeSet<String>,
        result: Vec<Vec<String>>,
    }
    fn visit(t: &mut Tarjan<'_>, v: &str) {
        let index = t.index.len();
        t.index.insert(v.into(), index);
        t.low.insert(v.into(), index);
        t.stack.push(v.into());
        t.on.insert(v.into());
        for w in &t.graph[v] {
            if !t.graph.contains_key(w) {
                continue;
            }
            if !t.index.contains_key(w) {
                visit(t, w);
                t.low.insert(v.into(), t.low[v].min(t.low[w]));
            } else if t.on.contains(w) {
                t.low.insert(v.into(), t.low[v].min(t.index[w]));
            }
        }
        if t.low[v] == t.index[v] {
            let mut comp = Vec::new();
            loop {
                let w = t.stack.pop().expect("Tarjan stack");
                t.on.remove(&w);
                comp.push(w.clone());
                if w == v {
                    break;
                }
            }
            comp.sort();
            t.result.push(comp);
        }
    }
    let mut t = Tarjan {
        graph,
        index: BTreeMap::new(),
        low: BTreeMap::new(),
        stack: Vec::new(),
        on: BTreeSet::new(),
        result: Vec::new(),
    };
    for v in graph.keys() {
        if !t.index.contains_key(v) {
            visit(&mut t, v);
        }
    }
    t.result
}
````

````rust
//! Strict JSON and RFC 8785 canonical serialization, without dependencies.
use crate::{err, Result};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Json {
    Null,
    Bool(bool),
    Number(String),
    String(String),
    Array(Vec<Json>),
    Object(BTreeMap<String, Json>),
}

impl Json {
    pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<Self> {
        let mut p = Parser {
            text,
            pos: 0,
            depth: 0,
        };
        let value = p.value()?;
        p.ws();
        if p.pos != text.len() {
            return err("§16.1", "trailing JSON input");
        }
        Ok(value)
    }
    pub fn canonical(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Self::Null => "null".into(),
            Self::Bool(b) => b.to_string(),
            Self::Number(n) => n.clone(),
            Self::String(s) => quote(s),
            Self::Array(a) => format!(
                "[{}]",
                a.iter().map(Self::canonical).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(",")
            ),
            Self::Object(o) => {
                let mut entries: Vec<_> = o.iter().collect();
                entries.sort_by(|(a, _), (b, _)| a.encode_utf16().cmp(b.encode_utf16()));
                format!(
                    "{{{}}}",
                    entries
                        .into_iter()
                        .map(|(k, v)| format!("{}:{}", quote(k), v.canonical()))
                        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                        .join(",")
                )
            }
        }
    }
    pub fn object(&self) -> Result<&BTreeMap<String, Json>> {
        if let Self::Object(o) = self {
            Ok(o)
        } else {
            err("§9.1", "expected JSON object")
        }
    }
    pub fn array(&self) -> Result<&[Json]> {
        if let Self::Array(a) = self {
            Ok(a)
        } else {
            err("§9.1", "expected JSON array")
        }
    }
    pub fn string(&self) -> Result<&str> {
        if let Self::String(s) = self {
            Ok(s)
        } else {
            err("§9.1", "expected JSON string")
        }
    }
    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Result<&Json> {
        self.object()?
            .get(key)
            .ok_or_else(|| crate::Error(format!("§9.1: missing field {key}")))
    }
    /// The canonical decimal text of a metadata integer of any size (§9.1):
    /// a JSON number iff it is at most 2^53 - 1, otherwise a decimal string.
    pub fn uint_text(&self) -> Result<&str> {
        let s = match self {
            Self::Number(s) | Self::String(s) => s,
            _ => return err("§9.1", "expected unsigned integer"),
        };
        if !crate::object::integer(s) || s.starts_with('-') {
            return err("§9.1", format!("invalid canonical unsigned integer {s}"));
        }
        let exact = s.len() < 16 || (s.len() == 16 && s.as_str() <= "9007199254740991");
        if matches!(self, Self::Number(_)) != exact {
            return err(
                "§9.1",
                format!("integer {s} must be a JSON number iff it is at most 2^53 - 1"),
            );
        }
        Ok(s)
    }
    /// Metadata integers may be JSON numbers or decimal strings (§9.1).
    pub fn uint(&self) -> Result<u128> {
        let s = self.uint_text()?;
        let value = s.parse::<u128>().map_err(|_| {
            crate::Error(format!("§9.1: integer {s} exceeds this field's u128 range"))
        })?;
        // §9.1 "Integers that may exceed 2^53 are decimal strings": a value above
        // 2^53 - 1 is a string and a smaller one a number (SPEC-QUESTIONS 17).
        let exact = value <= 9_007_199_254_740_991;
        if matches!(self, Self::Number(_)) != exact {
            return err(
                "§9.1",
                format!("integer {s} must be a JSON number iff it is at most 2^53 - 1"),
            );
        }
        Ok(value)
    }
    pub fn fields(&self, required: &[&str], optional: &[&str]) -> Result<()> {
        let obj = self.object()?;
        for key in required {
            self.get(key)?;
        }
        for key in obj.keys() {
            if !required.contains(&key.as_str()) && !optional.contains(&key.as_str()) {
                return err("§9.1", format!("unknown field {key}"));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

pub fn quote(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::from("\"");
    for c in s.chars() {
        match c {
            '"' => out.push_str("\\\""),
            '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            '\u{8}' => out.push_str("\\b"),
            '\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
            '\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            '\u{c}' => out.push_str("\\f"),
            '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            c if c < ' ' => out.push_str(&format!("\\u{:04x}", c as u32)),
            c => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out.push('"');
    out
}

fn canonical_number(raw: &str) -> Result<String> {
    let n: f64 = raw
        .parse()
        .map_err(|_| crate::Error("§16.1: invalid JSON number".into()))?;
    if !n.is_finite() {
        return err("§16.1", "non-finite JSON number");
    }
    if n == 0.0 {
        return Ok("0".into());
    }
    let negative = n < 0.0;
    let display = n.abs().to_string();
    let (mantissa, exponent) = match display.split_once('e') {
        Some((m, e)) => (m, e.parse::<i32>().expect("Rust float exponent")),
        None => (display.as_str(), 0),
    };
    let dot = mantissa.find('.').unwrap_or(mantissa.len()) as i32;
    let digits: String = mantissa.chars().filter(|c| *c != '.').collect();
    let leading = digits.bytes().take_while(|b| *b == b'0').count();
    let position = dot + exponent - leading as i32;
    let digits = digits[leading..].trim_end_matches('0');
    let mut out = if negative {
        "-".to_string()
    } else {
        String::new()
    };
    if position > 0 && position <= 21 {
        if position as usize >= digits.len() {
            out.push_str(digits);
            out.push_str(&"0".repeat(position as usize - digits.len()));
        } else {
            let (a, b) = digits.split_at(position as usize);
            out.push_str(a);
            out.push('.');
            out.push_str(b);
        }
    } else if position > -6 && position <= 0 {
        out.push_str("0.");
        out.push_str(&"0".repeat((-position) as usize));
        out.push_str(digits);
    } else {
        out.push_str(&digits[..1]);
        if digits.len() > 1 {
            out.push('.');
            out.push_str(&digits[1..]);
        }
        out.push('e');
        let e = position - 1;
        if e >= 0 {
            out.push('+');
        }
        out.push_str(&e.to_string());
    }
    Ok(out)
}

struct Parser<'a> {
    text: &'a str,
    pos: usize,
    depth: usize,
}
impl Parser<'_> {
    fn peek(&self) -> Option<u8> {
        self.text.as_bytes().get(self.pos).copied()
    }
    fn ws(&mut self) {
        while matches!(self.peek(), Some(b' ' | b'\n' | b'\r' | b'\t')) {
            self.pos += 1;
        }
    }
    fn take(&mut self, b: u8) -> bool {
        if self.peek() == Some(b) {
            self.pos += 1;
            true
        } else {
            false
        }
    }
    fn expect(&mut self, b: u8) -> Result<()> {
        if self.take(b) {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            err(
                "§16.1",
                format!("expected JSON '{}' at byte {}", b as char, self.pos),
            )
        }
    }
    fn value(&mut self) -> Result<Json> {
        self.ws();
        self.depth += 1;
        if self.depth > 256 {
            return err("§16.1", "JSON nesting exceeds 256");
        }
        let value = match self.peek() {
            Some(b'"') => Json::String(self.string()?),
            Some(b'{') => {
                self.pos += 1;
                self.ws();
                let mut o = BTreeMap::new();
                if !self.take(b'}') {
                    loop {
                        self.ws();
                        let key = self.string()?;
                        self.ws();
                        self.expect(b':')?;
                        let v = self.value()?;
                        if o.insert(key.clone(), v).is_some() {
                            return err("§16.1", format!("duplicate JSON key {key}"));
                        }
                        self.ws();
                        if self.take(b'}') {
                            break;
                        }
                        self.expect(b',')?;
                    }
                }
                Json::Object(o)
            }
            Some(b'[') => {
                self.pos += 1;
                self.ws();
                let mut a = Vec::new();
                if !self.take(b']') {
                    loop {
                        a.push(self.value()?);
                        self.ws();
                        if self.take(b']') {
                            break;
                        }
                        self.expect(b',')?;
                    }
                }
                Json::Array(a)
            }
            Some(b'-' | b'0'..=b'9') => {
                let start = self.pos;
                self.take(b'-');
                if !self.take(b'0') {
                    if !matches!(self.peek(), Some(b'1'..=b'9')) {
                        return err("§16.1", "invalid JSON integer");
                    }
                    while matches!(self.peek(), Some(b'0'..=b'9')) {
                        self.pos += 1;
                    }
                }
                if self.take(b'.') {
                    let p = self.pos;
                    while matches!(self.peek(), Some(b'0'..=b'9')) {
                        self.pos += 1;
                    }
                    if p == self.pos {
                        return err("§16.1", "empty fraction");
                    }
                }
                if self.take(b'e') || self.take(b'E') {
                    if !self.take(b'+') {
                        self.take(b'-');
                    }
                    let p = self.pos;
                    while matches!(self.peek(), Some(b'0'..=b'9')) {
                        self.pos += 1;
                    }
                    if p == self.pos {
                        return err("§16.1", "empty exponent");
                    }
                }
                Json::Number(canonical_number(&self.text[start..self.pos])?)
            }
            _ => {
                let mut found = None;
                for (s, v) in [
                    ("null", Json::Null),
                    ("true", Json::Bool(true)),
                    ("false", Json::Bool(false)),
                ] {
                    if self.text[self.pos..].starts_with(s) {
                        self.pos += s.len();
                        found = Some(v);
                        break;
                    }
                }
                found.ok_or_else(|| {
                    crate::Error(format!("§16.1: invalid JSON at byte {}", self.pos))
                })?
            }
        };
        self.depth -= 1;
        Ok(value)
    }
    fn hex4(&mut self) -> Result<u16> {
        let end = self.pos + 4;
        let s = self
            .text
            .as_bytes()
            .get(self.pos..end)
            .ok_or_else(|| crate::Error("§16.1: short Unicode escape".into()))?;
        let mut n = 0;
        for b in s {
            n = n * 16
                + match b {
                    b'0'..=b'9' => (b - b'0') as u16,
                    b'a'..=b'f' => (b - b'a' + 10) as u16,
                    b'A'..=b'F' => (b - b'A' + 10) as u16,
                    _ => return err("§16.1", "invalid Unicode escape"),
                };
        }
        self.pos = end;
        Ok(n)
    }
    fn string(&mut self) -> Result<String> {
        self.expect(b'"')?;
        let mut out = String::new();
        loop {
            match self.peek() {
                None => return err("§16.1", "unterminated JSON string"),
                Some(b'"') => {
                    self.pos += 1;
                    return Ok(out);
                }
                Some(b'\\') => {
                    self.pos += 1;
                    let b = self
                        .peek()
                        .ok_or_else(|| crate::Error("§16.1: short escape".into()))?;
                    self.pos += 1;
                    out.push(match b {
                        b'"' => '"',
                        b'\\' => '\\',
                        b'/' => '/',
                        b'b' => '\u{8}',
                        b'f' => '\u{c}',
                        b'n' => '\n',
                        b'r' => '\r',
                        b't' => '\t',
                        b'u' => {
                            let hi = self.hex4()?;
                            let n = if (0xd800..=0xdbff).contains(&hi) {
                                self.expect(b'\\')?;
                                self.expect(b'u')?;
                                let lo = self.hex4()?;
                                if !(0xdc00..=0xdfff).contains(&lo) {
                                    return err("§16.1", "invalid low surrogate");
                                }
                                0x10000 + (((hi as u32 - 0xd800) << 10) | (lo as u32 - 0xdc00))
                            } else {
                                hi as u32
                            };
                            char::from_u32(n)
                                .ok_or_else(|| crate::Error("§16.1: lone surrogate".into()))?
                        }
                        _ => return err("§16.1", "invalid JSON escape"),
                    });
                }
                Some(0..=31) => return err("§16.1", "unescaped JSON control character"),
                _ => {
                    let c = self.text[self.pos..].chars().next().expect("UTF-8 char");
                    self.pos += c.len_utf8();
                    out.push(c);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
````

````rust
impl std::fmt::Display for Error {
````

````rust
//! Symbol resolution and canonical linked objects (§9.3).
use crate::{err, identity::hex, json::Json, Error, Object, Result, SECTIONS};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

impl Object {
    pub fn link(objects: &[Object]) -> Result<Self> {
        let first = objects
            .first()
            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§9.3: no objects to link".into()))?;
        let mut result = Self {
            text: String::new(),
            ptr_width: first.ptr_width,
            metadata: BTreeMap::new(),
            functions: BTreeMap::new(),
            function_order: Vec::new(),
            data: BTreeMap::new(),
        };
        let mut definitions: BTreeMap<String, Json> = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut imports: Vec<(String, Json)> = Vec::new();
        let mut known_closures: BTreeMap<String, String> = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut old_identities = Vec::new();
        let mut certificates: Vec<Json> = Vec::new();
        for object in objects {
            object.check_hashes()?;
            if object.ptr_width != result.ptr_width {
                return err("§9.3", "pointer widths differ");
            }
            let identity = object.identity()?;
            for (name, hash) in &identity.closure_hashes {
                if let Some(hash) = hash {
                    if known_closures.get(name).is_some_and(|prior| prior != hash) {
                        return err("§9.3", format!("unequal closure definitions for @{name}"));
                    }
                    known_closures.insert(name.clone(), hash.clone());
                }
            }
            old_identities.push(identity);
            for symbol in object.symbols()?.values() {
                let name = symbol.get("name")?.string()?;
                if let Some(prior) = definitions.get(name) {
                    if prior.get("signature")? != symbol.get("signature")?
                        || prior.get("kind")? != symbol.get("kind")?
                    {
                        return err("§9.3", format!("incompatible duplicate @{name}"));
                    }
                } else {
                    definitions.insert(name.into(), symbol.clone());
                }
            }
            for (name, function) in &object.functions {
                if result
                    .functions
                    .get(name)
                    .is_some_and(|prior| prior.lines != function.lines)
                {
                    return err("§9.3", format!("conflicting function bodies for @{name}"));
                }
                result.functions.insert(name.clone(), function.clone());
            }
            for (name, bytes) in &object.data {
                if result.data.get(name).is_some_and(|prior| prior != bytes) {
                    return err("§9.3", format!("conflicting data @{name}"));
                }
                result.data.insert(name.clone(), bytes.clone());
            }
            if let Some(entries) = object.section("imports") {
                for (name, value) in entries.object()? {
                    imports.push((name.clone(), value.clone()));
                }
            }
            if let Some(c) = object.section("certificate") {
                certificates.push(c.clone());
            }
            for (section, value) in &object.metadata {
                if matches!(section.as_str(), "symbols" | "imports" | "certificate") {
                    continue;
                }
                match result.metadata.get_mut(section) {
                    None => {
                        result.metadata.insert(section.clone(), value.clone());
                    }
                    Some(prior) => merge_metadata(prior, value, section)?,
                }
            }
        }
        for (name, import) in &imports {
            let definition = definitions
                .get(name)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§9.3: unresolved import @{name}")))?;
            if import.get("signature")? != definition.get("signature")? {
                return err("§9.3", format!("import signature mismatch for @{name}"));
            }
        }
        result.function_order = result.functions.keys().cloned().collect();
        result.metadata.insert(
            "symbols".into(),
            Json::Object(
                definitions
                    .values()
                    .cloned()
                    .enumerate()
                    .map(|(i, s)| (i.to_string(), s))
                    .collect(),
            ),
        );
        // Resolution changes envelopes which used unresolved-name fingerprints.
        // Recompute the graph before rebinding any external metadata.
        let identity = result.identity()?;
        for (name, import) in &imports {
            if let Some(pin) = import.object()?.get("pinned_closure_hash") {
                if identity.closure_hashes[name].as_deref() != Some(pin.string()?) {
                    return err("§9.3", format!("pinned closure mismatch for @{name}"));
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(Json::Object(symbols)) = result.metadata.get_mut("symbols") {
            for symbol in symbols.values_mut() {
                let n = symbol.get("name")?.string()?.to_string();
                let Json::Object(fields) = symbol else {
                    return err("§9.1", "symbol entries are objects");
                };
                fields.insert(
                    "interface_hash".into(),
                    Json::String(identity.interface_hashes[&n].clone()),
                );
            }
        }
        let mut replacements = BTreeMap::new();
        for old in old_identities {
            for (name, hash) in old.interface_hashes {
                replacements.insert(hash, identity.interface_hashes[&name].clone());
            }
            for (name, hash) in old.closure_hashes {
                if let Some(hash) = hash {
                    let next = identity.closure_hashes[&name].clone().ok_or_else(|| {
                        Error(format!("§9.3: @{name} is still unresolved after linking"))
                    })?;
                    replacements.insert(hash, next);
                }
            }
        }
        let old_schedule = result
            .metadata
            .get("schedule")
            .map(|s| crate::sha256_hex(s.canonical().as_bytes()));
        for section in ["schedule", "coverage"] {
            if let Some(value) = result.metadata.get_mut(section) {
                replace_hashes(value, &replacements)?;
            }
        }
        // A rebound schedule has a new schedule_hash (§9.2): rebind references.
        if let (Some(old), Some(new)) = (
            old_schedule,
            result
                .metadata
                .get("schedule")
                .map(|s| crate::sha256_hex(s.canonical().as_bytes())),
        ) {
            replacements.insert(old, new);
        }
        for c in &mut certificates {
            replace_hashes(c, &replacements)?;
        }
        if !certificates.is_empty() {
            result
                .metadata
                .insert("certificate".into(), compose_certificates(&certificates)?);
        }
        result.text = result.render()?;
        let object_hash = result.identity()?.object_hash;
        if let Some(Json::Object(cert)) = result.metadata.get_mut("certificate") {
            if let Some(Json::Object(bindings)) = cert.get_mut("bindings") {
                bindings.insert("object_hash".into(), Json::String(object_hash));
            }
        }
        result.text = result.render()?;
        let linked = Self::parse(&result.text)?;
        linked.check_hashes()?;
        Ok(linked)
    }
    pub(crate) fn render(&self) -> Result<String> {
        let mut text=format!("bennett-object isa=0.8 object=0.8 launch=0.8 sched=0.8 cert=0.8 coverage=0.8 target=0.8 ptr_width={}\n",self.ptr_width);
        for section in SECTIONS {
            let body = match section {
                "functions" => {
                    if self.functions.is_empty() {
                        continue;
                    }
                    self.function_order
                        .iter()
                        .map(|n| self.functions[n].lines.join("\n"))
                        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                        .join("\n")
                }
                "data" => {
                    if self.data.is_empty() {
                        continue;
                    }
                    self.data
                        .iter()
                        .map(|(n, b)| format!("{n} {}", hex(b)))
                        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                        .join("\n")
                }
                _ => match self.section(section) {
                    Some(value) => value.canonical(),
                    None => continue,
                },
            };
            text.push_str(&format!("\nsection {section}\n{body}\n"));
        }
        Ok(text)
    }
}
fn merge_metadata(destination: &mut Json, source: &Json, path: &str) -> Result<()> {
    if destination == source {
        return Ok(());
    }
    if path == "coverage.entries" {
        let (Json::Array(a), Json::Array(b)) = (destination, source) else {
            return err("§9.3", "coverage entries must be arrays");
        };
        for e in b {
            if !a.contains(e) {
                a.push(e.clone());
            }
        }
        return Ok(());
    }
    let recursive = matches!(
        path,
        "layout"
            | "layout.globals"
            | "layout.interface_regions"
            | "devices"
            | "devices.models"
            | "devices.services"
            | "coverage"
    ) || path.starts_with("layout.interface_regions.")
        && path.split('.').count() == 3;
    if !recursive {
        return err("§9.3", format!("conflicting metadata at {path}"));
    }
    let Json::Object(target) = destination else {
        return err("§9.3", format!("metadata object required at {path}"));
    };
    for (key, value) in source.object()? {
        if let Some(prior) = target.get_mut(key) {
            merge_metadata(prior, value, &format!("{path}.{key}"))?;
        } else {
            target.insert(key.clone(), value.clone());
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
fn replace_hashes(value: &mut Json, replacements: &BTreeMap<String, String>) -> Result<()> {
    match value {
        Json::String(s) => {
            if let Some(next) = replacements.get(s) {
                *s = next.clone();
            }
        }
        Json::Array(values) => {
            for v in values {
                replace_hashes(v, replacements)?;
            }
        }
        Json::Object(fields) => {
            let previous = std::mem::take(fields);
            for (key, mut value) in previous {
                replace_hashes(&mut value, replacements)?;
                // Composite keys "<hash>:<variant>:<controls>" rebind their hash.
                let key = match replacements.get(&key) {
                    Some(next) => next.clone(),
                    None => match key.split_once(':') {
                        Some((h, rest)) if replacements.contains_key(h) => {
                            format!("{}:{rest}", replacements[h])
                        }
                        _ => key,
                    },
                };
                if let Some(prior) = fields.insert(key.clone(), value.clone()) {
                    if prior != value {
                        return err(
                            "§9.3",
                            format!("two metadata keys rebind to {key} with different values"),
                        );
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    Ok(())
}
/// §9.3 linking performs certificate composition (§12.3): the region records
/// of every certificate are united (one record per closure hash, equal where
/// they meet), multiplicities are united (equal where they meet), and
/// epsilon_total is recomputed by the sum over multiplicities from the local
/// error bounds, operator norms converting to diamond by x2 (SPEC-QUESTIONS 22).
/// The composed certificate binds to the first certificate's root region.
fn compose_certificates(certificates: &[Json]) -> Result<Json> {
    let first = &certificates[0];
    for c in &certificates[1..] {
        if c.get("versions")? != first.get("versions")? {
            return err("§9.3", "certificates disagree on versions");
        }
        for key in ["dialect_mapping_version", "target_hash"] {
            if c.get("bindings")?.get(key)? != first.get("bindings")?.get(key)? {
                return err("§9.3", format!("certificates bind different {key} values"));
            }
        }
        if c.get("composition")?.get("method")? != first.get("composition")?.get("method")? {
            return err("§12.3", "certificates use different composition methods");
        }
    }
    let mut regions = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut multiplicities = BTreeMap::new();
    for c in certificates {
        for (k, r) in c.get("regions")?.object()? {
            if regions.get(k).is_some_and(|prior: &Json| prior != r) {
                return err(
                    "§9.3",
                    format!("conflicting certificate records for region {k}"),
                );
            }
            regions.insert(k.clone(), r.clone());
        }
        for (k, n) in c.get("composition")?.get("multiplicities")?.object()? {
            if multiplicities.get(k).is_some_and(|prior: &Json| prior != n) {
                return err("§12.3", format!("conflicting multiplicities for {k}"));
            }
            multiplicities.insert(k.clone(), n.clone());
        }
    }
    let local = |region: &str, key: &str| -> Result<crate::exact::Decimal> {
        let Some(r) = regions.get(region) else {
            return err(
                "§12.3",
                format!("multiplicity names region {region} with no record"),
            );
        };
        let Some(e) = r.get("error")?.object()?.get(key) else {
            return Ok(crate::exact::Decimal::zero());
        };
        let l = e.get("local")?.object()?;
        let text = |v: &Json| -> Result<String> {
            Ok(match v {
                Json::Number(s) | Json::String(s) => s.clone(),
                _ => return err("§12.3", "error bound must be a decimal"),
            })
        };
        if let Some(d) = l.get("diamond") {
            return crate::exact::Decimal::parse(&text(d)?)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error("§12.3: invalid diamond bound".into()));
        }
        if let Some(o) = l.get("operator_norm") {
            return Ok(crate::exact::Decimal::parse(&text(o)?)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error("§12.3: invalid operator_norm bound".into()))?
                .mul_int(2));
        }
        Ok(crate::exact::Decimal::zero())
    };
    let mut total = crate::exact::Decimal::zero();
    for (k, n) in &multiplicities {
        let (region, key) = k
            .split_once(':')
            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§12.3: malformed multiplicity key".into()))?;
        total = total.add(&local(region, key)?.mul_int(n.uint()?));
    }
    let root = first.get("bindings")?.get("closure_hash")?.string()?;
    if let Some(r) = regions.get(root) {
        for key in r.get("error")?.object()?.keys() {
            total = total.add(&local(root, key)?);
        }
    }
    let mut out = first.clone();
    let Json::Object(fields) = &mut out else {
        return err("§12", "certificate must be an object");
    };
    fields.insert("regions".into(), Json::Object(regions));
    let total_text = total.to_text();
    let total_json = if total_text.contains('.') || total_text.len() > 15 {
        Json::String(total_text)
    } else {
        Json::Number(total_text)
    };
    fields.insert(
        "composition".into(),
        Json::Object(BTreeMap::from([
            (
                "epsilon_total".into(),
                Json::Object(BTreeMap::from([("diamond".into(), total_json)])),
            ),
            (
                "method".into(),
                first.get("composition")?.get("method")?.clone(),
            ),
            ("multiplicities".into(), Json::Object(multiplicities)),
        ])),
    );
    Ok(out)
}
````
