//! §14.1 sequential reference interpreter. It uses independent dynamic
//! activations rather than the reversible machine's global location file and
//! frame-slot exchanges, so the two engines check each other (deliverable 4).
//!
//! Every location, pseudo-location and cell is a `BitVector` of its declared
//! width: §3.3 bounds only `iN` (1..=128), never `wire[N]` or `reg[N]`.
//! Addresses are `reg[ptr_width]` values, ptr_width <= 128 (SPEC-QUESTIONS 14),
//! and memory/allocator arithmetic is exact (no wrap, §3.3, §3.7).
use crate::{
    err,
    object::{integer, is_binop, is_div, list},
    BitVector, Error, Function, Instruction, Object, Result, Type,
};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Budget {
    pub steps: u64,
    pub heap: u128,
    pub stack: u128,
    pub depth: u128,
}
impl Budget {
    pub fn steps(steps: u64) -> Self {
        Self {
            steps,
            heap: 0,
            stack: 0,
            depth: 0,
        }
    }
}
/// A classical argument: iN (N <= 128) and ptr (ptr_width <= 128) values,
/// f64 angles and budget tokens (§3.3).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum Argument {
    Bits(u128),
    Float(f64),
    Token(Budget),
}
/// Small-integer convenience form of an oracle input. Each value must fit its
/// declared bundle; wider interfaces use `OracleVectorInput` directly.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct OracleInput {
    pub ins: Vec<u128>,
    pub args: Vec<Argument>,
    pub regions: BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>,
}
impl OracleInput {
    pub fn bits(ins: &[u128]) -> Self {
        Self {
            ins: ins.into(),
            ..Self::default()
        }
    }
}
/// Small-integer convenience form of F_B. Conversion fails loudly when the
/// payload or code does not fit u128; `OracleVectorOutcome` is exact.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct OracleOutcome {
    pub payload: u128,
    pub code: u128,
    pub steps: u64,
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct OracleVectorInput {
    pub ins: Vec<BitVector>,
    pub args: Vec<Argument>,
    pub regions: BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>,
}
impl OracleVectorInput {
    pub fn from_input(object: &Object, name: &str, input: &OracleInput) -> Result<Self> {
        let f = object
            .functions
            .get(name)
            .filter(|f| f.kind == "oracle")
            .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§5.2: unknown oracle @{name}")))?;
        if input.ins.len() != f.params[0].len() {
            return err("§5.1", "oracle input count mismatch");
        }
        let ins = input
            .ins
            .iter()
            .zip(&f.params[0])
            .map(|(v, p)| {
                let width = p.ty.bits(object.ptr_width)?;
                if width < 128 && *v >> width != 0 {
                    return err("§3.3", "input value exceeds declared width");
                }
                BitVector::from_u128(width, *v)
            })
            .collect::<Result<_>>()?;
        Ok(Self {
            ins,
            args: input.args.clone(),
            regions: input.regions.clone(),
        })
    }
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct OracleVectorOutcome {
    pub payload: BitVector,
    pub code: BitVector,
    pub steps: u64,
}
impl OracleVectorOutcome {
    pub fn narrow(&self) -> Result<OracleOutcome> {
        let narrow = |v: &BitVector| {
            v.to_u128().map_err(|_| {
                Error("§3.3: value exceeds the u128 convenience API; use the vector API".into())
            })
        };
        Ok(OracleOutcome {
            payload: narrow(&self.payload)?,
            code: narrow(&self.code)?,
            steps: self.steps,
        })
    }
}

/// One `alloctab` entry (§7.2).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct Allocation {
    pub base: u128,
    pub size: u128,
    pub live: bool,
    pub pinned: bool,
}
/// Byte memory and allocation table, shared by the lifted engines and CC/R.
/// Addresses are below 2^ptr_width <= 2^128; every sum is checked, never wrapped.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub(crate) struct Memory {
    pub bytes: BTreeMap<u128, u8>,
    pub allocations: Vec<Allocation>,
    pub heap_base: u128,
    pub heap_used: u128,
    /// 2^A_tab, or None when 2^A_tab >= 2^128 (no reachable table index).
    pub table_capacity: Option<u128>,
    pub addresses: BTreeMap<String, u128>,
}
pub(crate) fn power_of_two(exponent: u128) -> Option<u128> {
    (exponent < 128).then(|| 1u128 << exponent)
}
impl Memory {
    pub fn initial(
        object: &Object,
        oracle: &Function,
        regions: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>,
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        let expected = if oracle.kind == "oracle" {
            oracle.params[3].len()
        } else {
            0
        };
        if regions.len() != expected {
            return err("§5.1", "interface region count mismatch");
        }
        let Some(layout) = object.section("layout") else {
            return Ok(Self::default());
        };
        let mut m = Self {
            heap_base: layout.get("heap_base")?.uint()?,
            table_capacity: power_of_two(layout.get("A_tab")?.uint()?),
            ..Self::default()
        };
        // Pre-entries in layout order: globals, then this oracle's regions (§3.7).
        for (n, g) in layout.get("globals")?.object()? {
            let base = g.get("base")?.uint()?;
            let size = g.get("size")?.uint()?;
            m.addresses.insert(n.clone(), base);
            m.allocations.push(Allocation {
                base,
                size,
                live: true,
                pinned: true,
            });
            let image = object
                .data
                .get(n)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§9.2: global {n} has no data image")))?;
            for (i, b) in image.iter().enumerate() {
                m.set_byte(offset(base, i)?, *b);
            }
        }
        if oracle.kind == "oracle" && !oracle.params[3].is_empty() {
            let mapping = layout.get("interface_regions")?.get(&oracle.name)?;
            for (n, r) in mapping.object()? {
                let p = oracle.params[3]
                    .iter()
                    .find(|p| p.name == *n)
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§7.2: layout maps unknown region {n}")))?;
                let Type::Region(a, _) = p.ty else {
                    return err("§5.1", "mem slot requires region type");
                };
                let base = r.get("base")?.uint()?;
                let size = power_of_two(a as u128)
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error("§7.2: interface region exceeds 2^H".into()))?;
                let bytes = regions
                    .get(n)
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§5.1: missing interface region {n}")))?;
                if bytes.len() as u128 != size {
                    return err("§5.1", format!("interface region {n} has wrong byte count"));
                }
                m.addresses.insert(n.clone(), base);
                m.allocations.push(Allocation {
                    base,
                    size,
                    live: true,
                    pinned: true,
                });
                for (i, b) in bytes.iter().enumerate() {
                    m.set_byte(offset(base, i)?, *b);
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(m)
    }
    /// inrange(p, n) of §4.2: some live entry i < atop has base_i <= p and
    /// p + n <= base_i + size_i, computed without wrap.
    pub fn valid(&self, p: u128, n: u128) -> bool {
        self.allocations
            .iter()
            .any(|e| e.live && e.base <= p && n <= e.size && p - e.base <= e.size - n)
    }
    /// inrange for a length that may exceed 128 bits: such a length exceeds
    /// every entry size (sizes are below 2^128), so the range is never valid.
    pub fn valid_vector(&self, p: u128, n: &BitVector) -> bool {
        n.to_u128().is_ok_and(|n| self.valid(p, n))
    }
    pub fn byte(&self, p: u128) -> u8 {
        self.bytes.get(&p).copied().unwrap_or(0)
    }
    pub fn set_byte(&mut self, p: u128, b: u8) {
        if b == 0 {
            self.bytes.remove(&p);
        } else {
            self.bytes.insert(p, b);
        }
    }
    /// N/8 bytes little-endian at p; the caller has established inrange.
    pub fn load(&self, p: u128, width: u64) -> Result<BitVector> {
        let count = (width / 8) as usize;
        let bytes = (0..count)
            .map(|i| Ok(self.byte(offset(p, i)?)))
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
        BitVector::from_le_bytes(width as usize, &bytes)
    }
    pub fn store(&mut self, p: u128, value: &BitVector) -> Result<()> {
        if !value.width().is_multiple_of(8) {
            return err("§3.3", "store width must be a byte multiple");
        }
        for (i, b) in value.to_le_bytes().into_iter().enumerate() {
            self.set_byte(offset(p, i)?, b);
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    pub fn load_u128(&self, p: u128, width: u64) -> Result<u128> {
        self.load(p, width)?.to_u128()
    }
    pub fn store_u128(&mut self, p: u128, width: u64, v: u128) -> Result<()> {
        let value = BitVector::from_u128(width as usize, v)?;
        self.store(p, &value)
    }
    /// The lift.alloc / alloc flag: heap_used + max(n,1) > heap_limit, or the
    /// table is full (atop >= 2^A_tab). The sum is exact (§3.7).
    pub fn allocation_fails(&self, n: u128, heap_limit: u128) -> bool {
        self.heap_used
            .checked_add(n.max(1))
            .is_none_or(|total| total > heap_limit)
            || self
                .table_capacity
                .is_some_and(|cap| self.allocations.len() as u128 >= cap)
    }
    pub fn allocate(&mut self, n: u128) -> Result<u128> {
        let base = self
            .heap_base
            .checked_add(self.heap_used)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§7.1: heap bump exceeds address space".into()))?;
        self.allocations.push(Allocation {
            base,
            size: n,
            live: true,
            pinned: false,
        });
        self.heap_used += n.max(1);
        Ok(base)
    }
    /// The lift.free row of §4.2: flag = no i < atop with base_i = p, live and
    /// unpinned; otherwise live_i ^= match_i for EVERY i < atop with base_i = p
    /// (SPEC-QUESTIONS 16). Returns false when the row faults.
    pub fn lifted_free(&mut self, p: u128) -> bool {
        if !self
            .allocations
            .iter()
            .any(|e| e.base == p && e.live && !e.pinned)
        {
            return false;
        }
        for e in &mut self.allocations {
            if e.base == p {
                e.live ^= true;
            }
        }
        true
    }
}
pub(crate) fn offset(base: u128, i: usize) -> Result<u128> {
    base.checked_add(i as u128)
        .ok_or_else(|| Error("§7.2: byte address exceeds 2^128".into()))
}

pub(crate) struct Program<'a> {
    pub rows: Vec<(&'a Function, &'a Instruction)>,
    pub labels: BTreeMap<(String, String), usize>,
    pub ranges: BTreeMap<String, (usize, usize)>,
    pub halt: usize,
}
impl<'a> Program<'a> {
    /// §3.6 index space: the oracle's blocks in text order, then its lproc
    /// closure ordered by closure hash (multi-member SCCs: SPEC-QUESTIONS 7).
    pub fn new(object: &'a Object, root: &str) -> Result<Self> {
        object.ensure_linked()?;
        let oracle = object
            .functions
            .get(root)
            .filter(|f| f.kind == "oracle")
            .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§5.2: unknown oracle @{root}")))?;
        let mut reachable = BTreeSet::new();
        let mut pending = vec![root.to_string()];
        while let Some(n) = pending.pop() {
            let function = object.functions.get(&n).ok_or_else(|| {
                Error(format!(
                    "§9.3: oracle closure has unresolved lproc @{n}; link before execution"
                ))
            })?;
            for i in function.instructions().filter(|i| i.op == "lift.call") {
                let n = i.operands[0].trim_start_matches('@').to_string();
                if reachable.insert(n.clone()) {
                    pending.push(n);
                }
            }
        }
        let mut closure: Vec<_> = reachable.into_iter().collect();
        if !closure.is_empty() {
            let identity = object.identity()?;
            let mut keys = BTreeMap::new();
            for n in &closure {
                let key = if identity.scc_members[n].len() > 1 {
                    identity.scc_hashes[n].clone()
                } else {
                    identity.closure_hashes[n]
                        .clone()
                        .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§9.3: lproc @{n} has no closure hash")))?
                };
                keys.insert(n.clone(), key);
            }
            closure.sort_by(|a, b| keys[a].cmp(&keys[b]).then(a.cmp(b)));
        }
        let order = std::iter::once(&oracle.name).chain(closure.iter());
        let mut rows = Vec::new();
        let mut labels = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut ranges = BTreeMap::new();
        for n in order {
            let f = &object.functions[n];
            let start = rows.len();
            for b in &f.blocks {
                labels.insert((n.clone(), b.name.clone()), rows.len());
                for i in &b.instructions {
                    rows.push((f, i));
                }
            }
            ranges.insert(n.clone(), (start, rows.len()));
        }
        let halt = rows.len();
        Ok(Self {
            rows,
            labels,
            ranges,
            halt,
        })
    }
    pub fn label(&self, f: &str, label: &str) -> Result<usize> {
        self.labels
            .get(&(f.into(), label.trim_start_matches('^').into()))
            .copied()
            .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§3.6: unknown label {label} in @{f}")))
    }
}

/// Width of a readable operand of `f` (§3.7 name resolution).
pub(crate) fn operand_width(object: &Object, f: &Function, n: &str) -> Result<u64> {
    let pseudo: Vec<_> = if f.kind == "oracle" {
        f.params[0].iter().chain(&f.params[4]).collect()
    } else {
        Vec::new()
    };
    f.locations()
        .into_iter()
        .chain(pseudo)
        .find(|p| p.name == n)
        .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§3.7: unknown operand {n} in @{}", f.name)))?
        .ty
        .width(object.ptr_width)
}
/// A length operand: an INT literal in [0, 2^ptr_width) or a location.
pub(crate) fn literal_u128(s: &str) -> Result<u128> {
    s.parse::<u128>()
        .map_err(|_| Error(format!("§3.3: literal {s} exceeds 2^ptr_width")))
}

struct Activation {
    function: String,
    values: BTreeMap<String, BitVector>,
    ret_pc: usize,
    destination: String,
}
impl Activation {
    fn new(f: &Function, ptr: u16) -> Result<Self> {
        Ok(Self {
            function: f.name.clone(),
            values: f
                .locations()
                .iter()
                .map(|p| Ok((p.name.clone(), BitVector::zero(p.ty.bits(ptr)?)?)))
                .collect::<Result<_>>()?,
            ret_pc: 0,
            destination: String::new(),
        })
    }
    fn read(&self, n: &str) -> Result<BitVector> {
        self.values.get(n).cloned().ok_or_else(|| {
            Error(format!(
                "§3.7: unreadable operand {n} in @{}",
                self.function
            ))
        })
    }
    fn write(&mut self, f: &Function, n: &str, value: BitVector, ptr: u16) -> Result<()> {
        let p = f
            .locations()
            .into_iter()
            .find(|p| p.name == n)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§3.7: unwritable location {n}")))?;
        if value.width() != p.ty.bits(ptr)? {
            return err(
                "§3.3",
                format!("internal width mismatch writing {n}: lifted writes are never resized"),
            );
        }
        self.values.insert(n.into(), value);
        Ok(())
    }
}
fn token(arguments: &BTreeMap<String, Argument>, n: &str) -> Result<Budget> {
    match arguments.get(n) {
        Some(Argument::Token(b)) => Ok(*b),
        _ => err(
            "§4.2",
            format!("tk operand {n} is not a token argument of the oracle"),
        ),
    }
}
/// Bytes of a mapped interface region passed by name to a nested region call.
pub(crate) fn region_bytes(memory: &Memory, n: &str, address_width: u64) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    let base = *memory
        .addresses
        .get(n)
        .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§4.2: mem operand {n} is not a mapped region")))?;
    let len = power_of_two(address_width as u128)
        .and_then(|n| usize::try_from(n).ok())
        .ok_or_else(|| Error("host limit: region exceeds host address space".into()))?;
    (0..len)
        .map(|i| Ok(memory.byte(offset(base, i)?)))
        .collect()
}

impl Object {
    pub fn validate_budget(&self, b: Budget) -> Result<()> {
        if let Some(l) = self.section("layout") {
            let s = l.get("S_cells")?.uint()?;
            if b.heap > l.get("heap_limit_max")?.uint()?
                || power_of_two(s).is_some_and(|cells| b.stack > cells)
            {
                return err("§5.4", "budget heap/stack limit exceeds the layout");
            }
            // depth_limit < 2^Dc - 1 holds for the derived Dc = ceil(log2(d + 2))
            // whenever d + 2 is representable (§3.7, §5.4).
            if b.depth.checked_add(2).is_none() {
                return err("§5.4", "depth limit exceeds the counter range");
            }
        } else if b.heap != 0 || b.stack != 0 || b.depth != 0 {
            return err(
                "§5.4",
                "memoryless budgets require zero heap, stack and depth",
            );
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    pub fn default_budget(&self, steps: u64) -> Result<Budget> {
        if let Some(l) = self.section("layout") {
            Ok(Budget {
                steps,
                heap: l.get("heap_limit_max")?.uint()?,
                stack: power_of_two(l.get("S_cells")?.uint()?).unwrap_or(u128::MAX),
                depth: 64,
            })
        } else {
            Ok(Budget::steps(steps))
        }
    }
    /// F_B on small-integer inputs: a checked adapter over `run_oracle_vectors`.
    pub fn run_oracle(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        input: &OracleInput,
        budget: Budget,
    ) -> Result<OracleOutcome> {
        let vector = OracleVectorInput::from_input(self, name, input)?;
        self.run_oracle_vectors(name, &vector, budget)?.narrow()
    }
    /// The §14.1 reference interpreter: defines F_B and the budget unit.
    pub fn run_oracle_vectors(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        input: &OracleVectorInput,
        budget: Budget,
    ) -> Result<OracleVectorOutcome> {
        self.validate_budget(budget)?;
        self.check_schedule_matches_for_run(name, budget, &input.args)?;
        let program = Program::new(self, name)?;
        let root = &self.functions[name];
        if input.ins.len() != root.params[0].len() || input.args.len() != root.params[4].len() {
            return err("§5.1", "oracle interface argument count mismatch");
        }
        let mut activation = Activation::new(root, self.ptr_width)?;
        for (p, v) in root.params[0].iter().zip(&input.ins) {
            if v.width() != p.ty.bits(self.ptr_width)? {
                return err("§3.3", "input value width differs from its bundle");
            }
            activation.values.insert(p.name.clone(), v.clone());
        }
        let arguments = self.bind_arguments(root, &input.args)?;
        for (p, v) in root.params[4].iter().zip(&input.args) {
            if let (Type::Int(_) | Type::Ptr, Argument::Bits(v)) = (&p.ty, v) {
                activation.values.insert(
                    p.name.clone(),
                    BitVector::from_u128(p.ty.bits(self.ptr_width)?, *v)?,
                );
            }
        }
        let mut memory = Memory::initial(self, root, &input.regions)?;
        let mut stack: Vec<Activation> = Vec::new();
        let mut sp = 0u128;
        let mut pc = 0;
        let mut steps = 0;
        let target_width = root.params[1][0].ty.bits(self.ptr_width)?;
        let fault_width = root.params[2][0].ty.bits(self.ptr_width)?;
        let mut result = BitVector::zero(target_width)?;
        macro_rules! fault {
            ($code:expr) => {
                return Ok(OracleVectorOutcome {
                    payload: BitVector::zero(target_width)?,
                    code: $code,
                    steps,
                })
            };
        }
        let code = |n: u128| BitVector::from_u128(fault_width, n);
        while steps < budget.steps {
            if pc == program.halt {
                return err("§3.6", "only lift.retval reaches HALT with success");
            }
            let (f, i) = program.rows[pc];
            if activation.function != f.name {
                return err("§3.7", "control escaped its active function");
            }
            steps += 1;
            let mut next = pc + 1;
            let op = i.op.as_str();
            let a = &i.operands;
            let rd = |n: &str| activation.read(n);
            let mut output = None;
            if let Some(n) = op.strip_prefix("lift.const.i") {
                let w = crate::object::host_count(n, "const width")? as usize;
                output = Some(BitVector::parse_decimal(w, &a[0])?);
            } else if let Some(bin) = op.strip_prefix("lift.").filter(|s| is_binop(s)) {
                output = Some(rd(&a[0])?.binary(bin, &rd(&a[1])?)?);
            } else if let Some(div) = op.strip_prefix("lift.").filter(|s| is_div(s)) {
                let (x, y) = (rd(&a[0])?, rd(&a[1])?);
                match x.division_fault(&y, div.starts_with('s'))? {
                    Some(c) => fault!(code(c)?),
                    None => output = Some(x.binary(div, &y)?),
                }
            } else if let Some(pred) = op.strip_prefix("lift.icmp.") {
                output = Some(BitVector::from_u128(
                    1,
                    u128::from(rd(&a[0])?.compare(pred, &rd(&a[1])?)?),
                )?);
            } else if let Some((cast, target)) = op
                .strip_prefix("lift.")
                .and_then(|s| s.split_once(".i"))
                .filter(|(c, _)| ["zext", "sext", "trunc"].contains(c))
            {
                let w = crate::object::host_count(target, "cast width")? as usize;
                output = Some(rd(&a[0])?.resize(w, cast == "sext")?);
            } else if let Some(n) = op.strip_prefix("lift.load.i") {
                let w = crate::object::host_count(n, "load width")?;
                let p = rd(&a[0])?.to_u128()?;
                if !memory.valid(p, (w / 8) as u128) {
                    fault!(code(7)?);
                }
                output = Some(memory.load(p, w)?);
            } else if op.starts_with("lift.store.i") {
                let p = rd(&a[0])?.to_u128()?;
                let v = rd(&a[1])?;
                if !memory.valid(p, (v.width() / 8) as u128) {
                    fault!(code(7)?);
                }
                memory.store(p, &v)?;
            } else {
                match op {
                    "lift.mov" => output = Some(rd(&a[0])?),
                    "lift.select" => {
                        output = Some(rd(if !rd(&a[0])?.is_zero() { &a[1] } else { &a[2] })?)
                    }
                    "lift.parmov" => {
                        let values = list(&a[0])?
                            .iter()
                            .map(|s| rd(s))
                            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
                        for (d, v) in i.lhs.iter().zip(values) {
                            activation.write(f, d, v, self.ptr_width)?;
                        }
                    }
                    "lift.label" => {
                        let w = operand_width(self, f, &i.lhs[0])? as usize;
                        output = Some(BitVector::from_u128(
                            w,
                            program.label(&f.name, &a[0])? as u128,
                        )?)
                    }
                    "lift.addr" => {
                        output = Some(BitVector::from_u128(
                            self.ptr_width as usize,
                            *memory
                                .addresses
                                .get(a[0].trim_start_matches('@'))
                                .ok_or_else(|| Error("§4.2: address not mapped".into()))?,
                        )?);
                    }
                    "lift.boundscheck" => {
                        let p = rd(&a[0])?.to_u128()?;
                        let ok = if integer(&a[1]) {
                            memory.valid(p, literal_u128(&a[1])?)
                        } else {
                            memory.valid_vector(p, &rd(&a[1])?)
                        };
                        if !ok {
                            fault!(code(7)?);
                        }
                    }
                    "lift.alloc" => {
                        // A length of 2^128 or more always exceeds heap_limit < 2^128.
                        let n = if integer(&a[0]) {
                            Some(literal_u128(&a[0])?)
                        } else {
                            rd(&a[0])?.to_u128().ok()
                        };
                        match n {
                            Some(n) if !memory.allocation_fails(n, budget.heap) => {
                                output = Some(BitVector::from_u128(
                                    self.ptr_width as usize,
                                    memory.allocate(n)?,
                                )?);
                            }
                            _ => fault!(code(2)?),
                        }
                    }
                    "lift.free" => {
                        let p = rd(&a[0])?.to_u128()?;
                        if !memory.lifted_free(p) {
                            fault!(code(7)?);
                        }
                    }
                    "lift.faultif" => {
                        if !rd(&a[0])?.is_zero() {
                            fault!(BitVector::parse_unsigned_exact(fault_width, &a[1])?);
                        }
                    }
                    "fault" => fault!(BitVector::parse_unsigned_exact(fault_width, &a[0])?),
                    "qjump" => next = program.label(&f.name, &a[0])?,
                    "qbranch" => {
                        next = program
                            .label(&f.name, if !rd(&a[0])?.is_zero() { &a[1] } else { &a[2] })?
                    }
                    "qjumpr" => {
                        let (start, end) = program.ranges[&f.name];
                        match rd(&a[0])?.to_u128() {
                            Ok(t) if t >= start as u128 && t < end as u128 => next = t as usize,
                            _ => fault!(code(4)?),
                        }
                    }
                    "lift.call" => {
                        let callee = &self.functions[a[0].trim_start_matches('@')];
                        let cells = callee.frame_cells() as u128;
                        if stack.len() as u128 + 1 > budget.depth
                            || sp.checked_add(cells).is_none_or(|p| p > budget.stack)
                        {
                            fault!(code(3)?);
                        }
                        let values = list(&a[1])?
                            .iter()
                            .map(|s| rd(s))
                            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
                        let mut called = Activation::new(callee, self.ptr_width)?;
                        called.ret_pc = pc + 1;
                        called.destination = i.lhs[0].clone();
                        for (p, v) in callee.params[0].iter().zip(values) {
                            called.write(callee, &p.name, v, self.ptr_width)?;
                        }
                        sp += cells;
                        stack.push(activation);
                        activation = called;
                        next = program.ranges[&callee.name].0;
                    }
                    "lift.ret" => {
                        let Some(caller) = stack.pop() else {
                            fault!(code(4)?);
                        };
                        let v = rd(&a[0])?;
                        let ret = activation.ret_pc;
                        let dest = activation.destination.clone();
                        activation = caller;
                        let caller = &self.functions[&activation.function];
                        activation.write(caller, &dest, v, self.ptr_width)?;
                        next = ret;
                    }
                    "lift.retval" => {
                        result = result.binary("xor", &rd(&a[0])?)?;
                        return Ok(OracleVectorOutcome {
                            payload: result,
                            code: BitVector::zero(fault_width)?,
                            steps,
                        });
                    }
                    "lift.oracle_call" | "lift.oracle_uncall" => {
                        let callee = &self.functions[a[0].trim_start_matches('@')];
                        let tk = token(&arguments, &a[1])?;
                        let mut child = OracleVectorInput {
                            ins: list(&a[2])?
                                .iter()
                                .map(|s| rd(s))
                                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?,
                            ..Default::default()
                        };
                        for (p, n) in callee.params[3].iter().zip(list(&a[5])?) {
                            let Type::Region(aw, _) = p.ty else {
                                return err("§5.1", "mem slot requires region type");
                            };
                            child
                                .regions
                                .insert(p.name.clone(), region_bytes(&memory, &n, aw)?);
                        }
                        for n in list(&a[6])? {
                            child.args.push(self.forward_argument(&arguments, &n)?);
                        }
                        // The matched inverse is the identical permutation (§4.2, §5.5).
                        let r = self.run_oracle_vectors(&callee.name, &child, tk)?;
                        let tgt = rd(&a[3])?.binary("xor", &r.payload)?;
                        let fr = rd(&a[4])?.binary("xor", &r.code)?;
                        activation.write(f, &a[3], tgt, self.ptr_width)?;
                        activation.write(f, &a[4], fr, self.ptr_width)?;
                    }
                    "lift.perm_call" => {
                        let callee = &self.functions[a[0].trim_start_matches('@')];
                        let destinations = list(&a[1])?;
                        let mutable = destinations
                            .iter()
                            .map(|n| rd(n))
                            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
                        let inputs = list(&a[2])?
                            .iter()
                            .map(|n| rd(n))
                            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
                        let mut regions = BTreeMap::new();
                        for (p, n) in callee.params[2].iter().zip(list(&a[3])?) {
                            let Type::Region(aw, _) = p.ty else {
                                return err("§5.1", "mem slot requires region type");
                            };
                            regions.insert(p.name.clone(), region_bytes(&memory, &n, aw)?);
                        }
                        let args = list(&a[4])?
                            .iter()
                            .map(|n| self.forward_argument(&arguments, n))
                            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
                        let values = self.permutation_action_vectors(
                            &callee.name,
                            &mutable,
                            &inputs,
                            &regions,
                            &args,
                            false,
                        )?;
                        for (n, v) in destinations.iter().zip(values) {
                            activation.write(f, n, v, self.ptr_width)?;
                        }
                    }
                    _ => return err("§4.8", format!("unknown lifted row {op}")),
                }
            }
            if let Some(v) = output {
                activation.write(f, &i.lhs[0], v, self.ptr_width)?;
            }
            pc = next;
        }
        Ok(OracleVectorOutcome {
            payload: BitVector::zero(target_width)?,
            code: code(1)?,
            steps,
        })
    }
    /// Validates and indexes an oracle's classical arguments (§3.3, §4.2).
    pub(crate) fn bind_arguments(
        &self,
        f: &Function,
        args: &[Argument],
    ) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Argument>> {
        let mut out = BTreeMap::new();
        for (p, v) in f.params[4].iter().zip(args) {
            check_argument(self, &p.ty, v)?;
            out.insert(p.name.clone(), v.clone());
        }
        Ok(out)
    }
    /// A classical argument forwarded to a nested region call: one of the
    /// calling oracle's own classical arguments (validate_region_call).
    fn forward_argument(
        &self,
        arguments: &BTreeMap<String, Argument>,
        n: &str,
    ) -> Result<Argument> {
        arguments
            .get(n)
            .cloned()
            .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§4.2: classical operand {n} is not an argument")))
    }
}
/// §3.3 classical argument typing, shared by oracles, actions and CC region calls.
pub(crate) fn check_argument(object: &Object, ty: &Type, v: &Argument) -> Result<()> {
    let fits = |w: u64, n: u128| w >= 128 || n >> w == 0;
    match (ty, v) {
        (Type::Int(w), Argument::Bits(n)) if fits(*w as u64, *n) => Ok(()),
        (Type::Ptr, Argument::Bits(n)) if fits(object.ptr_width as u64, *n) => Ok(()),
        (Type::F64, Argument::Float(x)) if x.is_finite() => Ok(()),
        (Type::Token, Argument::Token(b)) => object.validate_budget(*b),
        _ => err(
            "§3.3",
            format!("classical argument does not have type {}", ty.text()),
        ),
    }
}

//! §14.2 state semantics: a sparse basis-permutation fast path and a state
//! vector, each carrying an exact shadow (src/exact.rs) beside the binary64
//! amplitudes. Born selection uses refined exact-shadow enclosures; every
//! cleanliness and basis-value decision uses the exact amplitudes, so a
//! component is zero iff it is exactly zero (no tolerance, council B15).
//! The vector has no fixed wire limit: it is bounded only by host memory,
//! and an allocation the host cannot provide fails loudly.
use crate::{
    err,
    exact::{self, Amplitude},
    Argument, Error, Result,
};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
pub type Wire = u64;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Default)]
pub struct Complex {
    pub re: f64,
    pub im: f64,
}
impl Complex {
    pub const ZERO: Self = Self { re: 0.0, im: 0.0 };
    pub const ONE: Self = Self { re: 1.0, im: 0.0 };
    pub fn new(re: f64, im: f64) -> Self {
        Self { re, im }
    }
    fn phase(a: f64) -> Self {
        Self::new(a.cos(), a.sin())
    }
    fn scale(self, s: f64) -> Self {
        Self::new(self.re * s, self.im * s)
    }
}
impl std::ops::Add for Complex {
    type Output = Self;
    fn add(self, b: Self) -> Self {
        Self::new(self.re + b.re, self.im + b.im)
    }
}
impl std::ops::Mul for Complex {
    type Output = Self;
    fn mul(self, b: Self) -> Self {
        Self::new(
            self.re * b.re - self.im * b.im,
            self.re * b.im + self.im * b.re,
        )
    }
}
/// A basis index over arbitrarily many wires: little-endian words, no
/// trailing zero word (so allocating |0> wires leaves every key unchanged).
type Key = Vec<u64>;
fn key_bit(k: &Key, p: usize) -> bool {
    k.get(p / 64).is_some_and(|w| w >> (p % 64) & 1 == 1)
}
fn key_with(mut k: Key, p: usize, v: bool) -> Key {
    if k.len() <= p / 64 {
        if !v {
            return k;
        }
        k.resize(p / 64 + 1, 0);
    }
    if v {
        k[p / 64] |= 1 << (p % 64);
    } else {
        k[p / 64] &= !(1 << (p % 64));
    }
    while k.last() == Some(&0) {
        k.pop();
    }
    k
}
fn key_of(bits: &[bool]) -> Key {
    let mut k = Vec::new();
    for (p, b) in bits.iter().enumerate() {
        if *b {
            k = key_with(k, p, true);
        }
    }
    k
}
fn key_bits(k: &Key, n: usize) -> Vec<bool> {
    (0..n).map(|p| key_bit(k, p)).collect()
}
/// Drops the removed positions (release, measurement).
fn compress(k: &Key, remove: &[bool]) -> Key {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut next = 0;
    for (p, removed) in remove.iter().enumerate() {
        if !removed {
            if key_bit(k, p) {
                out = key_with(out, next, true);
            }
            next += 1;
        }
    }
    out
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
enum State {
    Basis {
        bits: Vec<bool>,
        phase: Complex,
        exact: Amplitude,
    },
    /// Sparse superposition: exactly the components whose exact amplitude is
    /// nonzero, each with its binary64 value for Born probabilities.
    Vector {
        amplitudes: BTreeMap<Key, (Complex, Amplitude)>,
    },
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) struct Content(Vec<Wire>, Vec<(Key, Amplitude)>);
pub(crate) type BorrowObservation = (Vec<Wire>, Vec<bool>, Content);
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct BorrowAudit {
    entry: BTreeMap<Wire, bool>,
    returns: Vec<BorrowObservation>,
    live: BTreeSet<Wire>,
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct QuantumState {
    ids: Vec<Wire>,
    next: Wire,
    state: State,
    borrow_audit: Option<BorrowAudit>,
    // Exact shadows of conditional states retain their projection scale for
    // support and Born ratios. Both amplitude observers emit the normalized
    // conditional vector; arbitrary set_state_vector input keeps its own scale.
    projected: bool,
}
impl PartialEq for QuantumState {
    /// Exact equality of the states (binary64 values are not compared).
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        if self.ids != other.ids || self.next != other.next || self.projected != other.projected {
            return false;
        }
        let support = |s: &State| -> BTreeMap<Key, Amplitude> {
            match s {
                State::Basis { bits, exact, .. } => BTreeMap::from([(key_of(bits), exact.clone())]),
                State::Vector { amplitudes } => amplitudes
                    .iter()
                    .map(|(k, (_, e))| (k.clone(), e.clone()))
                    .collect(),
            }
        };
        support(&self.state) == support(&other.state)
    }
}
impl Default for QuantumState {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct MeasurementBranch {
    pub probability: f64,
    pub bits: Vec<bool>,
    pub state: QuantumState,
    pub(crate) weight: Amplitude,
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct QuantumBindings {
    pub bundles: BTreeMap<String, Vec<Wire>>,
    pub regions: BTreeMap<String, QuantumRegion>,
    pub args: BTreeMap<String, Argument>,
    pub borrowed: Vec<Vec<Wire>>,
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct QuantumRegion {
    pub address_width: u64,
    pub cell_width: u64,
    pub cells: Vec<Vec<Wire>>,
}
fn insert(map: &mut BTreeMap<Key, (Complex, Amplitude)>, k: Key, f: Complex, e: Amplitude) {
    if e.is_zero() {
        map.remove(&k);
    } else {
        map.insert(k, (f, e));
    }
}

impl QuantumState {
    pub(crate) fn next_wire_id(&self) -> u64 {
        self.next
    }
    pub(crate) fn restore_next_wire_id(&mut self, next: u64) -> Result<()> {
        if self.ids.iter().any(|id| *id >= next) {
            return err("§7.4", "cannot restore wire counter over live wires");
        }
        self.next = next;
        Ok(())
    }
    /// Re-inserts clean released wires at their former positions (§7.4 reversal).
    pub(crate) fn restore_clean(&mut self, positions: &[(usize, Wire)]) -> Result<()> {
        let n = self
            .ids
            .len()
            .checked_add(positions.len())
            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§7.4: wire count overflow".into()))?;
        let mut removed = BTreeMap::new();
        for (pos, wire) in positions {
            if *pos >= n || removed.insert(*pos, *wire).is_some() || self.ids.contains(wire) {
                return err("§7.4", "invalid released-wire history");
            }
        }
        let mut ids = Vec::with_capacity(n);
        let mut source = self.ids.iter();
        for i in 0..n {
            ids.push(match removed.get(&i) {
                Some(w) => *w,
                None => *source
                    .next()
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error("§7.4: restored wire count".into()))?,
            });
        }
        let expand = |k: &Key| {
            let mut out = Vec::new();
            let mut bit = 0;
            for pos in 0..n {
                if !removed.contains_key(&pos) {
                    if key_bit(k, bit) {
                        out = key_with(out, pos, true);
                    }
                    bit += 1;
                }
            }
            out
        };
        match &mut self.state {
            State::Basis { bits, .. } => {
                let mut old = bits.iter();
                let mut next = Vec::with_capacity(n);
                for i in 0..n {
                    next.push(if removed.contains_key(&i) {
                        false
                    } else {
                        *old.next()
                            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§7.4: basis width".into()))?
                    });
                }
                *bits = next;
            }
            State::Vector { amplitudes } => {
                *amplitudes = std::mem::take(amplitudes)
                    .into_iter()
                    .map(|(k, a)| (expand(&k), a))
                    .collect();
            }
        }
        self.ids = ids;
        Ok(())
    }
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            borrow_audit: None,
            projected: false,
            ids: Vec::new(),
            next: 0,
            state: State::Basis {
                bits: Vec::new(),
                phase: Complex::ONE,
                exact: Amplitude::one(),
            },
        }
    }
    /// The exact state without its wire-identity counter (loop periods).
    pub(crate) fn content(&self) -> Content {
        Content(
            self.ids.clone(),
            match &self.state {
                State::Basis { bits, exact, .. } => vec![(key_of(bits), exact.clone())],
                State::Vector { amplitudes } => amplitudes
                    .iter()
                    .map(|(k, (_, e))| (k.clone(), e.clone()))
                    .collect(),
            },
        )
    }
    pub(crate) fn start_borrow_audit(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
        let entry = self
            .ids
            .iter()
            .map(|w| Ok((*w, self.read_basis(&[*w])? != 0)))
            .collect::<Result<_>>()?;
        self.borrow_audit = Some(BorrowAudit {
            entry,
            returns: Vec::new(),
            live: BTreeSet::new(),
        });
        Ok(())
    }
    pub(crate) fn auditing_borrows(&self) -> bool {
        self.borrow_audit.is_some()
    }
    pub(crate) fn audit_borrow(&mut self, wires: &[Wire]) {
        if let Some(audit) = &mut self.borrow_audit {
            audit.live.extend(wires);
        }
    }
    pub(crate) fn audit_frame(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
        if let Some(audit) = &self.borrow_audit {
            let wires: Vec<_> = audit.live.iter().copied().collect();
            if !wires.is_empty() {
                self.audit_borrow_boundary(&wires)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    pub(crate) fn audit_return(&mut self, wires: &[Wire]) -> Result<()> {
        self.audit_borrow_boundary(wires)?;
        if let Some(audit) = &mut self.borrow_audit {
            for w in wires {
                audit.live.remove(w);
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    fn audit_borrow_boundary(&mut self, wires: &[Wire]) -> Result<()> {
        let Some(audit) = &self.borrow_audit else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        for w in wires {
            if audit.entry.get(w).copied()
                != Some(
                    self.read_basis(&[*w]).map_err(|_| {
                        Error("§5.6: qreturn/frame borrowed entry is not restored".into())
                    })? != 0,
                )
            {
                return err("§5.6", "qreturn/frame does not restore its borrowed entry");
            }
        }
        let rest = audit
            .entry
            .iter()
            .filter(|(w, _)| !wires.contains(w))
            .map(|(_, v)| *v)
            .collect();
        let remove: Vec<_> = self.ids.iter().map(|w| wires.contains(w)).collect();
        let content = self.content();
        let output = Content(
            content
                .0
                .into_iter()
                .filter(|w| !wires.contains(w))
                .collect(),
            content
                .1
                .into_iter()
                .map(|(k, e)| (compress(&k, &remove), e))
                .collect(),
        );
        if let Some(audit) = &mut self.borrow_audit {
            audit.returns.push((wires.to_vec(), rest, output));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    pub(crate) fn take_borrow_audit(&mut self) -> Vec<BorrowObservation> {
        self.borrow_audit
            .take()
            .map_or_else(Vec::new, |a| a.returns)
    }
    pub fn wire_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.ids.len()
    }
    pub fn is_basis(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self.state, State::Basis { .. })
    }
    pub fn allocate(&mut self, n: usize) -> Result<Vec<Wire>> {
        let end = self
            .next
            .checked_add(n as u64)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§4.3: wire identity overflow".into()))?;
        let total = self
            .ids
            .len()
            .checked_add(n)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§4.3: wire count overflow".into()))?;
        // New wires are |0> at the high positions: sparse keys are unchanged.
        if let State::Basis { bits, .. } = &mut self.state {
            bits.try_reserve(n)
                .map_err(|e| Error(format!("host limit: wire allocation failed ({e})")))?;
            bits.resize(total, false);
        }
        let wires: Vec<_> = (self.next..end).collect();
        self.next = end;
        self.ids.extend(&wires);
        Ok(wires)
    }
    fn positions(&self, wires: &[Wire]) -> Result<Vec<usize>> {
        let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
        wires
            .iter()
            .map(|w| {
                if !seen.insert(w) {
                    return err("§3.3", "duplicate wire operand");
                }
                self.ids
                    .iter()
                    .position(|n| n == w)
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§3.3: dead or unknown wire {w}")))
            })
            .collect()
    }
    /// Dense binary64 amplitudes in allocation order (bundles little-endian).
    /// Materialising 2^n entries is a host-memory operation and fails loudly.
    pub fn amplitudes(&self) -> Result<Vec<Complex>> {
        let n = self.ids.len();
        if n >= usize::BITS as usize - 1 {
            return err(
                "host limit",
                format!("2^{n} dense amplitudes exceed the host address space"),
            );
        }
        let len = 1usize << n;
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        out.try_reserve_exact(len).map_err(|e| {
            Error(format!(
                "host limit: cannot allocate {len} amplitudes ({e})"
            ))
        })?;
        out.resize(len, Complex::ZERO);
        let dense = |k: &Key| {
            k.iter()
                .enumerate()
                .fold(0usize, |n, (i, w)| n | ((*w as usize) << (64 * i)))
        };
        match &self.state {
            State::Basis { bits, phase, .. } => out[dense(&key_of(bits))] = *phase,
            State::Vector { amplitudes } => {
                for (k, (a, _)) in amplitudes {
                    out[dense(k)] = *a;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(out)
    }
    /// Replaces the state over the currently allocated wires with the
    /// given sparse superposition (bit i is wire position i, allocation
    /// order). Every binary64 amplitude is held exactly as its dyadic
    /// value in the shadow. An empty list, a zero amplitude, a duplicate
    /// component or a wrong bit count is an error (§14.2); normalisation
    /// is the caller's to provide and is never imposed silently.
    pub fn set_state_vector(&mut self, components: &[(Vec<bool>, Complex)]) -> Result<()> {
        if components.is_empty() {
            return err("§14.2", "a state vector needs at least one component");
        }
        let mut amplitudes: BTreeMap<Key, (Complex, Amplitude)> = BTreeMap::new();
        for (bits, amp) in components {
            if bits.len() != self.ids.len() {
                return err(
                    "§14.2",
                    format!(
                        "state component has {} bits for {} wires",
                        bits.len(),
                        self.ids.len()
                    ),
                );
            }
            let exact = exact::amplitude_from_f64(amp.re, amp.im)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error("§14.2: non-finite amplitude".into()))?;
            if exact.is_zero() {
                return err("§14.2", "state component with zero amplitude");
            }
            if amplitudes.insert(key_of(bits), (*amp, exact)).is_some() {
                return err("§14.2", "duplicate state component");
            }
        }
        self.projected = false;
        if amplitudes.len() == 1 {
            let (bits, amp) = &components[0];
            let (_, exact) = amplitudes.into_values().next().expect("one component");
            self.state = State::Basis {
                bits: bits.clone(),
                phase: *amp,
                exact,
            };
        } else {
            self.state = State::Vector { amplitudes };
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    /// Exact support as (basis bits, approximate amplitude), for diagnostics.
    /// After projection the amplitudes describe the normalized conditional
    /// state, including after further gates. Unprojected caller-supplied vectors
    /// retain their input scale. Internal exact shadows keep their raw scale;
    /// Born weights use norm ratios rather than these binary64 diagnostics.
    pub fn exact_support(&self) -> Vec<(Vec<bool>, (f64, f64))> {
        let n = self.ids.len();
        let entries: Vec<_> = match &self.state {
            State::Basis { bits, exact, .. } => vec![(bits.clone(), exact.clone())],
            State::Vector { amplitudes } => amplitudes
                .iter()
                .map(|(k, (_, e))| (key_bits(k, n), e.clone()))
                .collect(),
        };
        let values = if self.projected {
            exact::normalized(&entries.iter().map(|(_, e)| e.clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>())
        } else {
            entries.iter().map(|(_, e)| e.approximate()).collect()
        };
        entries
            .into_iter()
            .zip(values)
            .map(|((bits, _), value)| (bits, value))
            .collect()
    }
    /// The value of `wires` when it is the same on every component of the
    /// exact state; otherwise an error.
    pub fn read_basis(&self, wires: &[Wire]) -> Result<u128> {
        if wires.len() > 128 {
            return err(
                "§3.3",
                "integer bundle read exceeds 128 bits; read bit by bit",
            );
        }
        let positions = self.positions(wires)?;
        let read = |bit: &dyn Fn(usize) -> bool| {
            positions
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .fold(0u128, |n, (j, p)| n | ((bit(*p) as u128) << j))
        };
        match &self.state {
            State::Basis { bits, .. } => Ok(read(&|p| bits[p])),
            State::Vector { amplitudes } => {
                let values: BTreeSet<u128> = amplitudes
                    .keys()
                    .map(|k| read(&|p| key_bit(k, p)))
                    .collect();
                match values.len() {
                    1 => Ok(*values.iter().next().expect("one value")),
                    _ => err("§14.2", "wires are not in a basis state"),
                }
            }
        }
    }
    /// §4.3 qfree / §3.3 qreg.free: release wires that are |0> on every
    /// component, decided exactly; on failure nothing changes.
    pub fn release(&mut self, wires: &[Wire]) -> Result<()> {
        let positions = self.positions(wires)?;
        let mut remove = vec![false; self.ids.len()];
        for p in &positions {
            remove[*p] = true;
        }
        match &mut self.state {
            State::Basis { bits, .. } => {
                if positions.iter().any(|p| bits[*p]) {
                    return err("§4.3", "E_QREG_NOT_CLEAN: released wire is one");
                }
                let mut index = 0;
                bits.retain(|_| {
                    let keep = !remove[index];
                    index += 1;
                    keep
                });
            }
            State::Vector { amplitudes } => {
                if let Some((k, (_, e))) = amplitudes
                    .iter()
                    .find(|(k, _)| positions.iter().any(|p| key_bit(k, *p)))
                {
                    return err(
                        "§4.3",
                        format!(
                            "E_QREG_NOT_CLEAN: released factor has an exactly nonzero component {:?} (about {:?})",
                            key_bits(k, remove.len()),
                            e.approximate()
                        ),
                    );
                }
                *amplitudes = std::mem::take(amplitudes)
                    .into_iter()
                    .map(|(k, a)| (compress(&k, &remove), a))
                    .collect();
            }
        }
        let mut index = 0;
        self.ids.retain(|_| {
            let keep = !remove[index];
            index += 1;
            keep
        });
        Ok(())
    }
    pub fn gate(
        &mut self,
        op: &str,
        wires: &[Wire],
        angle: Option<f64>,
        predicate: &[Wire],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        self.controlled_gate(
            op,
            wires,
            angle,
            &predicate.iter().map(|w| (*w, true)).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        )
    }
    pub(crate) fn controlled_gate(
        &mut self,
        op: &str,
        wires: &[Wire],
        angle: Option<f64>,
        predicate: &[(Wire, bool)],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let positions = self.positions(wires)?;
        let own = match op {
            "cx" => 1,
            "ccx" => 2,
            "mcx" => wires.len().saturating_sub(1),
            _ => 0,
        };
        let expected = match op {
            "x" | "h" | "s" | "sdg" | "t" | "tdg" | "rx" | "ry" | "rz" => 1,
            "cx" | "swap" | "cz" => 2,
            "ccx" => 3,
            "mcx" if !wires.is_empty() => wires.len(),
            _ => return err("§4.4", format!("unknown gate {op}")),
        };
        if wires.len() != expected {
            return err("§4.8", "wrong gate arity");
        }
        if matches!(op, "rx" | "ry" | "rz") && angle.is_none_or(|a| !a.is_finite()) {
            return err("§4.4", "rotation needs a finite angle");
        }
        let mut controls: Vec<_> = positions[..own].iter().map(|p| (*p, true)).collect();
        let targets = positions[own..].to_vec();
        for (w, value) in predicate {
            let p = self.positions(&[*w])?[0];
            if targets.contains(&p) {
                return err("§3.3", "effective control aliases target");
            }
            if !controls.contains(&(p, *value)) {
                controls.push((p, *value));
            }
        }
        let permutation = matches!(op, "x" | "cx" | "ccx" | "mcx" | "swap");
        let diagonal = matches!(op, "s" | "sdg" | "t" | "tdg" | "cz" | "rz");
        let f64_matrix = |op: &str| -> Result<[Complex; 4]> {
            let zero = Complex::ZERO;
            let one = Complex::ONE;
            let h = std::f64::consts::FRAC_1_SQRT_2;
            Ok(match op {
                "x" | "cx" | "ccx" | "mcx" => [zero, one, one, zero],
                "h" => [one.scale(h), one.scale(h), one.scale(h), one.scale(-h)],
                "s" => [one, zero, zero, Complex::new(0.0, 1.0)],
                "sdg" => [one, zero, zero, Complex::new(0.0, -1.0)],
                "t" => [one, zero, zero, Complex::phase(std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_4)],
                "tdg" => [
                    one,
                    zero,
                    zero,
                    Complex::phase(-std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_4),
                ],
                "cz" => [one, zero, zero, one.scale(-1.0)],
                _ => {
                    let a = angle.ok_or_else(|| Error("§4.4: rotation angle".into()))? / 2.0;
                    match op {
                        "rx" => [
                            one.scale(a.cos()),
                            Complex::new(0.0, -a.sin()),
                            Complex::new(0.0, -a.sin()),
                            one.scale(a.cos()),
                        ],
                        "ry" => [
                            one.scale(a.cos()),
                            one.scale(-a.sin()),
                            one.scale(a.sin()),
                            one.scale(a.cos()),
                        ],
                        _ => [Complex::phase(-a), zero, zero, Complex::phase(a)],
                    }
                }
            })
        };
        let exact_matrix = || -> Result<[Amplitude; 4]> {
            if op == "cz" {
                return Ok([
                    Amplitude::one(),
                    Amplitude::zero(),
                    Amplitude::zero(),
                    exact::minus_one(),
                ]);
            }
            exact::gate_matrix(op, angle)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§4.4: no exact entries for {op}")))
        };
        if let State::Basis { bits, phase, exact } = &mut self.state {
            if !controls.iter().all(|(p, v)| bits[*p] == *v) {
                return Ok(());
            }
            if permutation {
                if op == "swap" {
                    bits.swap(targets[0], targets[1]);
                } else {
                    bits[targets[0]] ^= true;
                }
                return Ok(());
            }
            if diagonal {
                // cz acts as a phase on its first target when the second is 1.
                let on = if op == "cz" { bits[targets[1]] } else { true };
                if on {
                    let bit = bits[targets[0]];
                    let (f, e) = (f64_matrix(op)?, exact_matrix()?);
                    let j = if bit { 3 } else { 0 };
                    *phase = *phase * f[j];
                    *exact = exact.mul(&e[j]);
                }
                return Ok(());
            }
            let key = key_of(bits);
            self.state = State::Vector {
                amplitudes: BTreeMap::from([(key, (*phase, exact.clone()))]),
            };
        }
        let State::Vector { amplitudes } = &mut self.state else {
            return err("§14.2", "state vector materialisation failed");
        };
        let enabled = |k: &Key| controls.iter().all(|(p, v)| key_bit(k, *p) == *v);
        if op == "swap" {
            let (a, b) = (targets[0], targets[1]);
            let moved: Vec<Key> = amplitudes
                .keys()
                .filter(|k| enabled(k) && key_bit(k, a) != key_bit(k, b))
                .cloned()
                .collect();
            let values: Vec<_> = moved
                .iter()
                .map(|k| (k.clone(), amplitudes.remove(k).expect("listed key")))
                .collect();
            for (k, v) in values {
                let flipped = key_with(key_with(k.clone(), a, !key_bit(&k, a)), b, !key_bit(&k, b));
                amplitudes.insert(flipped, v);
            }
            return Ok(());
        }
        if op == "cz" {
            for (k, (f, e)) in amplitudes.iter_mut() {
                if enabled(k) && key_bit(k, targets[0]) && key_bit(k, targets[1]) {
                    *f = f.scale(-1.0);
                    *e = e.mul(&exact::minus_one());
                }
            }
            return Ok(());
        }
        let (fm, em) = (f64_matrix(op)?, exact_matrix()?);
        let t = targets[0];
        let lows: BTreeSet<Key> = amplitudes
            .keys()
            .filter(|k| enabled(k))
            .map(|k| key_with(k.clone(), t, false))
            .collect();
        for low in lows {
            let high = key_with(low.clone(), t, true);
            let (fa, ea) = amplitudes
                .remove(&low)
                .unwrap_or((Complex::ZERO, Amplitude::zero()));
            let (fb, eb) = amplitudes
                .remove(&high)
                .unwrap_or((Complex::ZERO, Amplitude::zero()));
            insert(
                amplitudes,
                low,
                fm[0] * fa + fm[1] * fb,
                em[0].mul(&ea).add(&em[1].mul(&eb)),
            );
            insert(
                amplitudes,
                high,
                fm[2] * fa + fm[3] * fb,
                em[2].mul(&ea).add(&em[3].mul(&eb)),
            );
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    pub fn measurement_branches(&self, wires: &[Wire]) -> Result<Vec<MeasurementBranch>> {
        let positions = self.positions(wires)?;
        let mut remove = vec![false; self.ids.len()];
        for p in &positions {
            remove[*p] = true;
        }
        let kept_ids: Vec<Wire> = self
            .ids
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter_map(|(p, w)| (!remove[p]).then_some(*w))
            .collect();
        if let State::Basis { bits, exact, .. } = &self.state {
            let mut state = self.clone();
            let result = positions.iter().map(|p| bits[*p]).collect();
            let kept: Vec<_> = bits
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .filter_map(|(p, b)| (!remove[p]).then_some(*b))
                .collect();
            state.ids = kept_ids;
            state.projected = true;
            let (re, im) = exact::normalized(std::slice::from_ref(exact))[0];
            state.state = State::Basis {
                bits: kept,
                phase: Complex::new(re, im),
                exact: exact.clone(),
            };
            return Ok(vec![MeasurementBranch {
                probability: 1.0,
                weight: Amplitude::one(),
                bits: result,
                state,
            }]);
        }
        let State::Vector { amplitudes } = &self.state else {
            return err("§14.2", "unreachable state form");
        };
        let outcome = |k: &Key| {
            positions
                .iter()
                .map(|p| key_bit(k, *p))
                .collect::<Vec<bool>>()
        };
        // Outcomes with an exactly nonzero component; the exact projection is
        // left unnormalised (cleanliness and basis values are scale-invariant).
        let mut groups: BTreeMap<Vec<bool>, BTreeMap<Key, (Complex, Amplitude)>> = BTreeMap::new();
        for (k, a) in amplitudes {
            groups
                .entry(outcome(k))
                .or_default()
                .insert(compress(k, &remove), a.clone());
        }
        let weights: Vec<_> = groups
            .values()
            .map(|g| {
                g.values()
                    .fold(Amplitude::zero(), |s, (_, e)| s.add(&e.norm_squared()))
            })
            .collect();
        let total = weights.iter().fold(Amplitude::zero(), |s, w| s.add(w));
        let mut branches = Vec::new();
        for ((bits, mut group), weight) in groups.into_iter().zip(weights) {
            let probability = exact::probability(&weight, &total);
            let projected: Vec<_> = group.values().map(|(_, e)| e.clone()).collect();
            for ((f, _), (re, im)) in group.values_mut().zip(exact::normalized(&projected)) {
                *f = Complex::new(re, im);
            }
            let mut state = self.clone();
            state.ids = kept_ids.clone();
            state.projected = true;
            state.state = State::Vector { amplitudes: group };
            branches.push(MeasurementBranch {
                probability,
                weight,
                bits,
                state,
            });
        }
        Ok(branches)
    }
    /// Applies a basis permutation (oracle constructions, §5.2). On a sparse
    /// superposition the map must be injective on the support.
    pub(crate) fn permute(
        &mut self,
        mut permutation: impl FnMut(&[bool]) -> Result<Vec<bool>>,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let n = self.ids.len();
        match &mut self.state {
            State::Basis { bits, .. } => {
                let next = permutation(bits)?;
                if next.len() != bits.len() {
                    return err("§14.2", "permutation changes wire count");
                }
                *bits = next;
            }
            State::Vector { amplitudes } => {
                let mut out = BTreeMap::new();
                for (k, a) in std::mem::take(amplitudes) {
                    let mapped = permutation(&key_bits(&k, n))?;
                    if mapped.len() != n {
                        return err("§14.2", "permutation changes wire count");
                    }
                    if out.insert(key_of(&mapped), a).is_some() {
                        return err("§5.3", "action mapping is not a permutation");
                    }
                }
                *amplitudes = out;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    pub(crate) fn position(&self, w: Wire) -> Result<usize> {
        Ok(self.positions(&[w])?[0])
    }
}

//! CC quantum-register ownership and the reversible handle transitions of §3.3.
use crate::{err, quantum::Wire, Error, QuantumState, Result};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Status {
    Live,
    Viewed,
    Consumed,
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Handle {
    wires: Vec<Wire>,
    status: Status,
    parent: Option<u64>,
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct QuantumRegisters {
    pub(crate) state: QuantumState,
    handles: BTreeMap<u64, Handle>,
    next: u64,
}
impl Default for QuantumRegisters {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
enum KernelUndo {
    None,
    Allocation(Vec<Wire>),
    Release(Vec<(usize, Wire)>),
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct RegisterUndo {
    handles: Vec<(u64, Option<Handle>)>,
    next: u64,
    wire_next: u64,
    kernel: KernelUndo,
}

impl QuantumRegisters {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            state: QuantumState::new(),
            handles: BTreeMap::new(),
            next: 1,
        }
    }
    pub fn quantum_state(&self) -> &QuantumState {
        &self.state
    }
    pub fn prepare(&mut self, id: u64, bits: &[bool]) -> Result<()> {
        let wires = self.ordinary(id)?.wires.clone();
        if wires.len() != bits.len() {
            return err("§10", "E_ARG: preparation width mismatch");
        }
        let mut check = self.state.clone();
        check.release(&wires)?;
        for (wire, bit) in wires.iter().zip(bits) {
            if *bit {
                self.state.gate("x", &[*wire], None, &[])?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    pub fn bundle(&self, id: u64) -> Result<&[Wire]> {
        let h = self
            .handles
            .get(&id)
            .filter(|h| h.status == Status::Live)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§3.3: qreg {id} is not live")))?;
        Ok(&h.wires)
    }
    fn ordinary(&self, id: u64) -> Result<&Handle> {
        self.bundle(id)?;
        let h = &self.handles[&id];
        if h.parent.is_some() {
            return err(
                "§3.3",
                "a qreg view may only be used by its one region call",
            );
        }
        Ok(h)
    }
    pub(crate) fn idle_bundle(&self, id: u64) -> Result<&[Wire]> {
        Ok(&self.ordinary(id)?.wires)
    }
    fn set_status(&mut self, id: u64, status: Status) -> Result<()> {
        self.handles
            .get_mut(&id)
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                Error(format!(
                    "§3.3: missing qreg handle {id} during ownership transition"
                ))
            })?
            .status = status;
        Ok(())
    }
    fn record(&self, ids: &[u64]) -> RegisterUndo {
        RegisterUndo {
            handles: ids
                .iter()
                .map(|id| (*id, self.handles.get(id).cloned()))
                .collect(),
            next: self.next,
            wire_next: self.state.next_wire_id(),
            kernel: KernelUndo::None,
        }
    }
    fn create(&mut self, wires: Vec<Wire>, parent: Option<u64>) -> Result<u64> {
        let id = self.next;
        let next = id
            .checked_add(1)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§3.3: qreg identity overflow".into()))?;
        self.handles.insert(
            id,
            Handle {
                wires,
                status: Status::Live,
                parent,
            },
        );
        self.next = next;
        Ok(id)
    }
    pub fn allocate(&mut self, n: usize) -> Result<u64> {
        Ok(self.allocate_recorded(n)?.0)
    }
    pub(crate) fn allocate_recorded(&mut self, n: usize) -> Result<(u64, RegisterUndo)> {
        let mut undo = self.record(&[self.next]);
        let wires = self.state.allocate(n)?;
        undo.kernel = KernelUndo::Allocation(wires.clone());
        let id = self.create(wires, None)?;
        Ok((id, undo))
    }
    pub fn free(&mut self, id: u64) -> Result<()> {
        self.free_recorded(id).map(|_| ())
    }
    pub(crate) fn free_recorded(&mut self, id: u64) -> Result<RegisterUndo> {
        let wires = self.ordinary(id)?.wires.clone();
        let mut undo = self.record(&[id]);
        let positions = wires
            .iter()
            .map(|w| Ok((self.state.position(*w)?, *w)))
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
        self.state.release(&wires)?;
        self.set_status(id, Status::Consumed)?;
        undo.kernel = KernelUndo::Release(positions);
        Ok(undo)
    }
    pub fn slice(&mut self, id: u64, lo: usize, len: usize) -> Result<u64> {
        Ok(self.slice_recorded(id, lo, len)?.0)
    }
    pub(crate) fn slice_recorded(
        &mut self,
        id: u64,
        lo: usize,
        len: usize,
    ) -> Result<(u64, RegisterUndo)> {
        let h = self.ordinary(id)?;
        let end = lo
            .checked_add(len)
            .filter(|end| *end <= h.wires.len())
            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§3.3: qreg slice out of bounds".into()))?;
        let wires = h.wires[lo..end].to_vec();
        let undo = self.record(&[id, self.next]);
        self.set_status(id, Status::Viewed)?;
        let view = self.create(wires, Some(id))?;
        Ok((view, undo))
    }
    pub fn concat(&mut self, a: u64, b: u64) -> Result<u64> {
        Ok(self.concat_recorded(a, b)?.0)
    }
    pub(crate) fn concat_recorded(&mut self, a: u64, b: u64) -> Result<(u64, RegisterUndo)> {
        if a == b {
            return err("§3.3", "qreg concat operands alias");
        }
        let mut wires = self.ordinary(a)?.wires.clone();
        wires.extend(&self.ordinary(b)?.wires);
        if wires.iter().collect::<BTreeSet<_>>().len() != wires.len() {
            return err("§3.3", "qreg concat wires overlap");
        }
        let undo = self.record(&[a, b, self.next]);
        self.set_status(a, Status::Consumed)?;
        self.set_status(b, Status::Consumed)?;
        let id = self.create(wires, None)?;
        Ok((id, undo))
    }
    pub fn complete_call(&mut self, ids: &[u64]) -> Result<()> {
        self.complete_call_recorded(ids).map(|_| ())
    }
    pub(crate) fn complete_call_recorded(&mut self, ids: &[u64]) -> Result<RegisterUndo> {
        let mut affected = Vec::new();
        let mut wires = BTreeSet::new();
        for id in ids {
            for wire in self.bundle(*id)? {
                if !wires.insert(*wire) {
                    return err("§3.3", "region interface qregs overlap");
                }
            }
            affected.push(*id);
            if let Some(parent) = self.handles[id].parent {
                affected.push(parent);
            }
        }
        let undo = self.record(&affected);
        for id in ids {
            if let Some(parent) = self.handles[id].parent {
                self.set_status(*id, Status::Consumed)?;
                self.set_status(parent, Status::Live)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(undo)
    }
    pub(crate) fn measure(&mut self, id: u64, draw: f64) -> Result<Vec<bool>> {
        if !(0.0..1.0).contains(&draw) {
            return err("§14.2", "measurement draw outside [0,1)");
        }
        let wires = self.ordinary(id)?.wires.clone();
        let branches = self.state.measurement_branches(&wires)?;
        let total = branches
            .iter()
            .fold(crate::exact::Amplitude::zero(), |s, b| s.add(&b.weight));
        let negative_threshold = total.times_f64(draw)?.times_f64(-1.0)?;
        let mut cumulative = crate::exact::Amplitude::zero();
        let mut selected = None;
        for branch in branches {
            cumulative = cumulative.add(&branch.weight);
            if cumulative.add(&negative_threshold).real_sign() == std::cmp::Ordering::Greater {
                selected = Some(branch);
                break;
            }
        }
        let branch =
            selected.ok_or_else(|| Error("§14.2: measurement has no nonzero outcome".into()))?;
        self.state = branch.state;
        self.set_status(id, Status::Consumed)?;
        Ok(branch.bits)
    }
    pub(crate) fn undo(&mut self, undo: RegisterUndo) -> Result<()> {
        match undo.kernel {
            KernelUndo::None => {}
            KernelUndo::Allocation(wires) => self.state.release(&wires)?,
            KernelUndo::Release(positions) => self.state.restore_clean(&positions)?,
        };
        for (id, prior) in undo.handles {
            if let Some(prior) = prior {
                self.handles.insert(id, prior);
            } else {
                self.handles.remove(&id);
            }
        }
        self.next = undo.next;
        self.state.restore_next_wire_id(undo.wire_next)?;
        Ok(())
    }
}
