````rust
#[test]
fn r2_multi_input_invocation_keys_preserve_tuple_boundaries() {
    let si = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[8,8],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":8,"tier":"q"}"#;
    let so = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":["token"],"fault":4,"in":[8,8],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":8,"tier":"q"}"#;
    let build = |middle: &str| {
        object(&[
        ("sum2", si, "oracle @sum2 (x:wire[8] in, y:wire[8] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () ()\nregs { r:reg[8] }\n^entry():\nr = lift.add x y\nlift.retval r"),
        ("p", so, &format!("oracle @p (a:wire[8] in, b:wire[8] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () (tk:token)\nregs {{ x:reg[8], y:reg[8], out:reg[8], fr:reg[4] }}\n^entry():\nx = lift.mov a\ny = lift.mov b\nlift.oracle_call @sum2 tk (x, y) out fr () ()\n{middle}lift.oracle_uncall @sum2 tk (x, y) out fr () ()\nlift.retval out"))], "{}", "")
    };
    for middle in ["x = lift.add x y\n", "y = lift.const.i8 1\n"] {
        rejects(&build(middle), "§5.5");
    }
    // (1+2) XOR (1+2)=0; 2 moves + call + uncall + retval = 5.
    let o = rehash(&build(""));
    let mut input = OracleInput::bits(&[1, 2]);
    input.args.push(Argument::Token(Budget::steps(2)));
    assert_eq!(check(&o, "p", &input, Budget::steps(5)), (0, 0, 5));
}

#[test]
fn r2_qjumpr_can_enter_an_uncall_at_a_non_label_row() {
    let si =
        r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[8],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":8,"tier":"q"}"#;
    let so = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":["token"],"fault":4,"in":[],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":8,"tier":"q"}"#;
    let inner =
        "oracle @inner (x:wire[8] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () ()\n^entry():\nlift.retval x";
    let bad = "oracle @p () (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () (tk:token)\nregs { x:reg[8], dest:reg[32], off:reg[32], out:reg[8], fr:reg[4] }\n^entry():\nx = lift.const.i8 1\ndest = lift.label ^pair\noff = lift.const.i32 1\ndest = lift.add dest off\nqjumpr dest\n^pair():\nlift.oracle_call @inner tk (x) out fr () ()\nlift.oracle_uncall @inner tk (x) out fr () ()\nlift.retval out";
    rejects(
        &object(&[("inner", si, inner), ("p", so, bad)], "{}", ""),
        "§5.5",
    );
    // Call at entry dominates all targets of the computed jump. Every route
    // to the uncall has an outstanding call (even if the jump revisits entry).
    let good = "oracle @p () (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () (tk:token)\nregs { x:reg[8], dest:reg[32], out:reg[8], fr:reg[4] }\n^entry():\nlift.oracle_call @inner tk (x) out fr () ()\ndest = lift.label ^cleanup\nqjumpr dest\n^cleanup():\nlift.oracle_uncall @inner tk (x) out fr () ()\nlift.retval out";
    let o = rehash(&object(&[("inner", si, inner), ("p", so, good)], "{}", ""));
    let mut input = OracleInput::bits(&[]);
    input.args.push(Argument::Token(Budget::steps(1)));
    assert_eq!(check(&o, "p", &input, Budget::steps(5)), (0, 0, 5));
}

#[test]
fn r2_codex_changed_second_input_and_two_memory_regions() {
    let si = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[8,8],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":8,"tier":"q"}"#;
    let so = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":["token"],"fault":4,"in":[8],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":8,"tier":"q"}"#;
    let inner = "oracle @inner (x:wire[8] in, y:wire[8] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () ()\n^entry():\nlift.retval y";
    let outer = "oracle @outer (x:wire[8] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () (tk:token)\nregs { a:reg[8], b:reg[8], r:reg[8], fr:reg[4] }\n^entry():\na = lift.mov x\nlift.oracle_call @inner tk (a, b) r fr () ()\nb = lift.const.i8 1\nlift.oracle_uncall @inner tk (a, b) r fr () ()\nlift.retval r";
    rejects(
        &object(&[("inner", si, inner), ("outer", so, outer)], "{}", ""),
        "§5.5",
    );
    let good = outer.replace("b = lift.const.i8 1\n", "");
    let o = rehash(&object(
        &[("inner", si, inner), ("outer", so, &good)],
        "{}",
        "",
    ));
    for x in [0, 1, 255] {
        let mut input = OracleInput::bits(&[x]);
        input.args.push(Argument::Token(Budget::steps(1)));
        assert_eq!(check(&o, "outer", &input, Budget::steps(4)), (0, 0, 4));
    }
    let mem = r#"[{"A":1,"W":8,"role":"in"},{"A":1,"W":8,"role":"in"}]"#;
    let si = si.replace("\"mem\":[]", &format!("\"mem\":{mem}"));
    let so = so.replace("\"mem\":[]", &format!("\"mem\":{mem}"));
    let inner = inner.replace(
        "(f:wire[4]) () ()",
        "(f:wire[4]) (db:region[1,8] in, aux:region[1,8] in) ()",
    );
    let layout = "\nsection layout\n{\"A_tab\":2,\"H\":8,\"S_cells\":0,\"globals\":{},\"heap_base\":64,\"heap_limit_max\":0,\"interface_regions\":{\"inner\":{\"aux\":{\"base\":32},\"db\":{\"base\":16}},\"outer\":{\"aux\":{\"base\":32},\"db\":{\"base\":16}}},\"null_size\":16,\"ptr_width\":32}\n";
    let outer = good
        .replace(
            "(f:wire[4]) () (tk:token)",
            "(f:wire[4]) (db:region[1,8] in, aux:region[1,8] in) (tk:token)",
        )
        .replace("fr:reg[4]", "fr:reg[4], p:reg[32]")
        .replace("r fr () ()", "r fr (db, aux) ()");
    Object::parse(&object(
        &[("inner", &si, &inner), ("outer", &so, &outer)],
        "{}",
        layout,
    ))
    .unwrap();
    for region in ["db", "aux"] {
        let bad = outer.replace(
            "lift.oracle_uncall",
            &format!("p = lift.addr @{region}\nlift.store.i8 p a\nlift.oracle_uncall"),
        );
        rejects(
            &object(
                &[("inner", &si, &inner), ("outer", &so, &bad)],
                "{}",
                layout,
            ),
            "§5.5",
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn r3_nested_oracle_deliveries_invalidate_outstanding_inputs() {
    let si =
        r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[8],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":8,"tier":"q"}"#;
    let so = si
        .replace("\"args\":[]", "\"args\":[\"token\"]")
        .replace("[8],\"kind", "[8,8],\"kind");
    let inc = "oracle @inc8 (x:wire[8] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () ()\nregs { one:reg[8], r:reg[8] }\n^entry():\none = lift.const.i8 1\nr = lift.add x one\nlift.retval r";
    let build = |before: &str, middle: &str| {
        object(&[("inc8",si,inc),("p",&so,&format!("oracle @p (a:wire[8] in, b:wire[8] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () (tk:token)\nregs {{ x:reg[8], out:reg[8], fr:reg[4], fr2:reg[4] }}\n^entry():\nx = lift.mov a\n{before}lift.oracle_call @inc8 tk (x) out fr () ()\n{middle}lift.oracle_uncall @inc8 tk (x) out fr () ()\nlift.retval out"))],"{}", "")
    };
    support::reject_cli(
        &build("", "lift.oracle_call @inc8 tk (b) x fr2 () ()\n"),
        "§5.5",
        "nested-target",
    );
    // The other uncall has a matching earlier call; its delivery still writes x.
    support::reject_cli(
        &build(
            "lift.oracle_call @inc8 tk (b) x fr2 () ()\n",
            "lift.oracle_uncall @inc8 tk (b) x fr2 () ()\n",
        ),
        "§5.5",
        "nested-uncall",
    );
    // Fault delivery can clobber a four-bit input just as payload delivery can.
    let fault = build("", "lift.oracle_call @inc8 tk (b) out x () ()\n")
        .replace("x:reg[8]", "x:reg[4]")
        .replace("x = lift.mov a", "x = lift.trunc.i4 a")
        .replace(
            "lift.oracle_call @inc8 tk (x)",
            "lift.oracle_call @id4 tk (x)",
        )
        .replace(
            "lift.oracle_uncall @inc8 tk (x)",
            "lift.oracle_uncall @id4 tk (x)",
        );
    let id = "oracle @id4 (x:wire[4] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () ()\nregs { r:reg[8] }\n^entry():\nr = lift.zext.i8 x\nlift.retval r";
    let fault = fault.replace("section functions\n", &format!("section functions\n{id}\n"));
    // Add id4 through the object builder so the symbol table remains well-formed.
    let parsed_sig = si.replace("[8],\"kind", "[4],\"kind");
    let parent = fault.split("oracle @p").nth(1).unwrap();
    let fault = object(
        &[
            ("inc8", si, inc),
            ("id4", &parsed_sig, id),
            ("p", &so, &format!("oracle @p{parent}")),
        ],
        "{}",
        "",
    );
    support::reject_cli(&fault, "§5.5", "nested-fault");
    let o = rehash(&build("", ""));
    let mut input = OracleInput::bits(&[1, 0]);
    input.args.push(Argument::Token(Budget::steps(3)));
    // move + call + uncall + retval: (1+1) XOR (1+1) = 0.
    assert_eq!(check(&o, "p", &input, Budget::steps(4)), (0, 0, 4));
}

#[test]
fn codex_r3_b01_exact_implicit_delivery_witnesses() {
    let si =
        r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[8],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":8,"tier":"q"}"#;
    let so = si
        .replace("\"args\":[]", "\"args\":[\"token\"]")
        .replace("\"in\":[8]", "\"in\":[]");
    let inner = "oracle @i (x:wire[8] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () ()\n^entry():\nlift.retval x";
    let outer = "oracle @o () (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () (tk:token)\nregs { a:reg[8], b:reg[8], r:reg[8], fr:reg[4], fr2:reg[4] }\n^entry():\na = lift.const.i8 1\nb = lift.const.i8 2\nlift.oracle_call @i tk (a) r fr () ()\nlift.oracle_call @i tk (b) a fr2 () ()\nlift.oracle_uncall @i tk (a) r fr () ()\nlift.retval r";
    let build = |outer: &str| object(&[("i", si, inner), ("o", &so, outer)], "{}", "");
    // Hand trace of the invalid six-row body: r=1, a=1 XOR 2=3,
    // r=1 XOR 3=2. It must reject before hashing or execution (§5.5).
    support::reject_cli(&build(outer), "§5.5", "codex-implicit-target");
    // The same outstanding input can instead be overwritten by fault delivery.
    let s4 = si.replace("\"in\":[8]", "\"in\":[4]");
    let i4 = "oracle @i4 (x:wire[4] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () ()\nregs { r:reg[8] }\n^entry():\nr = lift.zext.i8 x\nlift.retval r";
    let fault = outer
        .replace("a:reg[8]", "a:reg[4]")
        .replace("a = lift.const.i8", "a = lift.const.i4")
        .replace("@i tk (a)", "@i4 tk (a)")
        .replace("(b) a fr2", "(b) r a");
    support::reject_cli(
        &object(
            &[("i", si, inner), ("i4", &s4, i4), ("o", &so, &fault)],
            "{}",
            "",
        ),
        "§5.5",
        "codex-implicit-fault",
    );
    let good = outer.replace("lift.oracle_call @i tk (b) a fr2 () ()\n", "");
    let o = rehash(&build(&good));
    let mut input = OracleInput::bits(&[]);
    input.args.push(Argument::Token(Budget::steps(1)));
    // Two constants, identical one-row calls, retval: 1 XOR 1 = 0.
    assert_eq!(check(&o, "o", &input, Budget::steps(5)), (0, 0, 5));
}
````

## `tests/r1_widths.rs` (470 lines)

````rust
//! Council round 1: fable R1-B1, codex B01, muse B1 (§3.3 bounds only iN).
//! Every expected value below is derived by hand from §3.3, §3.6, §4.2, §5.2.
mod support;
use bennett_isa_ref::{
    BitVector, Budget, Object, OracleInput, OracleVectorInput, OracleVectorMachine,
};

fn oracle(name: &str, header: &str, regs: &str, body: &str, inputs: &[u64], tgt: u64) -> Object {
    let ins = inputs
        .iter()
        .map(u64::to_string)
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join(",");
    let signature = format!(
        r#"{{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[{ins}],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":{tgt},"tier":"q"}}"#
    );
    let text = format!("{header}\n{regs}^entry():\n{body}");
    support::rehash(&support::object(&[(name, &signature, &text)], "{}", ""))
}
fn pow2(width: usize, k: usize) -> BitVector {
    let mut v = BitVector::zero(width).unwrap();
    v.set(k, true).unwrap();
    v
}
/// F_B and T2 for one input: the sequential engine, the literal machine with
/// its outcome, and the restoration of the complete tuple after B inverse steps.
fn both(o: &Object, name: &str, x: &[BitVector], steps: u64) -> (BitVector, BitVector, u64) {
    let input = OracleVectorInput {
        ins: x.to_vec(),
        ..Default::default()
    };
    let budget = Budget::steps(steps);
    let r = o.run_oracle_vectors(name, &input, budget).unwrap();
    let mut m = OracleVectorMachine::new(o, name, &input, budget).unwrap();
    let entry = m.snapshot();
    for _ in 0..steps {
        m.forward_step().unwrap();
    }
    assert_eq!(m.outcome().unwrap(), r, "machine agrees with §14.1");
    for _ in 0..steps {
        m.inverse_step().unwrap();
    }
    assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), entry, "prefix reversal restores the tuple");
    assert!(m.frames_clean());
    (r.payload, r.code, r.steps)
}

#[test]
fn codex_b01_wire129_identity_at_b0_and_b1() {
    let o = oracle(
        "id129",
        "oracle @id129 (x:wire[129] in) (t:wire[129]) (f:wire[4]) () ()",
        "",
        "lift.retval x",
        &[129],
        129,
    );
    for x in [BitVector::zero(129).unwrap(), pow2(129, 128)] {
        // B = 0 commits FAULT_BUDGET_STEPS on every input (§3.6).
        let (p, c, s) = both(&o, "id129", std::slice::from_ref(&x), 0);
        assert!(p.is_zero());
        assert_eq!((c.to_u128().unwrap(), s), (1, 0));
        // B = 1: lift.retval x halts with success after one row.
        let (p, c, s) = both(&o, "id129", std::slice::from_ref(&x), 1);
        assert_eq!(p, x);
        assert_eq!((c.to_u128().unwrap(), s), (0, 1));
    }
}

#[test]
fn codex_b01_reg129_move_with_bit_128_set_reverses() {
    let o = oracle(
        "mov129",
        "oracle @mov129 (x:wire[129] in) (t:wire[129]) (f:wire[4]) () ()",
        "regs { r:reg[129] }\n",
        "r = lift.mov x\nlift.retval r",
        &[129],
        129,
    );
    let mut x = pow2(129, 128);
    x.set(0, true).unwrap();
    let (p, c, s) = both(&o, "mov129", std::slice::from_ref(&x), 2);
    assert_eq!(p, x);
    assert_eq!((c.to_u128().unwrap(), s), (0, 2));
    let (p, c, _) = both(&o, "mov129", &[x], 1);
    assert!(p.is_zero());
    assert_eq!(c.to_u128().unwrap(), 1);
}

#[test]
fn fable_r1_b1_wide_add_is_2x_mod_2_256_in_both_engines() {
    let o = oracle(
        "wide",
        "oracle @wide (x:wire[256] in) (t:wire[256]) (f:wire[4]) () ()",
        "regs { r:reg[256] }\n",
        "r = lift.add x x\nlift.retval r",
        &[256],
        256,
    );
    let all_ones = BitVector::zero(256)
        .unwrap()
        .binary("sub", &pow2(256, 0))
        .unwrap();
    let cases = [
        (BitVector::zero(256).unwrap(), BitVector::zero(256).unwrap()),
        (pow2(256, 0), pow2(256, 1)),
        (pow2(256, 200), pow2(256, 201)),
        // 2(2^256 - 1) mod 2^256 = 2^256 - 2.
        (
            all_ones.clone(),
            all_ones.binary("sub", &pow2(256, 0)).unwrap(),
        ),
    ];
    for (x, twice) in cases {
        for b in 0..=3u64 {
            let (p, c, s) = both(&o, "wide", std::slice::from_ref(&x), b);
            if b >= 2 {
                assert_eq!((p, c.to_u128().unwrap(), s), (twice.clone(), 0, 2));
            } else {
                assert!(p.is_zero());
                assert_eq!((c.to_u128().unwrap(), s), (1, b));
            }
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn fable_r1_b1_unused_wide_input_through_the_small_integer_api() {
    // The witness that panicked with 1u128 << 256: a 256-bit input is legal.
    let o = oracle(
        "wide",
        "oracle @wide (x:wire[256] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () ()",
        "regs { one:reg[8] }\n",
        "one = lift.const.i8 1\nlift.retval one",
        &[256],
        8,
    );
    let r = o
        .run_oracle("wide", &OracleInput::bits(&[0]), Budget::steps(2))
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!((r.payload, r.code, r.steps), (1, 0, 2));
    let r = o
        .run_oracle("wide", &OracleInput::bits(&[7]), Budget::steps(1))
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!((r.payload, r.code, r.steps), (0, 1, 1));
}

#[test]
fn muse_b1_mov_of_2_255() {

#[test]
fn wide_lifted_suffixes_constants_and_casts() {
    // SPEC-QUESTIONS 15: lift.const.iN / lift.zext.iM name reg widths, not iN.
    let o = oracle(
        "k",
        "oracle @k (x:wire[8] in) (t:wire[300]) (f:wire[4]) () ()",
        "regs { c:reg[300], z:reg[300], r:reg[300] }\n",
        // 2^299 = 1018517988167243043134222844204689080525734196832968125318070224677190649881668353091698688
        "c = lift.const.i300 1018517988167243043134222844204689080525734196832968125318070224677190649881668353091698688\nz = lift.zext.i300 x\nr = lift.or c z\nlift.retval r",
        &[8],
        300,
    );
    let x = BitVector::from_u128(8, 0xa5).unwrap();
    let (p, c, s) = both(&o, "k", &[x], 4);
    let mut expected = pow2(300, 299);
    for bit in [0, 2, 5, 7] {
        expected.set(bit, true).unwrap();
    }
    assert_eq!((p, c.to_u128().unwrap(), s), (expected, 0, 4));
}

#[test]
fn bundle_widths_above_u16_and_large_region_dimensions_are_well_formed() {
    // §3.3 states no bound for wire[N], reg[N] or region[A,W].
    let o = oracle(
        "big",

    let (p, c, s) = both(&o, "big", std::slice::from_ref(&x), 1);

    );
}

#[test]
fn ashr_by_n_or_more_is_zero_in_every_engine() {
    // §4.1 "wrap; shift >= N -> 0": 0x80 ashr 8 = 0 (not 0xff), 0x80 ashr 7 = 0xff.
    let o = oracle(
        "sh",
        "oracle @sh (x:wire[8] in, y:wire[8] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () ()",
        "regs { r:reg[8] }\n",
        "r = lift.ashr x y\nlift.retval r",
        &[8, 8],
        8,
    );
    for (y, expected) in [(7u128, 0xffu128), (8, 0), (200, 0)] {
        let x = [
            BitVector::from_u128(8, 0x80).unwrap(),
            BitVector::from_u128(8, y).unwrap(),
        ];
        let (p, _, _) = both(&o, "sh", &x, 2);
        assert_eq!(p.to_u128().unwrap(), expected, "0x80 ashr {y}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn derived_counter_widths_follow_section_3_7() {
    // H = 127 with ptr_width = 128: Hc >= H + 2 = 129 (codex B01), Ac = A_tab + 1,
    // Sc = S_cells + 1, Dc = ceil(log2(depth_limit + 2)).
    let layout = r#"
section layout
{"A_tab":3,"H":127,"S_cells":5,"globals":{},"heap_base":16,"heap_limit_max":1024,"interface_regions":{},"null_size":16,"ptr_width":128}
"#;
    let signature =
        r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[8],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":8,"tier":"q"}"#;
    let text = support::object(
        &[(
            "h",
            signature,
            "oracle @h (x:wire[8] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () ()\n^entry():\nlift.retval x",
        )],
        "{}",
        layout,
    )
    .replace("ptr_width=32", "ptr_width=128");
    let o = support::rehash(&text);
    let budget = Budget {
        steps: 1,
        heap: 1024,
        stack: 32,
        depth: 6,
    };
    let w = bennett_isa_ref::DerivedWidths::derive(&o, "h", budget).unwrap();
    // depth_limit 6: ceil(log2 8) = 3. One row: 2^P > 1 needs P = 1.
    assert_eq!((w.hc, w.ac, w.sc, w.dc, w.p), (129, 4, 6, 3, 1));
    // H = 128 = ptr_width is legal (§7.2 H <= ptr_width): Hc = 130.
    let o = support::rehash(&text.replace("\"H\":127", "\"H\":128"));
    let w = bennett_isa_ref::DerivedWidths::derive(&o, "h", budget).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(w.hc, 130);
}

#[test]
fn r13_derived_counter_width_overflow_reports_host_limit() {
    for key in ["S_cells", "A_tab"] {
        let o = support::r13_check(key, "inc8");
        let input = OracleVectorInput {
            ins: vec![BitVector::from_u128(8, 8).unwrap()],
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let b = Budget::steps(0);
        let r = o.run_oracle_vectors("inc8", &input, b).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            (
                r.payload.to_u128().unwrap(),
                r.code.to_u128().unwrap(),
                r.steps
            ),
            (0, 1, 0)
        );
        let derived =
            std::panic::catch_unwind(|| bennett_isa_ref::DerivedWidths::derive(&o, "inc8", b));
        let e = derived
            .expect("width derivation must not panic")
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            e.to_string().contains("host limit") && e.to_string().contains("§3.7"),
            "{e}"
        );
        let machine = std::panic::catch_unwind(|| OracleVectorMachine::new(&o, "inc8", &input, b));
        let e = machine
            .expect("machine construction must not panic")
            .err()
            .expect("host limit");
        assert!(
            e.to_string().contains("host limit") && e.to_string().contains("§3.7"),
            "{e}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn r13_generated_derived_width_extremes_family() {
    let mut cases = 0;
    let mut admitted = 0;
    let mut rejected = 0;
    let mut host_limits = 0;
    let values = [
        0u128,
        1,
        63,
        64,
        127,
        128,
        u64::MAX as u128 - 64,
        u64::MAX as u128 - 63,
        u64::MAX as u128 - 2,
        u64::MAX as u128 - 1,
        u64::MAX as u128,
        1u128 << 64,
    ];
    for (text, root) in [
        (
            support::r13_text("S_cells")
                .replace(r#""S_cells":"18446744073709551615""#, r#""S_cells":0"#),
            "inc8",
        ),
        (
            support::r13_text("S_cells")
                .replace(r#""S_cells":"18446744073709551615""#, r#""S_cells":0"#)
                .replace("ptr_width=32", "ptr_width=128")
                .replace(r#""ptr_width":32"#, r#""ptr_width":128"#)
                .replace(r#""H":6"#, r#""H":128"#),
            "inc8",
        ),
        (include_str!("fixtures/heap.bisa").into(), "heap"),
        (include_str!("fixtures/sum_db.bisa").into(), "sum_db"),
        (
            include_str!("fixtures/tiny_memory.bisa").into(),
            "tiny_load",
        ),
    ] {
        let o = Object::parse(&text).unwrap();
        let root = if o.functions.contains_key(root) {
            root
        } else {
            o.function_order[0].as_str()
        };
        let layout = o.section("layout").unwrap();
        // All scalars, including nested global base/size and interface base.
        fn paths(
            v: &bennett_isa_ref::json::Json,
            path: &mut Vec<String>,
            out: &mut Vec<Vec<String>>,
        ) {
            if let bennett_isa_ref::json::Json::Object(m) = v {
                for (k, v) in m {
                    path.push(k.clone());
                    paths(v, path, out);
                    path.pop();
                }
            } else if matches!(v, bennett_isa_ref::json::Json::Number(_)) {
                out.push(path.clone());
            }
        }
        fn put(v: &mut bennett_isa_ref::json::Json, path: &[String], n: u128) {
            if path.is_empty() {
                *v = if n <= 9_007_199_254_740_991 {
                    bennett_isa_ref::json::Json::Number(n.to_string())
                } else {
                    bennett_isa_ref::json::Json::String(n.to_string())
                };
            } else if let bennett_isa_ref::json::Json::Object(m) = v {
                put(m.get_mut(&path[0]).unwrap(), &path[1..], n);
            }
        }
        let mut all = Vec::new();
        paths(layout, &mut Vec::new(), &mut all);
        for path in all {
            for n in values {
                cases += 1;
                let mut l = layout.clone();
                put(&mut l, &path, n);
                let mutated = text.replace(&layout.canonical(), &l.canonical());
                let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(|| -> bennett_isa_ref::Result<bool> {
                    let object = match Object::parse(&mutated) {
                        Ok(o) => o,
                        Err(e) => {
                            assert!(e.to_string().contains('§'), "{e}");
                            return Ok(false);
                        }
                    };
                    let f = &object.functions[root];
                    let mut input = OracleVectorInput::default();
                    for p in &f.params[0] {
                        input
                            .ins
                            .push(BitVector::zero(p.ty.bits(object.ptr_width)?)?);
                    }
                    for p in &f.params[3] {
                        if let bennett_isa_ref::Type::Region(a, w) = p.ty {
                            input.regions.insert(
                                p.name.clone(),
                                vec![0; (1usize << a) * (w as usize).div_ceil(8)],
                            );
                        }
                    }
                    let b = Budget::steps(0);
                    // A legal layout always preserves the sequential B=0 result.
                    let r = object.run_oracle_vectors(root, &input, b)?;
                    assert_eq!(
                        (r.payload.to_u128()?, r.code.to_u128()?, r.steps),
                        (0, 1, 0)
                    );
                    let d = bennett_isa_ref::DerivedWidths::derive(&object, root, b)?;
                    assert_eq!(d.hc as u128, l.get("H")?.uint()? + 2);
                    assert_eq!(d.ac as u128, l.get("A_tab")?.uint()? + 1);
                    assert_eq!(d.sc as u128, l.get("S_cells")?.uint()? + 1);
                    assert_eq!(d.w_cell, d.p.max(d.sc).max(d.did).max(d.w_max));
                    let m = OracleVectorMachine::new(&object, root, &input, b)?;
                    assert!(m.frames_clean());
                    Ok(true)
                });
                match result.unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!("panic for {root} {path:?}={n}")) {
                    Ok(true) => admitted += 1,
                    Ok(false) => rejected += 1,
                    Err(e) => {
                        assert!(e.to_string().contains('§'), "{root} {path:?}={n}: {e}");
                        host_limits += 1;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    // Dc's logarithm and d+2 boundary are independent of the layout exponents.
    let text = support::r13_text("S_cells")
        .replace(r#""S_cells":"18446744073709551615""#, r#""S_cells":128"#);
    let o = Object::parse(&text).unwrap();
    let input = OracleVectorInput {
        ins: vec![BitVector::from_u128(8, 8).unwrap()],
        ..Default::default()
    };
    for depth in values
        .into_iter()
        .chain([u128::MAX - 2, u128::MAX - 1, u128::MAX])
    {
        cases += 1;
        let b = Budget {
            depth,
            ..Budget::steps(0)
        };
        let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(|| -> bennett_isa_ref::Result<()> {
            let d = bennett_isa_ref::DerivedWidths::derive(&o, "inc8", b)?;
            let expected = (128 - (depth + 1).leading_zeros() as usize).max(1);
            assert_eq!(d.dc, expected);
            OracleVectorMachine::new(&o, "inc8", &input, b)?;
            Ok(())
        })
        .expect("depth arithmetic must not panic");
        match result {
            Ok(()) => admitted += 1,
            Err(e) => {
                assert!(e.to_string().contains('§'), "{e}");
                host_limits += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    eprintln!("R13 widths: {cases} cases; {admitted} constructed, {rejected} layout rejections, {host_limits} resource diagnostics");
    assert_eq!(cases, 507);
    assert_eq!(cases, admitted + rejected + host_limits);
}
````

## `tests/r2_validation.rs` (84 lines)

````rust
//! Round 2 load-time witnesses; expectations follow §§3.3, 3.5, 16.1.
mod support;
use bennett_isa_ref::Object;
use std::process::Command;
fn reject(text: &str, rule: &str, tag: &str) {
    let e = Object::parse(text).expect_err("malformed object accepted");
    assert!(e.to_string().contains(rule), "{e}");
    let path = format!("{}/.tmp/r2-{tag}.bisa", env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"));
    std::fs::write(&path, text).unwrap();
    for cmd in ["hash", "check"] {
        let out = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_bennett-isa-ref"))
            .args([cmd, &path])
            .output()
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out.status.code(), Some(1), "{:?}", out);
        assert!(out.stdout.is_empty());
        assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).contains(rule));
    }
}
#[test]
fn qif_arms_cannot_pop_or_leave_predicates() {
    for (n, arm) in ["qunpred p", "qpred t"].iter().enumerate() {
        let text = support::object(&[("a", support::ACTION_1_1, &format!("action @a (t:wire mut) (p:wire in) () () ()\n^entry():\nqif p {{\n{arm}\n}} {{\nx t\n}}"))], "{}", "");
        reject(&text, "§3.5", &format!("pred-{n}"));
    }
    Object::parse(&support::object(&[("a", support::ACTION_1_1, "action @a (t:wire mut) (p:wire in) () () ()\n^entry():\nqif p {\nqpred p\nx t\nqunpred p\n} {\nqif p {\nx t\n} {\nx t\n}\n}")], "{}", "")).unwrap();
}

fn icmp_requires_integer_or_pointer_operands() {
    for ty in ["token", "f64", "qreg[1]"] {
        let sig = format!(
            r#"{{"abi":"0.8","kind":"cc","params":["{ty}","{ty}"],"results":["i1"],"tier":"cc"}}"#
        );
        let text = support::object(&[("cmp", &sig, &format!("fn cc @cmp (a:{ty}, b:{ty}) (r:i1) () () ()\n^entry():\nr = icmp.eq a b\nret r"))], "{}", "");
        reject(&text, "§3.3", ty);
    }
}
#[test]
fn lifted_memory_widths_are_canonical_at_load() {
    for (fixture, op) in [("sum_db", "load"), ("heap", "store")] {
        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(format!(
            "{}/tests/fixtures/{fixture}.bisa",
            env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")
        ))
        .unwrap();
        let width = if fixture == "heap" { 16 } else { 8 };
        let old = format!("lift.{op}.i{width}");
        assert!(text.contains(&old));

#[test]
fn integer_and_pointer_comparisons_execute_and_reverse() {
    use bennett_isa_ref::{ClassicalMachine, ClassicalValue};
    for ty in ["i8", "ptr"] {
        let sig = format!(
            r#"{{"abi":"0.8","kind":"cc","params":["{ty}","{ty}"],"results":["i1"],"tier":"cc"}}"#
        );
        let text = support::object(&[("cmp", &sig, &format!("fn cc @cmp (a:{ty}, b:{ty}) (r:i1) () () ()\n^entry():\nr = icmp.eq a b\nret r"))], "{}", "");
        let o = Object::parse(&text).unwrap();
        for b in [3, 4] {
            let val = |v| {
                if ty == "ptr" {
                    ClassicalValue::Ptr(v)
                } else {
                    ClassicalValue::int(8, v).unwrap()
                }
            };
            let mut m = ClassicalMachine::new(&o, "cmp", &[val(3), val(b)], &[]).unwrap();
            let before = m.snapshot();
            assert_eq!(
                m.run(3).unwrap().values,
                [ClassicalValue::int(1, u128::from(b == 3)).unwrap()]
            );
            m.reverse().unwrap();
            assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), before);
        }
    }
}
````

````rust
mod support;
use bennett_isa_ref::{ClassicalMachine, ClassicalValue, Object, QuantumRegisters};
use support::{object, rehash};
fn program() -> Object {
    Object::parse(include_str!("fixtures/registers.bisa")).unwrap()

#[test]
fn register_handles_enforce_views_consumption_and_cleanliness() {
    let mut r = QuantumRegisters::new();
    let q = r.allocate(2).unwrap();
    let s = r.slice(q, 0, 1).unwrap();
    assert!(r.bundle(q).is_err());
    assert!(r.free(s).is_err());
    assert!(r.slice(s, 0, 1).is_err());
    r.complete_call(&[s]).unwrap();
    assert!(r.bundle(s).is_err());
    assert_eq!(r.bundle(q).unwrap().len(), 2);
    let b = r.allocate(1).unwrap();
    let joined = r.concat(q, b).unwrap();
    assert!(r.bundle(q).is_err());
    assert!(r.bundle(b).is_err());
    assert_eq!(r.bundle(joined).unwrap().len(), 3);
    r.free(joined).unwrap();
    assert!(r.bundle(joined).is_err());
}
#[test]
fn allocation_views_and_region_calls_reverse_with_their_frames() {
    let p = program();
    for name in ["allocation", "views"] {
        let mut m = ClassicalMachine::new(&p, name, &[], &[]).unwrap();
        let before = m.snapshot();
        assert_eq!(m.run(100).unwrap().fault, None);
        m.reverse().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), before, "{name}");
    }
    let mut m = ClassicalMachine::new(&p, "unclean", &[], &[]).unwrap();
    let before = m.snapshot();
    assert_eq!(m.run(100).unwrap().fault, Some(4));
    m.reverse().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), before);
}

        let r = m.run(100).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.values, vec![ClassicalValue::int(2, expected).unwrap()]);

    let mut m = ClassicalMachine::new(&p, "bad_uncall", &[], &[]).unwrap();
    m.push_measurement_draw(0.1).unwrap();

        regs.prepare(x, &[true, true, true, false, false, false, false, false])
            .unwrap();
        regs.prepare(t, &[true, true, true, true, true, false, false, false])
            .unwrap();
        regs.prepare(f, &[true, true, false, false]).unwrap();
        assert!(regs.prepare(x, &[false; 8]).is_err());
        let args = [
            ClassicalValue::Qreg(x),
            ClassicalValue::Qreg(t),
            ClassicalValue::Qreg(f),
            ClassicalValue::Token(Budget::steps(steps)),
        ];
        let mut m =
            ClassicalMachine::with_quantum_registers(&p, "invoke", &args, &[], regs).unwrap();
        let before = m.snapshot();
        m.run(100).unwrap();
        let r = m.quantum_registers();
        assert_eq!(
            r.quantum_state().read_basis(r.bundle(t).unwrap()).unwrap(),
            if steps == 3 { 31 ^ 8 } else { 31 }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            r.quantum_state().read_basis(r.bundle(f).unwrap()).unwrap(),
            if steps == 3 { 3 } else { 2 }
        );
        m.reverse().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), before);
    }
}

#[test]
fn r3_typed_cc_controlled_calls_execute_and_restore_history() {
    let ac = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}"#;
    let cc = r#"{"abi":"0.8","kind":"cc","params":["qreg[1]","qreg[1]"],"results":[],"tier":"cc"}"#;
    for forward_reference in [false, true] {
        let body = if forward_reference {
            "fn cc @p (input:qreg[1], q:qreg[1]) () () () ()\n^entry():\nbr ^def()\n^use():\nctl c action_call @a (q) () () ()\nret\n^def():\nyes = const.i1 1\nc = select yes input input\nbr ^use()"
        } else {
            "fn cc @p (c:qreg[1], q:qreg[1]) () () () ()\n^entry():\nctl c action_call @a (q) () () ()\nret"
        };
        let o = rehash(&object(
            &[
                (
                    "a",
                    ac,
                    "action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()\n^entry():\nx t",
                ),
                ("p", cc, body),
            ],
            "{}",
            "",
        ));
        for c in 0..2 {
            for t in 0..2 {
                let mut regs = QuantumRegisters::new();
                let control = regs.allocate(1).unwrap();
                let target = regs.allocate(1).unwrap();
                regs.prepare(control, &[c == 1]).unwrap();
                regs.prepare(target, &[t == 1]).unwrap();
                let mut m = ClassicalMachine::with_quantum_registers(
                    &o,
                    "p",
                    &[ClassicalValue::Qreg(control), ClassicalValue::Qreg(target)],
                    &[],
                    regs,
                )
                .unwrap();
                let entry = m.snapshot();
                let outcome = m.run(10).unwrap();
                assert_eq!(
                    (outcome.fault, outcome.steps),
                    (None, if forward_reference { 6 } else { 2 })
                );
                let regs = m.quantum_registers();
                assert_eq!(
                    regs.quantum_state()
                        .read_basis(regs.bundle(target).unwrap())
                        .unwrap(),
                    t ^ c
                );
                assert_eq!(
                    regs.quantum_state()
                        .read_basis(regs.bundle(control).unwrap())
                        .unwrap(),
                    c
                );
                m.reverse().unwrap();
                assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), entry);
            }
        }
    }
}

fn dynamic_region_alias_case(kind: &str) {
    use bennett_isa_ref::Budget;
    for tier in ["cc", "r"] {
        let o = support::dynamic_region_alias_object(kind, tier);
        for c in 0..2 {
            let mut regs = QuantumRegisters::new();
            let q = regs.allocate(1).unwrap();
            let r = regs.allocate(1).unwrap();
            regs.prepare(r, &[true]).unwrap();
            let mut args = vec![
                ClassicalValue::int(1, c).unwrap(),
                ClassicalValue::Qreg(q),
                ClassicalValue::Qreg(r),
            ];
            if kind == "oracle" {
                let f = regs.allocate(4).unwrap();
                args.extend([
                    ClassicalValue::Qreg(f),
                    ClassicalValue::Token(Budget::steps(1)),
                ]);
            }
            let before_regs = regs.clone();
            let mut m =
                ClassicalMachine::with_quantum_registers(&o, "p", &args, &[], regs).unwrap();
            let entry = m.snapshot();
            let result = m.run(10).unwrap();
            // select is row 1; the failed call is terminal row 2. The
            // disjoint branch executes CX/X/XOR(1) then ret: 3 rows, q=1.
            assert_eq!(
                (result.fault, result.steps),
                if c == 1 { (Some(4), 2) } else { (None, 3) },
                "{tier}/{kind}"
            );
            assert!(result.values.is_empty());
            let regs = m.quantum_registers();
            if c == 1 {
                assert_eq!(
                    regs, &before_regs,
                    "a failed call must not mutate state or handles"
                );
            } else {
                assert_eq!(
                    regs.quantum_state()
                        .read_basis(regs.bundle(q).unwrap())
                        .unwrap(),
                    1
                );
                assert_eq!(
                    regs.quantum_state()
                        .read_basis(regs.bundle(r).unwrap())
                        .unwrap(),
                    1
                );
            }
            m.reverse().unwrap();
            assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), entry, "{tier}/{kind}/{c}");
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn r4_dynamic_interface_alias_is_an_atomic_reversible_cc_and_r_fault() {
    dynamic_region_alias_case("interface");
}
#[test]
fn r4_dynamic_control_target_alias_is_an_atomic_reversible_cc_and_r_fault() {
    dynamic_region_alias_case("control");

#[test]
fn r4_dynamic_control_can_overlap_a_readonly_input() {
    dynamic_region_alias_case("readonly-control");
}
#[test]
fn r4_dynamic_oracle_input_output_alias_is_an_atomic_reversible_cc_and_r_fault() {
    dynamic_region_alias_case("oracle");
}

#[test]
fn r4_dynamic_alias_checks_cover_regions_block_parameters_and_child_targets() {
    // Mut bundle q[2] and region m[1,1] must be disjoint even if the child
    // is an identity. c=1 aliases both slots; c=0 binds two distinct handles.
    let ac = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[{"A":1,"W":1,"role":"mut"}],"mut":[2],"tier":"q"}"#;
    let ps =
        r#"{"abi":"0.8","kind":"cc","params":["i1","qreg[2]","qreg[2]"],"results":[],"tier":"cc"}"#;
    let o = rehash(&object(&[("a",ac,"action @a (t:wire[2] mut) () (m:region[1,1] mut) () ()\n^entry():\nx t[0]\nx t[0]"),("p",ps,"fn cc @p (c:i1, q:qreg[2], r:qreg[2]) () () () ()\n^entry():\ns = select c q r\naction_call @a (q) () (s) ()\nret")],"{}", "\nsection layout\n{\"A_tab\":0,\"H\":0,\"S_cells\":0,\"globals\":{},\"heap_base\":1,\"heap_limit_max\":0,\"interface_regions\":{},\"null_size\":1,\"ptr_width\":32}\n"));
    for c in 0..2 {
        let mut regs = QuantumRegisters::new();
        let q = regs.allocate(2).unwrap();
        let r = regs.allocate(2).unwrap();
        let before = regs.clone();
        let mut m = ClassicalMachine::with_quantum_registers(
            &o,
            "p",
            &[
                ClassicalValue::int(1, c).unwrap(),
                ClassicalValue::Qreg(q),
                ClassicalValue::Qreg(r),
            ],
            &[],
            regs,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let entry = m.snapshot();
        let outcome = m.run(10).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            (outcome.fault, outcome.steps),
            if c == 1 { (Some(4), 2) } else { (None, 3) }
        );
        assert_eq!(m.quantum_registers(), &before);
        m.reverse().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), entry);
    }
    // A block parameter is another dynamic alias, and inherited controls
    // must be checked against targets reached through the child action.
    let base = support::dynamic_region_alias_object("control", "r");
    let ac = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}"#;
    let ps =
        r#"{"abi":"0.8","kind":"r","params":["i1","qreg[1]","qreg[1]"],"results":[],"tier":"r"}"#;
    let o = rehash(&object(&[("leaf",ac,"action @leaf (t:wire mut) () () () ()\n^entry():\nx t"),("a",ac,"action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()\n^entry():\naction_call @leaf (t) () () ()"),("p",ps,"fn r @p (c:i1, q:qreg[1], r:qreg[1]) () () () ()\n^entry():\ns = select c q r\nbr ^invoke(s)\n^invoke(v:qreg[1]):\nctl v action_call @a (q) () () ()\nret")],"{}",""));
    // Also bind q and r directly to the SAME register at the R entry.
    for entry_alias in [false, true] {
        for o in [&base, &o] {
            let mut regs = QuantumRegisters::new();
            let q = regs.allocate(1).unwrap();
            let r = if entry_alias {
                q
            } else {
                regs.allocate(1).unwrap()
            };
            let before = regs.clone();
            let mut m = ClassicalMachine::with_quantum_registers(
                o,
                "p",
                &[
                    ClassicalValue::int(1, 1).unwrap(),
                    ClassicalValue::Qreg(q),
                    ClassicalValue::Qreg(r),
                ],
                &[],
                regs,
            )
            .unwrap();
            let entry = m.snapshot();
            let outcome = m.run(10).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(outcome.fault, Some(4));
            assert_eq!(
                outcome.steps,
                if o.functions.contains_key("leaf") {
                    3
                } else {
                    2
                }
            );
            assert_eq!(m.quantum_registers(), &before);
            m.reverse().unwrap();
            assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), entry);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn muse_r5_measurement_draws_order_bits_lexicographically() {
    // |++>: printed bits 00,01,10,11 have values 0,2,1,3 (little endian).
    let text = program().text.replace("cx t[0] t[1]", "h t[1]");
    let p = rehash(&text);
    for (draw, expected) in [(0.1, 0), (0.3, 2), (0.6, 1), (0.9, 3)] {
        let mut m = ClassicalMachine::new(&p, "measurement", &[], &[]).unwrap();
        m.push_measurement_draw(draw).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            m.run(100).unwrap().values,
            vec![ClassicalValue::int(2, expected).unwrap()]
        );
    }
}
````

````rust
use bennett_isa_ref::{Budget, Object, OracleInput, OracleMachine};

fn compare(o: &Object, name: &str, input: &OracleInput, budget: Budget) {
    let expected = o.run_oracle(name, input, budget).unwrap();
    let mut m = OracleMachine::new(o, name, input, budget).unwrap();
    let initial = m.snapshot();
    for _ in 0..budget.steps {
        m.forward_step().unwrap();
    }
    assert_eq!(m.outcome().unwrap(), expected, "{name}:B={}", budget.steps);
    for _ in 0..budget.steps {
        m.inverse_step().unwrap();
    }
    assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), initial, "{name}: prefix reversal");
    assert!(m.frames_clean());
}

fn recursive_call_and_ret_each_invert_the_complete_pre_step_tuple() {
    let o = Object::parse(include_str!("fixtures/sum_db.bisa")).unwrap();
    let mut input = OracleInput::bits(&[2]);
    input.regions.insert("db".into(), (1..=16).collect());

        stack: 512,
        depth: 64,
    };
    let mut m = OracleMachine::new(&o, "sum_db", &input, budget).unwrap();
    for _ in 0..budget.steps {
        let before = m.snapshot();

        let after = m.snapshot();

        assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), before);
        m.forward_step().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), after);
    }
    for stack in [0, 15, 16, 47, 48, 512] {
        for depth in [0, 1, 2, 3] {
            compare(
                &o,
                "sum_db",
                &input,
                Budget {
                    stack,
                    depth,
                    ..budget
                },
            );
        }
    }
}

#[ignore = "all prefixes of recursive sum for each 8-bit n"]
fn exhaustive_recursive_prefixes() {
    let o = Object::parse(include_str!("fixtures/sum_db.bisa")).unwrap();
    for n in 0..=255 {
        let mut input = OracleInput::bits(&[n]);
        input.regions.insert("db".into(), (1..=16).collect());
        let stop = if n <= 16 { 14 * n as u64 + 11 } else { 14 };
        for steps in 0..=stop {
            compare(
                &o,
                "sum_db",
                &input,
                Budget {
                    steps,
                    heap: 4080,
                    stack: 512,
                    depth: 64,
                },
            );
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn full_small_domain_includes_memory_and_nonzero_target_and_fault() {
    let o = Object::parse(include_str!("fixtures/tiny_memory.bisa")).unwrap();
    let mut covered = 0;
    for x in 0..=1 {
        for byte in 0..=255u128 {
            for steps in 0..=9 {
                let mut input = OracleInput::bits(&[x]);
                input.regions.insert("db".into(), vec![byte as u8]);
                let budget = Budget::steps(steps);
                let expected = if x == 0 && steps >= 4 {
                    (0, 5)
                } else if x == 1 && steps >= 8 {
                    (byte & 1, 0)
                } else {
                    (0, 1)
                };
                let result = o.run_oracle("tiny", &input, budget).unwrap();
                assert_eq!((result.payload, result.code), expected);
                let mut machine = OracleMachine::new(&o, "tiny", &input, budget).unwrap();
                let initial = machine.snapshot();
                for _ in 0..steps {
                    machine.forward_step().unwrap();
                }
                assert_eq!(machine.outcome().unwrap(), result);
                for target in 0..=1 {
                    for fault in 0..16 {
                        assert_eq!(
                            machine.commit(target, fault).unwrap(),
                            (target ^ expected.0, fault ^ expected.1)
                        );
                        covered += 1;
                    }
                }
                for _ in 0..steps {
                    machine.inverse_step().unwrap();
                }
                assert_eq!(machine.snapshot(), initial);
                assert!(machine.frames_clean());
            }
        }
    }
    assert_eq!(covered, 10 * (1 << 14));
}

        input.regions.insert("db".into(), (1..=16).collect());
        // 14*n+10 real rows, then one HALT idle row: cover every cutoff.

                &o,
                "sum_db",
                &input,
                Budget {
                    steps,
                    heap: 4080,
                    stack: 512,
                    depth: 64,
                },
            );
        }
    }
}
````

````rust
use bennett_isa_ref::Object;

fn action(kind: &str, body: &str, bounds: &str) -> String {
    let signature = format!(
        r#"{{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[{bounds}],"in":[1],"kind":"{kind}","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}}"#
    );
    let regs = if bounds.is_empty() {
        String::new()
    } else {
        format!("regs {{  }} bounds {{{bounds}}}\n")
    };
    format!("bennett-object isa=0.8 object=0.8 launch=0.8 sched=0.8 cert=0.8 coverage=0.8 target=0.8 ptr_width=32\n\nsection symbols\n{{\"0\":{{\"interface_hash\":\"{}\",\"kind\":\"{kind}\",\"name\":\"a\",\"signature\":{signature}}}}}\n\nsection functions\n{kind} @a (t:wire mut) (p:wire in) () () ()\n{regs}^entry():\n{body}\n","0".repeat(64))
}
fn bad(text: &str, rule: &str) {
    let e = Object::parse(text).expect_err("invalid action accepted");
    assert!(e.to_string().contains(rule), "{e} must cite {rule}");
}

    bad(&action("action", "qloop 3 {\nx t\n}", ""), "§5.3");
````

````rust
#![allow(dead_code)]
use bennett_isa_ref::{json::Json, Object};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

pub fn json(s: &str) -> Json {
    Json::parse(s).unwrap()
}
pub fn object(functions: &[(&str, &str, &str)], imports: &str, extra: &str) -> String {
    let symbols = functions
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(i, (name, signature, _))| {
            let sig = json(signature);
            let value = Json::Object(BTreeMap::from([
                ("name".into(), Json::String((*name).into())),
                ("kind".into(), sig.get("kind").unwrap().clone()),
                ("signature".into(), sig),
                ("interface_hash".into(), Json::String("0".repeat(64))),
            ]));
            (i.to_string(), value)
        })
        .collect();
    let mut text=format!("bennett-object isa=0.8 object=0.8 launch=0.8 sched=0.8 cert=0.8 coverage=0.8 target=0.8 ptr_width=32\n\nsection symbols\n{}\n",Json::Object(symbols).canonical());
    if imports != "{}" {
        text.push_str(&format!(
            "\nsection imports\n{}\n",
            json(imports).canonical()
        ));
    }
    text.push_str("\nsection functions\n");
    for (_, _, body) in functions {
        text.push_str(body.trim_end_matches('\n'));
        text.push('\n');
    }
    text.push_str(extra);
    text
}
pub fn rehash(text: &str) -> Object {
    let parsed = Object::parse(text).unwrap();
    let hashes = parsed.identity().unwrap().interface_hashes;
    let mut lines: Vec<_> = text.lines().map(str::to_string).collect();
    let i = lines.iter().position(|s| s == "section symbols").unwrap() + 1;
    let Json::Object(mut symbols) = json(&lines[i]) else {
        unreachable!()
    };
    for symbol in symbols.values_mut() {
        let name = symbol.get("name").unwrap().string().unwrap().to_string();
        let Json::Object(value) = symbol else {
            unreachable!()
        };
        value.insert("interface_hash".into(), Json::String(hashes[&name].clone()));
    }
    lines[i] = Json::Object(symbols).canonical();
    Object::parse(&(lines.join("\n") + "\n")).unwrap()
}
/// An object with functions, data symbols (name, hex) and trailing sections
/// (layout and later, each starting with "\nsection ..."). Hashes are zero;
/// pass the text through `rehash` to obtain canonical identities.
pub fn object_with_data(
    functions: &[(&str, &str, &str)],
    data: &[(&str, &str)],
    tail: &str,
) -> String {
    let mut symbols = BTreeMap::new();
    for (i, (name, signature, _)) in functions.iter().enumerate() {
        let sig = json(signature);
        symbols.insert(
            i.to_string(),
            Json::Object(BTreeMap::from([
                ("name".into(), Json::String((*name).into())),
                ("kind".into(), sig.get("kind").unwrap().clone()),
                ("signature".into(), sig),
                ("interface_hash".into(), Json::String("0".repeat(64))),
            ])),
        );
    }
    for (j, (name, hex)) in data.iter().enumerate() {
        let sig = json(&format!(
            r#"{{"abi":"0.8","kind":"data","size":{},"tier":"-"}}"#,
            hex.len() / 2
        ));
        symbols.insert(
            (functions.len() + j).to_string(),
            Json::Object(BTreeMap::from([
                ("name".into(), Json::String((*name).into())),
                ("kind".into(), Json::String("data".into())),
                ("signature".into(), sig),
                ("interface_hash".into(), Json::String("0".repeat(64))),
            ])),
        );
    }
    let mut text = format!(
        "bennett-object isa=0.8 object=0.8 launch=0.8 sched=0.8 cert=0.8 coverage=0.8 target=0.8 ptr_width=32\n\nsection symbols\n{}\n\nsection functions\n",
        Json::Object(symbols).canonical()
    );
    for (_, _, body) in functions {
        text.push_str(body.trim_end_matches('\n'));
        text.push('\n');
    }
    if !data.is_empty() {
        text.push_str("\nsection data\n");
        for (name, hex) in data {
            text.push_str(&format!("{name} {hex}\n"));
        }
    }
    text.push_str(tail);
    text
}
pub const ACTION_1_1: &str =
    r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[1],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}"#;

/// Invalid objects must fail before producing any CLI data.
pub fn reject_cli(text: &str, rule: &str, tag: &str) {
    let e = Object::parse(text).expect_err("malformed object accepted");
    assert!(e.to_string().contains(rule), "{e}");
    let dir = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join(".tmp");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
    let path = dir.join(format!("r3-{tag}.bisa"));
    std::fs::write(&path, text).unwrap();
    for cmd in ["hash", "check"] {
        let out = std::process::Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_bennett-isa-ref"))
            .arg(cmd)
            .arg(&path)
            .output()
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out.status.code(), Some(1), "{out:?}");
        assert!(out.stdout.is_empty());
        assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).contains(rule));
    }
}

/// Memoryless round-4 borrow fixtures, with exactly the advertised loop bounds.
pub fn borrow_lifetime_object(body: &str, bounds: &[u64]) -> String {
    let sig = format!(
        r#"{{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":{bounds:?},"in":[],"kind":"perm_action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}}"#
    );
    let regs = if bounds.is_empty() {
        String::new()
    } else {
        format!(
            "regs {{  }} bounds {{{}}}\n",
            bounds
                .iter()
                .map(u64::to_string)
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(", ")
        )
    };
    object(
        &[(
            "a",
            &sig,
            &format!("perm_action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()\n{regs}^entry():\n{body}"),
        )],
        "{}",
        "",
    )
}

/// Identity on all t,b basis entries, a superposition, and b entangled with an
/// untouched reference proves the controls do not merely hide a pool mutation.
pub fn borrow_identity(o: &Object) {
    use bennett_isa_ref::{QuantumBindings, QuantumState};
    for input in 0..6u32 {
        let mut q = QuantumState::new();
        let w = q.allocate(3).unwrap();
        if input == 5 {
            q.gate("h", &[w[1]], None, &[]).unwrap();
            q.gate("cx", &[w[1], w[2]], None, &[]).unwrap();
            q.gate("h", &[w[0]], None, &[]).unwrap();
        } else {
            for (bit, wire) in w[..2].iter().enumerate() {
                if input == 4 {
                    q.gate("h", &[*wire], None, &[]).unwrap();
                } else if input >> bit & 1 == 1 {
                    q.gate("x", &[*wire], None, &[]).unwrap();
                }
            }
        }
        let entry = q.clone();
        let mut b = QuantumBindings::default();
        b.bundles.insert("t".into(), vec![w[0]]);
        b.borrowed.push(vec![w[1]]);
        for adjoint in [false, true] {
            o.execute_action("a", &mut q, &b, adjoint, &[]).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(q, entry, "input={input}, adjoint={adjoint}");
        }
    }
}

/// R4-B02: select dynamically chooses q itself (c=1) or distinct r (c=0).
/// Both handles have the same static type; the precondition is physical.
pub fn dynamic_region_alias_object(kind: &str, tier: &str) -> Object {
    let ac = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[1],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}"#;
    let xc = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}"#;
    let os =
        r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[1],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":1,"tier":"q"}"#;
    let (sig, child, call, extra_types, extra_params) = match kind {
        "interface" => (
            ac,
            "action @a (t:wire mut) (s:wire in) () () ()\n^entry():\ncx s t",
            "action_call @a (q) (s) () ()",
            "",
            "",
        ),
        "control" => (
            xc,
            "action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()\n^entry():\nx t",
            "ctl s action_call @a (q) () () ()",
            "",
            "",
        ),
        "readonly-control" => (
            ac,
            "action @a (t:wire mut) (s:wire in) () () ()\n^entry():\ncx s t",
            "ctl s action_call @a (q) (s) () ()",
            "",
            "",
        ),
        "oracle" => (
            os,
            "oracle @a (s:wire in) (t:wire) (f:wire[4]) () ()\n^entry():\nlift.retval s",
            "oracle_call @a tk (s) q f () ()",
            ",\"qreg[4]\",\"token\"",
            ", f:qreg[4], tk:token",
        ),
        _ => panic!("unknown fixture family {kind}"),
    };
    let ps = format!(
        r#"{{"abi":"0.8","kind":"{tier}","params":["i1","qreg[1]","qreg[1]"{extra_types}],"results":[],"tier":"{tier}"}}"#
    );
    let parent = format!("fn {tier} @p (c:i1, q:qreg[1], r:qreg[1]{extra_params}) () () () ()\n^entry():\ns = select c q r\n{call}\nret");
    rehash(&object(&[("a", sig, child), ("p", &ps, &parent)], "{}", ""))
}

/// Independently hash a memoryless subject and attach its complete four-row
/// interface/pool identity claim. Never parse an uncertified subject here.
pub fn certified_borrow_identity(body: &str, bounds: &[u64]) -> String {
    certified_borrow_identity_kind(body, bounds, "perm_action")
}
pub fn certified_borrow_identity_kind(body: &str, bounds: &[u64], kind: &str) -> String {
    let sig = format!(
        r#"{{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":{bounds:?},"in":[],"kind":"perm_action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}}"#
    );
    let sig = json(&sig.replace("perm_action", kind)).canonical();
    let raw = borrow_lifetime_object(body, bounds).replace("perm_action", kind);
    let function = raw.split("section functions\n").nth(1).unwrap();
    let envelope = format!("isa=0.8\nptr_width=32\n{sig}\n{function}");
    let h = bennett_isa_ref::sha256_hex(envelope.as_bytes());
    let text = raw.replace(&"0".repeat(64), &h);
    let object_hash = bennett_isa_ref::sha256_hex(text.as_bytes());
    let cert = json(&format!(
        r#"{{"versions":{{"isa":"0.8","object":"0.8","launch":"0.8","sched":"0.8","cert":"0.8","coverage":"0.8","target":"0.8"}},"bindings":{{"object_hash":"{object_hash}","interface_hash":"{h}","closure_hash":"{h}","reference_program_hash":"{h}","dialect_mapping_version":"test.1","target_hash":"{}"}},"producer":{{"name":"tests","version":"1","materialisation":{{"llvm_version":"none","pipeline":"none","normaliser_version":"1"}}}},"regions":{{"{h}":{{"kind":"{kind}","signature":{sig},"bounds":{bounds:?},"frame":{{"interface":[{{"role":"mut","width":1,"class":"any"}}],"scratch":{{}},"retained_history":0,"borrow":{{"any":1}},"scheme_ancillae":{{}}}},"resources":{{}},"gates_used":{{}},"claims":[{{"kind":"exhaustive","label":"proof","domain":{{"bundles":[{{"name":"t","width":1,"lo":0,"hi":1}}],"borrowed":[{{"name":"b","width":1,"lo":0,"hi":1}}],"regions":[]}},"expected":{{"table":[[0,0],[0,1],[1,0],[1,1]]}}}}],"verification":{{"oracle":null,"borrow_frames":[0],"inverse_pairs":[],"unitary":[],"channel":[],"fault_rate":{{"domain":{{"bundles":[],"borrowed":[],"regions":[]}},"faults_by_code":{{}},"undefined_excluded":0,"layout_dependent_excluded":0}}}},"cleanup":{{}},"error":{{}},"definedness_assumptions":[]}}}},"composition":{{"multiplicities":{{}},"epsilon_total":{{"diamond":0}},"method":"sum_over_multiplicities"}}}}"#,
        "3".repeat(64)
    ));
    format!("{text}\nsection certificate\n{}\n", cert.canonical())
}

/// Full H_t tensor I_bR map, including basis, superposed and entangled inputs.
/// Each direction starts independently at entry; workspace cannot escape.
pub fn r6_map(o: &Object, hadamard: bool) {
    use bennett_isa_ref::{QuantumBindings, QuantumState};
    for input in 0..18 {
        let mut q = QuantumState::new();
        let w = q.allocate(5).unwrap();
        for (bit, wire) in w[..4].iter().enumerate() {
            if input >= 16 {
                q.gate("h", &[*wire], None, &[]).unwrap();
            } else if input >> bit & 1 == 1 {
                q.gate("x", &[*wire], None, &[]).unwrap();
            }
        }
        if input == 17 {
            q.gate("cx", &[w[1], w[4]], None, &[]).unwrap();
        }
        let entry = q.clone();
        let mut expected = q.clone();
        if hadamard {
            expected.gate("h", &[w[0]], None, &[]).unwrap();
        }
        let mut b = QuantumBindings::default();
        b.bundles.insert("t".into(), vec![w[0]]);
        b.borrowed.push(w[1..4].to_vec());
        for adjoint in [false, true] {
            let mut actual = entry.clone();
            o.execute_action("a", &mut actual, &b, adjoint, &[])
                .unwrap();
            assert_eq!(actual, expected, "input={input}, adjoint={adjoint}");
            o.execute_action("a", &mut actual, &b, !adjoint, &[])
                .unwrap();
            assert_eq!(actual, entry);
        }
    }
}

        "diagonal" => ("c = qalloc any 1\ns c\nb = qborrow any 1\ncx c b\nqreturn b\nsdg c\nqfree c", &[], "0d7a3eccbc3cdd7440ec3c1ad66a12e8650203486b2736f6fe5ea2ddb87a56f6", "5b407065c615539c15c7f9381b8fccfebc8e109cae3e8966c05fbd4acd687205"),

        "rotate-8" => ("c = qalloc any 4\nx c[0]\nqloop 8 {\nh t\nb = qborrow any 1\ncx c[3] b\nqreturn b\nh t\nswap c[3] c[2]\nswap c[2] c[1]\nswap c[1] c[0]\n}\nqloop 8 {\nh t\nswap c[1] c[0]\nswap c[2] c[1]\nswap c[3] c[2]\nh t\n}\nx c[0]\nqfree c", &[8, 8], "4036a594dfa32ab65353367719970549a2cbe1237e471ff6f43b169e09844112", "bc9ac8d642fe4c4569d81021da302108919d500fda82cde3577a2916b681068c"),
        _ => panic!("unknown round-7 witness"),
    };
    let text = borrow_lifetime_object(body, bounds)
        .replace("perm_action", "action")

/// Independent I_t tensor I_bR expectation; each direction starts at entry.
pub fn r9_identity(o: &Object, args: &[bennett_isa_ref::Argument]) {
    use bennett_isa_ref::{QuantumBindings, QuantumState};
    for input in 0..10 {
        let mut q = QuantumState::new();
        let w = q.allocate(3).unwrap();
        for (bit, wire) in w.iter().enumerate() {
            if input < 8 && input >> bit & 1 == 1 {
                q.gate("x", &[*wire], None, &[]).unwrap();
            }
        }
        if input >= 8 {
            q.gate("h", &[w[0]], None, &[]).unwrap();
            q.gate("h", &[w[1]], None, &[]).unwrap();
            if input == 9 {
                q.gate("cx", &[w[1], w[2]], None, &[]).unwrap();
            }
        }
        let entry = q;
        let mut bindings = QuantumBindings::default();
        bindings.bundles.insert("t".into(), vec![w[0]]);
        bindings.borrowed.push(vec![w[1]]);
        if let Some(arg) = args.first() {
            bindings.args.insert("tk".into(), arg.clone());
        }
        for adjoint in [false, true] {
            let mut actual = entry.clone();
            o.execute_action("a", &mut actual, &bindings, adjoint, &[])
                .unwrap();
            assert_eq!(actual, entry, "input={input} adjoint={adjoint}");
            o.execute_action("a", &mut actual, &bindings, !adjoint, &[])
                .unwrap();
            assert_eq!(actual, entry);
        }
    }
}

pub fn r9_opaque_object(body: &str, bounds: &[u64], child: Option<&str>) -> String {
    let os =
        r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[1],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":1,"tier":"q"}"#;
    let ac = format!(
        r#"{{"abi":"0.8","args":["token"],"bounds":{:?},"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}}"#,
        bounds
    );
    let bound_text = bounds
        .iter()
        .map(u64::to_string)
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join(", ");
    let regs = if bounds.is_empty() {
        String::new()
    } else {
        format!("regs {{  }} bounds {{{bound_text}}}\n")
    };
    let action = format!("action @a (t:wire mut) () () (tk:token) ()\n{regs}^entry():\n{body}");
    let mut functions = vec![(
        "o",
        os,
        "oracle @o (p:wire in) (v:wire) (fr:wire[4]) () ()\n^entry():\nlift.retval p",
    )];
    let child_sig = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":["token"],"bounds":[],"in":[1],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1,4],"tier":"q"}"#;
    if let Some(child) = child {
        functions.push(("child", child_sig, child));
    }
    functions.push(("a", &ac, &action));
    object(&functions, "{}", "")
}

pub fn r10_case(tag: &str) -> Json {
    json(include_str!("r10_cases.json"))
        .get(tag)
        .unwrap()
        .clone()
}
pub fn r10_text(tag: &str) -> String {
    r10_case(tag).get("text").unwrap().string().unwrap().into()
}
pub fn r10_pin(tag: &str) -> Object {
    let c = r10_case(tag);
    let text = c.get("text").unwrap().string().unwrap();
    let o = Object::parse(text).unwrap();
    o.check_hashes().unwrap();
    let id = o.identity().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        id.object_hash,
        c.get("object_hash").unwrap().string().unwrap()
    );
    for (name, h) in c.get("hashes").unwrap().object().unwrap() {
        assert_eq!(id.interface_hashes[name], h.string().unwrap());
        assert_eq!(
            id.closure_hashes[name].as_deref(),
            Some(h.string().unwrap())
        );
    }
    o
}
/// Every forbidden prefix at both definition positions, including aliases of
/// otherwise valid minimal function bodies. No hash normalization is involved.
pub fn r10_bad_headers() -> Vec<String> {
    let mut cases = vec![];
    let cc = r10_text("cc");
    for kind in ["cc", "r", "oracle", "action", "perm_action", "lproc"] {
        let (sig, body, bad) = match kind {
            "cc" | "r" => {
                let text = r10_text(if kind == "cc" { "cc" } else { "r" });
                let o = Object::parse(&text).unwrap();
                (o.functions["a"].signature().canonical(),
                 text.split("section functions\n").nth(1).unwrap().to_string(),
                 kind.to_string())
            }
            "oracle" => (r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[8],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":8,"tier":"q"}"#.into(),
                include_str!("../fixtures/inc8.bisa").split("section functions\n").nth(1).unwrap().replace("@inc8", "@a"),
                "fn oracle".into()),
            "lproc" => (r#"{"abi":"0.8","kind":"lproc","params":[8],"result":8,"tier":"q"}"#.into(),
                "lproc @a (x:reg[8]) (r:reg[8]) () () ()\n^entry():\nlift.ret x\n".into(), "fn lproc".into()),
            _ => (format!(r#"{{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"{kind}","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}}"#),
                format!("{kind} @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()\n^entry():\nx t\n"), format!("fn {kind}")),
        };
        let first_space = body.find(" @").unwrap();
        let mutated = format!("{bad}{}", &body[first_space..]);
        cases.push(object(&[("a", &sig, &mutated)], "{}", ""));
        let cc_o = Object::parse(&cc).unwrap();
        let cc_sig = cc_o.functions["a"].signature().canonical();
        let cc_body = cc
            .split("section functions\n")
            .nth(1)
            .unwrap()
            .replace("@a", "@first");
        cases.push(object(
            &[("first", &cc_sig, &cc_body), ("a", &sig, &mutated)],
            "{}",
            "",
        ));
    }
    cases
}

/// Independent identity on t,p,q and the arbitrary borrowed b/reference R.
/// Each direction starts from the original state; equality includes allocator.
pub fn r10_identity(o: &Object, steps: u64) {
    use bennett_isa_ref::{Argument, Budget, QuantumBindings, QuantumState};
    for input in 0..34 {
        let mut q = QuantumState::new();
        let w = q.allocate(5).unwrap();
        if input < 32 {
            for (bit, wire) in w.iter().enumerate() {
                if input >> bit & 1 == 1 {
                    q.gate("x", &[*wire], None, &[]).unwrap();
                }
            }
        } else {
            for wire in &w[..4] {
                q.gate("h", &[*wire], None, &[]).unwrap();
            }
            if input == 33 {
                q.gate("cx", &[w[3], w[4]], None, &[]).unwrap();
            }
        }
        let mut bindings = QuantumBindings::default();
        for (name, wire) in [("t", w[0]), ("p", w[1]), ("q", w[2])] {
            bindings.bundles.insert(name.into(), vec![wire]);
        }
        bindings.borrowed.push(vec![w[3]]);
        bindings
            .args
            .insert("tk".into(), Argument::Token(Budget::steps(steps)));
        for adjoint in [false, true] {
            let mut actual = q.clone();
            o.execute_action("a", &mut actual, &bindings, adjoint, &[])
                .unwrap();
            assert_eq!(actual, q, "input={input} adjoint={adjoint} B={steps}");
            o.execute_action("a", &mut actual, &bindings, !adjoint, &[])
                .unwrap();
            assert_eq!(actual, q);
        }
    }
}

pub fn r10_context(stack: &[&str], op: &str) -> String {
    let push: String = stack.iter().map(|p| format!("qpred {p}\n")).collect();
    let pop: String = stack
        .iter()
        .rev()
        .map(|p| format!("qunpred {p}\n"))
        .collect();
    format!("{push}{op}\n{pop}")
}
pub const R10_ORACLE: &str = "oracle_call @o tk (c) d f () ()";
pub fn r10_object(middle: &str, bounds: &[u64], child: bool, inverse: bool) -> String {
    let pinned = r10_text("controls");
    let sigs = json(pinned.lines().nth(3).unwrap());
    let os = sigs.get("0").unwrap().get("signature").unwrap().canonical();
    let mut sig = sigs.get("1").unwrap().get("signature").unwrap().clone();
    if let Json::Object(map) = &mut sig {
        map.insert("bounds".into(), json(&format!("{bounds:?}")));
    }
    let oracle = "oracle @o (x:wire in) (t:wire) (f:wire[4]) () ()\n^entry():\nlift.retval x";
    let bound_text = bounds
        .iter()
        .map(u64::to_string)
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join(", ");
    let regs = if bounds.is_empty() {
        String::new()
    } else {
        format!("regs {{  }} bounds {{{bound_text}}}\n")
    };
    let action = format!("action @a (t:wire mut) (p:wire in, q:wire in) () (tk:token) ()\n{regs}^entry():\nc = qalloc any 1\nd = qalloc any 1\nf = qalloc any 4\nh c\n{middle}h c\nb = qborrow any 1\ncx c b\nqreturn b\nqfree f\nqfree d\nqfree c");
    let child_sig = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":["token"],"bounds":[],"in":[1,1],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1,1,4],"tier":"q"}"#;
    let child_body = "action @child (c:wire mut, d:wire mut, f:wire[4] mut) (p:wire in, q:wire in) () (tk:token) ()\n^entry():\nqpred q\nqpred p\noracle_call @o tk (c) d f () ()\nqunpred p\nqunpred q";
    let oi = oracle.replace("@o ", "@oi ");
    let a_sig = sig.canonical();
    let mut funcs = vec![("o", os.as_str(), oracle)];
    if child {
        funcs.push(("child", child_sig, child_body));
    }
    if inverse {
        funcs.push(("oi", os.as_str(), oi.as_str()));
    }
    funcs.push(("a", a_sig.as_str(), action.as_str()));
    object(&funcs, "{}", "")
}

pub fn r11_case(tag: &str) -> Json {
    json(include_str!("r11_cases.json"))
        .get(tag)
        .unwrap()
        .clone()
}
pub fn r11_text(tag: &str) -> String {
    r11_case(tag).get("text").unwrap().string().unwrap().into()
}
pub fn r11_pin(tag: &str) -> Object {
    let c = r11_case(tag);
    let o = Object::parse(c.get("text").unwrap().string().unwrap()).unwrap();
    let id = o.identity().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        id.object_hash,
        c.get("object_hash").unwrap().string().unwrap()
    );
    for (name, hash) in c.get("hashes").unwrap().object().unwrap() {
        assert_eq!(id.interface_hashes[name], hash.string().unwrap());
        assert_eq!(
            id.closure_hashes[name].as_deref(),
            Some(hash.string().unwrap())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            id.envelopes[name],
            c.get("envelopes")
                .unwrap()
                .get(name)
                .unwrap()
                .string()
                .unwrap()
        );
    }
    o.check_hashes().unwrap();
    o
}

/// Literal R13 member witnesses and independently assembled §9.2 pins.
pub fn r13_case(name: &str) -> Json {
    json(include_str!("r13_cases.json"))
        .array()
        .unwrap()
        .iter()
        .find(|c| c.get("name").unwrap().string().unwrap() == name)
        .unwrap()
        .clone()
}
pub fn r13_text(name: &str) -> String {
    r13_case(name)
        .get("object")
        .unwrap()
        .string()
        .unwrap()
        .into()
}
pub fn r13_check(name: &str, root: &str) -> Object {
    let c = r13_case(name);
    let o = Object::parse(c.get("object").unwrap().string().unwrap()).unwrap();
    o.check_hashes().unwrap();
    let i = o.identity().unwrap();
    let pin = c.get("interface_hash").unwrap().string().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(i.interface_hashes[root], pin);
    assert_eq!(i.closure_hashes[root].as_deref(), Some(pin));
    assert_eq!(
        i.envelopes[root],
        c.get("envelope").unwrap().string().unwrap()
    );
    assert_eq!(
        i.object_hash,
        c.get("object_hash").unwrap().string().unwrap()
    );
    o
}
````

## `tests/support/r10_pins.py` (66 lines)

````python
"""Independent §9.2 literal envelopes, including rejected R10 grammar bytes.
Run this script to reproduce r10_cases.json; no interpreter calls.
"""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
def j(x):
    return json.dumps(x, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
def sha(s):
    return hashlib.sha256(s.encode()).hexdigest()
HEADER = "bennett-object isa=0.8 object=0.8 launch=0.8 sched=0.8 cert=0.8 coverage=0.8 target=0.8 ptr_width=32\n\nsection symbols\n"
cases = {}
def case(tag, funcs, expected=None):
    symbols, hashes = {}, {}
    for name, sig, body, refs in funcs:
        env = "isa=0.8\nptr_width=32\n" + j(sig) + "\n" + body
        for ref in refs:
            env = env.replace("@" + ref, "@" + hashes[ref])
        env += "".join(hashes[ref] + "\n" for ref in refs)
        h = sha(env)
        hashes[name] = h
        symbols[str(len(symbols))] = dict(name=name,kind=sig["kind"],signature=sig,interface_hash=h)
    text = HEADER + j(symbols) + "\n\nsection functions\n" + "".join(f[2] for f in funcs)
    result = dict(text=text, hashes=hashes, object_hash=sha(text))
    if expected:
        assert (hashes["a" if "a" in hashes else "inc8"], sha(text)) == expected, (tag, result)
    cases[tag] = result
    print(tag, hashes, sha(text))

cc = dict(abi="0.8",kind="cc",params=[],results=[],tier="cc")
def simple(tag, head, regs="", sig=cc, expected=None):
    body = head + " @a () () () () ()\n" + regs + "^entry():\nret\n"
    case(tag, [("a",sig,body,[])], expected)
simple("bare-cc","cc",expected=("2060222c2773451dd9a97e146d566bfca81c7a91c7fe04bd90d7e841163f531e","b6f4dc99c6f84d162c82c54ea4c41ceee3e9d4cc09a00c3ab8bd80d282faec3f"))
simple("cc","fn cc",expected=("218bf0ae43801ce9c291e2c3276d60df583a7a8b939b56312f88b1623c2e68cd","d2cb6bf361cd11bd9e68e31a0329b5b62bb9c2d23cf6cb7ca9d8ddf89bd208e5"))
simple("empty-bounds","fn cc","regs {  } bounds {}\n",expected=("cb5e25ba34a6c84c96766f19a4b30c0999b7f262c2df63ae436296ba4a2554c8","8f2d76a7e18603d59a53082cd0493913725397140a6cbd162b7150fdb5358f11"))
simple("omitted-bounds","fn cc","regs {  }\n",expected=("4b749e1b37d610bc72f3b4d5c63ea551364492a370bd2dc5054282c5b1b89e62","028699ab2f8bd8767b19d021e1153bac74c470d9a302636fe66928bcc0d74de5"))
simple("bare-r","r",sig=dict(cc,kind="r",tier="r"))
simple("r","fn r",sig=dict(cc,kind="r",tier="r"))
inc = (ROOT/"fixtures/inc8.bisa").read_text()
sig = json.loads(inc.splitlines()[3])["0"]["signature"]
body = inc.split("section functions\n")[1]
for tag, mutated, hp, op in [
    ("fn-oracle",body.replace("oracle @","fn oracle @"),"607bffa4376f76dc181141c19dc70dfbde0d8064e3d220187b13001e25cab0ca","3868eb11e0293db6f43d3a9c5589c36feab4d88916327a34241141c1949b2dd6"),
    ("inc-empty-bounds",body.replace("regs { one:reg[8], r:reg[8] }","regs { one:reg[8], r:reg[8] } bounds {}"),"31e7ad0837d13f0cd78e0fc2a155016c006ab18e3ecf6cc367308d58eb274437","6e0b6cfb1a74f8974706264ddc3b762bda7226e0abeb284f97978d5cb2f7d4f3"),
    ("empty-lhs",body.replace("lift.retval r","() = lift.retval r"),"a2f5278ca8db3abb0e407e475c1fba93c4307b97f0db8c1fe4a0bbe2b48da782","4ede077a7344efa101b22cd0f990feacde2c1a415dbec6667ee61290f9747480")]:
    case(tag,[("inc8",sig,mutated,[])],(hp,op))
case("tuple-lhs",[("inc8",sig,body.replace("r = lift.add","(r) = lift.add"),[])])
loop_sig=dict(abi="0.8",args=[],bounds=[1],**{"in":[]},kind="action",mem=[],mut=[1],tier="q")
case("one-trip",[("a",loop_sig,"action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()\nregs {  } bounds {1}\n^entry():\nqloop 1 {\nx t\n}\n",[])])
old=(ROOT/"fixtures/r9-codex-oracle.bisa").read_text()
os=json.loads(old.splitlines()[3])["0"]["signature"]
oracle=old.split("section functions\n")[1].split("action @a")[0]
a_sig=dict(abi="0.8",args=["token"],bounds=[],**{"in":[1,1]},kind="action",mem=[],mut=[1],tier="q")
prefix="action @a (t:wire mut) (p:wire in, q:wire in) () (tk:token) ()\n^entry():\nc = qalloc any 1\nd = qalloc any 1\nf = qalloc any 4\nh c\n"
call="oracle_call @o tk (c) d f () ()\n"
suffix="h c\nb = qborrow any 1\ncx c b\nqreturn b\nqfree f\nqfree d\nqfree c\n"
def ctx(stack):
    return "".join("qpred "+s+"\n" for s in stack)+call+"".join("qunpred "+s+"\n" for s in reversed(stack))
for tag,first,second,expected in [
    ("controls",["p","q"],["q","p"],("386dce74595f0e05ed2b7eb9218fc22fece3fafe7ad6fd206aed542ad8b7deef","7b1153bae80cc041447870eaa9623f73e6cb6df5085365a1efcbac99789076ad")),
    ("duplicate",["p"],["p","p"],None)]:
    case(tag,[("o",os,oracle,[]),("a",a_sig,prefix+ctx(first)+ctx(second)+suffix,["o"])],expected)
(ROOT/"support/r10_cases.json").write_text(j(cases)+"\n")
````
